spoiler_text.text:
The film starts after Spike (Alfie Williams) has been found by the Fingers gang, a Satanist cult led by Sir Lord Jimmy Crystal (Jack O’Connell). The gang wears unflattering blonde wigs fashioned after notorious predator Jimmy Saville. The rest of the gang includes Jimmy Ink (Erin Kellyman), Jimmima (Emma Laird), Jimmy Fox (Sam Locke), Jimmy Jimmy (Robert Rhodes), Jimmy Snake (Ghazi Al Rufai), Jimmy Jones (Maura Bird), and Jimmy Shite (Connor Newall). The Fingers force Spike to undergo an initiation ritual where he must fight and kill one of the Jimmys before becoming a Finger himself. He ends up having to fight Shite, who taunts him and knocks him around until Spike drops Shite’s pants and stabs him in the thigh. Shite pulls the knife out, causing blood to gush out since Spike hit an artery. Shite panics as he dies, and Sir Jimmy dubs Spike a new “Jimmy”.

On the outskirts, Samson (Chi Lewis-Parry) feasts upon another one of his kills. Meanwhile, Dr. Ian Kelson (Ralph Fiennes) picks up the corpse of the pregnant infected woman (the one who gave birth to Baby Isla) and adds her remains to his Bone Temple. Kelson continues to tranquilize Samson with morphine to keep him from getting violent. Eventually, it appears as though Samson is deliberately visiting Kelson to get drugged, putting him in a peaceful, almost lucid state. Kelson sits with Samson and gazes at the stars while listening to Duran Duran.

A trio of survivors – Tom (Louis Ashbourne Serkis), his pregnant partner Cathy (Mirren Mack), and their companion Jonno (Gordon Alexander) – are walking through the woods trying to avoid the infected. They get spotted, forcing them to run. Jonno gets cornered and slashes away at the infected, but their blood infects and turns him, so Tom and Cathy leave him behind and make their way back home.

When they arrive home, Tom and Cathy find the Fingers have taken over their farm home where they live with two other people, George (David Sterne), Matthew (Elliot Benn), and Jane (Lynne Anne Rodgers). Sir Jimmy makes Jimmima do a “Teletubbies” dance since they (or at least, Sir Jimmy is) are obsessed with the program, before he makes his intentions to kill them clear. Matthew throws boiling water on them, causing a commotion that allows Cathy to escape, but the Fingers capture the rest of the house.

Kelson has been enjoying his time getting high and dancing with Samson, but he knows that he only has a limited supply of morphine left, and he knows what will happen with Samson when he runs out. As night falls, Kelson prepares to euthanize Samson, until the Alpha looks up at the sky and utters the word “moon”. Kelson is overjoyed.

The Fingers tie up George, Jane, Tom, and Matthew in the barn and start to skin and disembowel them as sacrifices to Satan, whom Sir Jimmy constantly refers to as “Old Nick”. The imagery causes Spike to go outside the barn and vomit. Jimmy Ink, who is less enthused by Sir Jimmy’s methods, sympathizes with Spike and tries to comfort him. From a distance, Ink sees Kelson dancing by the fires with Samson.

Sir Jimmy gives Tom a chance to go free if he can fight and kill one of the Fingers. Tom picks Jimmima since he thinks she would be the easiest to fight. Jimmima cuts him pretty bad and prepares to execute him, but Cathy, who made her way back into the barn, throws a hook into Jimmima’s head, killing her. As Sir Jimmy orders the Fingers to go after her, Tom grabs a propane tank and lights one of the Jimmys on fire before taking an arrow to the chest. The barn goes up in flames, taking the rest of the survivors with it, while the Fingers get out. Sir Jimmy orders Spike to chase Cathy, but when he catches up to her, he begs her to take him with her. Cathy appears like she might comply, but she slugs Spike in the stomach and gets away, locking the gate behind her. Spike lies to Sir Jimmy and says that he killed Cathy, but he knows she got away and he’s pissed.

Ink tells Sir Jimmy about seeing “Old Nick”, so she leads the Fingers to the Bone Temple, which Spike recognizes. Sir Jimmy approaches Kelson, believing him to be an incarnation of Satan due to the red residue on his skin and being surrounded by thousands of skulls and bones. Sir Jimmy tells Kelson to play along with him and convince the other Fingers that he is indeeed Satan, threatening him if he does not comply.

Spike attempts to sneak away from the Fingers but is cornered by Jimmy Fox, who wants revenge against Spike for killing Shite. Fox gets killed by Ink, who then tells the other Fingers that Fox ran away out of fear of meeting Old Nick.

Kelson gives Samson a huge dose of drugs in anticipation of what is to come. Samson wanders off onto the nearby abandoned train, where he flashes back to when he was a child. It appears as though a train guard is asking him for his ticket, but Samson actually says “I don’t have a ticket”. This causes the infected to attack, snapping Samson back into his feral ways so he can rip them to pieces in self-defense.

The Fingers arrive at the Bone Temple. Kelson puts on an over-the-top show with flames and hallucinogenics, all set to Iron Maiden’s “The Number of the Beast”. The Fingers are all impressed, and Kelson gives the Fingers “orders” to obey Sir Jimmy and continue carrying out sacrifices in the name of Satan. Before letting them leave, Kelson sees Spike and recognizes him. Fearing for his safety, he also orders the Fingers to crucify Sir Jimmy. When Ink tries to act on it, Sir Jimmy stabs Kelson in the abdomen. The remaining Fingers try to get Ink to defend Sir Jimmy, but she kills them all before putting Sir Jimmy out of order. Spike stays with Kelson for a bit before Ink takes him away. She reveals to Spike her real name is Kelly before they walk away into the woods. Samson returns, and a drugged up Sir Jimmy, who is crucified upside down, envisions him as Satan as he carries Kelson’s body away. The nearby infected then proceed to finish Sir Jimmy off.

Somewhere nearby, it is shown that Jim (Cillian Murphy), one of the survivors of the London outbreak, is still living in his cottage with his teenage daughter Sam. They hear the commotion of the infected nearby, and from a distance, they see Spike and Kelly running from them. Jim and Sam arm themselves and head out to defend them.

wiki_plot.text:
After being rescued by the Fingers, a gang led by the psychopathic Satan worshipper, "Sir Lord" Jimmy Crystal, Spike is forced to kill Jimmy Shite in a death match, as an initiation. Sir Jimmy then renames the young boy "Jimmy" to match the other Fingers, who include the slightly empathetic Jimmy Ink, and the deranged, sadistic Jimmima.

Dr Ian Kelson, who covers his skin in iodine solution to protect himself from the virus, continues to build up the Bone Temple, an ossuary for those killed in the Rage Virus epidemic, while the Alpha Infected, Samson, repeatedly visits him. Kelson deduces that Samson is becoming addicted to the morphine from his blowgun, deliberately allowing himself to be drugged. Samson no longer attacks Kelson, and the two develop a human connection as his humanity begins to resurface.

The Fingers raid a farm inhabited by survivors, including Tom and his pregnant sister, Cathy. From a distance, Jimmy Ink catches sight of the Bone Temple, and Kelson dancing with Samson. In a barn, Cathy hides as Sir Jimmy orders the Fingers to skin the captured survivors alive as a sacrifice to Old Nick, claiming that Satan is his father.

Running low on morphine, Kelson prepares to euthanise Samson, but is overjoyed when Samson says his first word, "moon", suggesting that the Rage Virus may be treatable. Meanwhile, Jimmy Ink, who is growing disillusioned with Sir Jimmy, takes pity on Spike and protects him. Sir Jimmy offers Tom a place in the gang if he can win a death match against a Finger, but Tom is outmatched by his opponent, Jimmima. Cathy breaks her cover to kill Jimmima and Tom sets the barn on fire with a propane tank, killing one of the Fingers before being killed. Sir Jimmy sends Spike to capture Cathy; Spike, traumatised, begs her to take him with her, but Cathy does not trust him, and escapes.

With the gang's numbers and morale low, Sir Jimmy threatens to kill Spike for his failure to capture Cathy, but Ink suggests they visit Kelson — who she assumes is Old Nick, having mistaken the iodine for red skin, and Samson as a demon — and let him decide Spike's fate. At the Bone Temple, Sir Jimmy meets Kelson alone and threatens to kill him if Kelson does not pose as Satan and substantiate Sir Jimmy's leadership over the Fingers.

The next morning, Spike tries to leave Sir Jimmy's camp, but is confronted by Jimmy Fox, who attempts to kill him to avenge Jimmy Shite's death. Ink kills Fox and brings Spike back. Kelson fears that his research on Samson will be cut short and, in a premature attempt to grant him peace, administers him a cocktail of antipsychotics and other drugs, hypothesising that the Rage Virus causes aggression indirectly via psychotic hallucinations. Experiencing some clarity, Samson visits the abandoned train where he hallucinates a childhood memory. When he speaks normally again, a pack of infected attack him; now immune to reinfection, Samson overpowers and kills them all.

That night, Kelson complies with Sir Jimmy's demands, impersonating Satan in a pyrotechnic-filled performance of Iron Maiden's "The Number of the Beast" while exposing the gang to hallucinogens. Upon recognising Spike, Kelson betrays Sir Jimmy by ordering the Fingers to crucify him. Sir Jimmy fatally stabs Kelson, and Ink is forced to kill the other two Fingers in self-defence. Spike stabs Sir Jimmy, before comforting the dying Kelson. Ink crucifies Sir Jimmy on an inverted cross. Spike and Ink, whose real name is Kellie, leave the Bone Temple. Samson arrives and greets Kelson by name, thanking him as Kelson succumbs to his wounds. Samson carries his body away. After hallucinating Samson as the devil, Sir Jimmy is attacked by an infected.

Some time later, Spike and Kellie are attempting to escape a group of infected, unaware that they are being observed by Jim, a survivor of the initial outbreak of the Rage Virus, and his teenage daughter, Sam, who break off a history lesson about postwar Europe to go to their aid.

wiki_plot.text:
Marie-Lou Fontaine is the director of a for-profit nursing home for patients with dementia in the Parisian suburbs. Along with her administrative partner, Olivier, she attempts to train the staff in a humane caregiving technique named "Humanitude", which reminds patients of the presence of the caregiver and seeks to have them standing up and walking. She comes into frequent conflict with senior nurse Sophie, who worked at the home when it was formerly a mental hospital, who refuses to train herself in the technique due to the overworking of the nurses. When a nurse quits and Sophie threatens to quit over an altercation, Marie-Lou, unable to sleep and close to burnout, starts looking for answers.

One day, Marie-Lou leaves her workplace and comes across a developmentally disabled Japanese man running next to her tram. She follows him to a park, where she spends time with him and waits for his caregivers to come. The man is revealed to be Tomoki, the grandson of actor Gorō Kiyomiya, who comes to pick him up through GPS tracking along with the director of his play, Mari Morisaki. Mari hands Marie-Lou a pamphlet to her play.

Marie-Lou attends Mari and Gorō's play, where Gorō plays Italian psychiatrist Franco Basaglia, responsible for abolishing mental hospitals in Italy. Tomoki walks on stage and is incorporated into the performance. At the question and answer session after the play, Marie-Lou speaks in Japanese to Mari, to the chagrin of the French audience, about how the play resonated with her as a mental health professional. Mari reveals to her in her response that she is terminally ill and has been diagnosed with cancer. Mari and Marie-Lou meet after the session and walk to the banks of the Seine, chatting about their histories with Japan and France.

Marie-Lou invites Mari to stay with her at the nursing home, where she demonstrates Humanitude techniques to her. They discuss, from Mari's background as a philosopher, the way in which capitalism creates an "inside" and an "outside", where the "outside" is constantly expanding as its resources are consumed and the "inside" contracts.

Suddenly, Mari's health deteriorates, and she is forced to return to Kyoto, Japan. Marie-Lou follows with her, and they have heartfelt conversations at Mari's old house. At the doctor in Japan, it is revealed that Mari's cancer has returned and metastasized, and she has three months to live. Marie-Lou convinces Mari to return to Paris instead of entering hospice care in Japan.

Marie-Lou allows Mari to stay with her at the nursing home as an artist-in-residence as it is close to a large hospital. As Marie-Lou apologizes to Sophie and accepts staff requests to reduce Humanitude training sessions, Mari creates conceptual workshops for the patients using theatrical techniques. One day, shareholders arrive at the nursing home to see how the progress with Humanitude is going, seeing the patients walking and patients' families interacting with the nurses. 

During a production of Mari's play at the home, Tomoki accidentally knocks over the screens that are providing French-language subtitles to the Japanese-language play. While Gorō decides to switch to French, Tomoki's actions cause a ripple effect wherein multiple patients spontaneously begin engaging in activities from Mari's workshops. Mari is overcome with emotion, and Marie-Lou hugs her. Mari expresses for the first time that she wants to live.

Some time later, Gorō and Tomoki return to Japan. On a mountain overlooking Mari's house where Marie-Lou and Mari spoke, they spread Mari's ashes into the wind. At the nursing home, Mari's workshops continue under the guidance of Marie-Lou, who is finally able to rest.

wiki_plot.text:
The film follows three American physicians of different backgrounds. Dr. Mark Perlmutter is a Jewish American orthopedic surgeon from North Carolina; Dr. Thaer Ahmad is a Palestinian American emergency physician from Chicago; and Dr. Feroze Sidhwa is a trauma surgeon from California of Pakistani Parsi heritage. The three doctors operated primarily out of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis during two visits to Gaza, before and after the 2025 ceasefire.

In an opening scene, Perlmutter demands that Teng show an unblurred photograph of babies killed in a missile strike, arguing that blurring the images would obscure the reality of events. The film documents the doctors' work in operating rooms and hospital corridors, their media appearances upon returning to the United States, and the death threats some received as a result of their public advocacy. The film also documents the particular difficulty Ahmad faced gaining entry to Gaza due to his Palestinian heritage, despite holding the same American credentials as his colleagues.

spoiler_text.text:
The film starts with a video tape from the 90s. An unseen scientist named Naren Warne (Avan Jogia) is wandering through a mysterious location known as the Backrooms, recording whatever he sees. There is scattered furniture throughout the vast, empty halls and rooms. Naren finds a room full of video and camera equipment and tries to radio for help. A seagull then suddenly flies in out of nowhere. Naren continues wandering until he sees some type of large, growling creature stomping towards him. Naren tries to find a place to run or escape, but he fails and gets attacked by the entity. The video then cuts out, as it was being viewed by Naren’s fellow scientists.

A furniture store owner named Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor), of “Cap’n Clark’s Ottoman Empire”, is struggling to keep his business afloat since he is competing with a different store owner. He visits his therapist, Dr. Mary Kline (Renate Reinsve), who herself frequently thinks about the destruction of her childhood home and her mother being institutionalized. Mary has Clark role-play with her the issues that led to him divorcing his wife, such as his alcoholism, which causes Clark to grow genuinely irate and bitter as he vents about his frustrations.

Clark tries to film a promo with his assistant manager Kat Taylor (Lukita Maxwell) and her boyfriend Bobby Roberts (Finn Bennett), but it goes wrong when a chair that Clark sits on breaks. Later, he deals with the store’s electrical problem and meets with an electrician. They go into the basement of the store and find the electric panel, but they discover three switches set up diagonally that seemingly do not connect to the rest of the store.

At night, Clark is shown staying in the store. The show he’s watching is interrupted by a video from the Backrooms before the TV goes out. Clark goes back into the basement and sees a bit of light coming out from behind one of the walls. To his surprise, he is able to pass through it and finds himself in the Backrooms. He wanders in shock throughout the area, coming upon a room with a cardboard cutout of a man, plus multiple voices speaking in different languages. Clark also sees several artifacts fused into the floor, and even finds Naren’s badge (but not his body). He then sees the creature from earlier, causing him to run until he finally makes it back to the store’s basement.

At a corporation called Async Research Institute, a scientist named Phil (Mark Duplass) watches a recording of Clark walking through the Backrooms.

Clark returns to Mary to tell her about the Backrooms, but based on his description, she thinks he is suffering from alcohol withdrawals. Promising to return with proof, Clark goes to find Kat and Bobby to recruit them for gathering research.

Clark puts up tape around the space to enter the Backrooms and shows Kat and Bobby what he found. They react with stunned surprise at the entrance but they follow Clark anyway. Bobby is tied to a rope and is lowered down into a space filled with discarded clothing, including a t-shirt he was wearing earlier, and some of it is covered in blood. Bobby then hears the growling of the creature and he quickly gets pulled up. The creature yanks Bobby back down and drags his bloody body into a closed space. Kat goes after him and gets separated from Clark, who tries to hide. He enters a room with a lit Christmas tree and sees two humanoid figures (known as “Still Life”) moving towards him. Clark then makes it to a room where Kat sees him from the other side of a wall, but he cannot see her. The creature then grabs Clark’s camera and moves toward him.

Mary gets a message on her answering machine from Clark, who says he is “never coming back”, which raises her concerns. Meanwhile, Phil is at home with his family when he sees a commercial for Clark’s store, and he looks surprised when he recognizes Clark.

Mary goes to Clark’s store to try and find him. She goes to the basement and ends up in the Backrooms. Mary ends up in a room with creepy drawings before Clark emerges. He then puts Mary in a headlock and knocks her out.

Clark brings Mary into a room that is recreated to look like a regular dining room, with poorly-created copies of other humans (the Still Life) occupying the space. Clark explains to Mary that everything in the Backrooms is something or someone “remembered”. Clark opens the fridge door, revealing Kat’s severed head inside. He then cuts off the scalp of the female Still Life to make Mary continue re-enacting his marriage role play, but Mary refuses and tells him that his wife left him because he’s so whiny. She eventually manages to talk Clark into letting her go since he wants to remain in the Backrooms. This causes the other Still Life to scatter since the main Still Life, the tall monstrous being, is approaching. It takes the warped and deformed appearance of Clark as “Cap’n Clark”. Clark tries to speak to it like a friend, but the Still Life chomps into Clark’s neck, killing him.

Mary runs away and goes through several areas in the Backrooms that are recreated to look like her old neighborhood. After running through a tight space, she ends up in a copy of the store’s lobby. The Still Life chases her until Mary breaks its wooden leg and then starts hitting it with a rock that she always carries (actually a piece of the driveway of her childhood home where she imprinted her hands). Mary triggers an alarm that sets off gas. She runs from the Still Life and back into where she originally entered the Backrooms, where she is found by scientists.

Mary is brought to an interrogation room at Async, where she is greeted by Phil. He asks her to confirm the things she saw, but she cannot begin to explain. Phil tells Mary that their company used to make MRI machines, but they shifted their focus after discovering the Backrooms and have been trying to map out the place. As Phil continues talking, his words drown out and Mary just has a light smile on her face.

Inside the Backrooms, more spaces based off Mary’s memories have been recreated, including a Still Life of her sitting in the interrogation room.

wiki_plot.text:
On June 19, 1990, a researcher within the Async Research Institute, Naren Warne, is separated from his group and becomes lost in "the Backrooms", a labyrinthine extradimensional space containing a chaotic expanse of dull yellow rooms, fluorescent lights, long corridors, and malformed furniture. While attempting to call for rescue, Naren is chased and killed by a mysterious entity. Async scientists watch the recovered footage of the incident.

Clark, a failed architect who owns a struggling furniture store in San Jose, California, attempts to cope with his alcoholism and failing marriage. He sees therapist Mary Kline, who is working through her own trauma from the demolition of her childhood home and her agoraphobic mother's institutionalization. Clark recruits his assistant manager Kat and her boyfriend Bobby to film a television commercial featuring himself dressed as the store's pirate mascot. Having taken up residence in the store, he notices the lights flickering mysteriously at night and his television functioning erratically. While checking the breaker box, Clark notices a glowing slit in a wall. Approaching it, he falls through and enters the Backrooms. Clark finds Naren's belongings and narrowly escapes back to the store when an unseen figure chases him. An Async scientist, Phil, watches these events on a surveillance camera.

After days of exploring, Clark tells Mary about the Backrooms but is met with skepticism. In need of proof, Clark brings Kat and Bobby into the Backrooms to film their discoveries. While exploring a steeply sloped corridor, Bobby is ambushed and fatally dragged away by the mysterious entity; Clark and Kat frantically give chase through an unexplored area, where they are separated. Carrying the camera, Clark eventually encounters two other humanoid entities, one of which gives chase to him. He reaches a dead end, where Kat is apparently able to see him through a wall but not vice versa. Clark sets down the camera; an unseen entity picks it up as Kat screams for Clark to look behind him. 

Some time later, Mary receives a cryptic answering machine message from Clark, who tells her that he is staying in the Backrooms and will not return. Phil watches television with his family and recognizes Clark in a commercial for the furniture store. Concerned about Clark, Mary visits the store and enters the Backrooms herself, where she finds a crude and cryptic mural. An apparently psychotic Clark arrives; hearing an entity approaching, he tries to calm Mary before choking her unconscious. 

Mary awakens tied to a chair in a space resembling a dining room, occupied by Clark and three grotesque and largely static simulacra of humans. Clark demonstrates they are made of an edible white substance and reveals Kat's severed head in a refrigerator. Clark demands that Mary continue their therapy sessions, but she instead scolds Clark, telling him that his wife left him due to his inability to take responsibility for his failures. He begins to release Mary, but is interrupted by the arrival of a towering, distorted simulacrum of himself dressed as the pirate mascot. Clark tries to calm the pirate monster, which suddenly kills him and then chases Mary through various chaotic and surreal spaces until they reach a flawed replica of the furniture store. Cornered by the monster, she uses a large hat stand to destroy the monster's peg leg, then bashes it in the face using a chunk of concrete from her childhood home. Their struggle triggers an Async gas trap, alerting a group of researchers in hazmat suits. The monster is subdued, and Mary is taken to their research facility.

After recovering, Mary is taken to an interrogation room where she meets Phil. He explains that Async made magnetic resonance imaging machines until they discovered the Backrooms, which have since become their primary research focus. When asked how she came across the Backrooms and what she found there, she repeats Clark's description of it as a faulty, misremembered copy of reality. Mary asks if Async will let her go, but Phil states that the decision is not up to him. Inside the Backrooms, a series of spaces are distorted by Clark's and Mary's experiences and their consequences, ending in a loosely copied interrogation room in which her own deformed simulacrum sits still and silent.

wiki_plot.text:
During the start of Jimmy Carter's presidential term in 1977, Judith Heumann is a disability rights activist, wheelchair user, and polio survivor protesting against the delayed implementation of Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, legislation protecting access rights for disabled persons. The Rehabilitation Act was originally signed by Richard Nixon four years earlier, but concerns about costs had kept Section 504 in limbo, lacking the necessary implementation signature of the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare. Heumann's tactics include blocking traffic and lobbying the offices of Congressman George Miller and HEW Secretary Joseph A. Califano Jr. by phone. 

When these tactics fail, Heumann and other disabled protestors start a sit-in at the regional HEW offices in San Francisco, refusing to leave the building until Section 504 is signed by Califano. After a few days, the building's phone lines and food supply are cut off, so Heumann decides to go on a hunger strike inspired by Gandhi. The phone lines are eventually restored, and Heumann is notified of Califano's plans to meet the protesters in person, only to be met with his staff. During this meeting, Heumann and the protestors testify about the reasons for their protest. When the building is evacuated due to a bomb threat, Heumann still refuses to leave. As a result, Heumann gets into an argument with her co-organizer, Kitty Cone, over their handling of the situation. Eventually, Hale Zukas, another protester with cerebral palsy, convinces some of the protesters, including Heumann, to fly to Washington, D.C. and confront Califano directly. 

They attempt to wake Califano up by driving to his house in a Hertz rental truck, but Califano drives off, so the protesters resort to attempting to breach a press conference he is attending.
The police attempt to arrest them but cannot due to the lack of accessible jail cells. After nearly four weeks of protest in DC and San Francisco, Heumann sees a televised news report of Califano signing Section 504 into law. She calls Cone about the protestors' victory, and Cone leads the remaining sit-in protestors out of the HEW building in celebration. Later, Califano calls Heumann and admits that his reluctance to sign Section 504 came from fears for his job.

Thirteen years later, protestors in Washington, D.C. lobby for the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 to be signed, thus expanding Section 504's regulations into every public building in the United States.

wiki_plot.text:
A Hungarian immigrant family relocate to Vancouver Island in the late 1990s.  The family consists of the two parents, and four children. Jeremy is the couple's oldest son, but his father is from his mother's previous relationship. The remaining three children are a few years younger than Jeremy. Among them is Sasha, who is the youngest daughter. 

Jeremy engages in risky and disruptive behavior such as petty theft, climbing to dangerous heights, disappearing for long lengths of time, bullying the other children, exhibiting bursts of rage, and creating annoying noises. Jeremy is emotionally and verbally closed off, talking infrequently and never discussing his internal feelings.  At the same time Jeremy also demonstrates the capacity for occasional kindness towards his siblings and an exceptional talent in drawing maps of cities.  The family struggles to understand Jeremy.

The parents have tried a variety of therapeutic and parental strategies to improve Jeremy's behavior, but nothing produces long-lasting improvements.  After several more incidents, the parents consult with a social worker who recommends voluntary placement, where Jeremy would be sent to live with a different family.  The parents are aghast at the suggestion, but also feel that they have exhausted all other options.  They therefore proceed with the voluntary placement.

Years later in 2025, an adult Sasha attempts to process her memories of her late older brother with a video project. The project becomes a personal journey of understanding and reconciliation.  Sasha gathers several social workers and hopes that thirty years of advancement in social work will provide an answer to Jeremy's behavior, thereby giving some closure to the family.  Sasha is disappointed to hear that voluntary placement is once again the consensus strategy.  Sasha despairs in her perceived failure to find the solution that would have worked for Jeremy.  Sasha reaches out to everyone who knew Jeremy in the 1990s, including his high school friends and therapist.  The film closes with a response from one of Jeremy's friends, who acknowledges the trouble that they often sought out, but also offers a more optimistic account of Jeremy than previously known.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens with text stating that Mary Shelley (Jessie Buckley) wrote “Frankenstein” on a dare when she was 18 years old, on a dare. The spirit of Shelley appears from some state of limbo, where she expresses how her real vision of her famous book could not be completed before her death, and as such, she has found an opportunity to tell her real story.

Chicago, 1936 – Shelley possesses a woman named Ida (also Buckley), who is out at a restaurant in the presence of mob boss Vito Lupino (Zlatko Buric). She makes Ida start speaking in a Cockney accent and ranting about Lupino’s crimes. His two lackeys, Clyde and James (John Magaro and Matthew Maher), take Ida away to a private area, where she continues talking crazy. They move her near a stairway, where she takes a tumble and breaks her neck. Shelley declares that Ida is now “the motherfucking Bride”.

The monster created by Victor Frankenstein, who goes by “Frank” (Christian Bale) arrives in Chicago at the home of Dr. Cornelia Euphronius (Annette Bening), who lives with her assistant Greta (Jeannie Berlin). Euphronius is astonished by Frank’s existence, but he comes to her with the request that she create for him a companion, due to spending over a century alone and deprived of personal pleasures, and since he has read Euphronius’s work on reanimation. Despite her reluctance, Euphronius agrees to help Frank.

The two go to a grave and dig up Ida’s corpse. Euphronius performs a successful experiment, but Ida cannot remember her name or who she is, and her skin is stained black by a fluid used by Euphronius, but she continues to go between her normal voice and the voice used by Shelley (who also talks to Ida internally). Frank is quickly smitten with Ida but accidentally strikes her when she approaches him as he sleeps. After a meal with Euphronius, Frank takes Ida out and tells her that she was previously his bride before she died.

Frank brings Ida to the cinema to watch a film with his favorite actor, Ronnie Reed (Jake Gyllenhaal), before taking her to a nightclub. He finds himself falling for Ida, picturing himself dancing with her like a classic film. After Ida hangs out with some showgirls, she ends up harassed by some punks. Frank gets them away from her, but the two follow the couple down an alley. They physically harass the two until Frank smashes both of their heads open in front of the other patrons, forcing him and Ida to run. Frank feels he has to run off on his own, urging Ida to hide herself, but she chooses to go with him.

Frank and Ida board a train heading to New York City but are caught by a security guard. In his struggle to apprehend them, Ida pushes the man off the train, causing him to fatally smash his head on the tracks. The deaths of the two club guys attracts the attention of Detectives Jake Wiles (Peter Sarsgaard) and Myrna Malloy (Penelope Cruz). They are also alerted to the guard’s death and follow the duo to New York.

After arriving in New York, Frank changes his clothes. Ida says she cannot remember her name, so Frank starts calling her “Penny”. She tries to initiate sex with him when they are alone, but he cannot get into it. They later go to a screening of “Revolt of the Zombies”, where Ida hits a guy who is getting too handsy with his date. The guy recognizes Frank and Ida as “the killer monsters”, causing a panic in the theater.

The duo run through the streets and sneak into a fancy party, where Ronnie Reed is attending. Frank disguises himself and approaches Reed to express his admiration, but he acts like a jerk to Frank. He and Ida then begin dancing, which somehow causes the other guests to match their rhythm as if the two were possessing them. Wiles and Malloy show up, and Ida holds Reed at gunpoint. Wiles appears to recognize Ida. In the chaos, she accidentally shoots and kills a cop. Ida and Frank flee and hot-wire a car, allowing them to escape New York, but not before sharing a passionate kiss.

Frank and Ida, who now calls herself “The Bride”, fall in love and drive toward Niagara Falls. The Bride inspires other women in the area, especially victims of violence, to dress up like her and spread chaos and anarchy. Lupino catches wind of The Bride’s survival, prompting him to execute James for failing to kill her and for him to send Clyde to get the job done.

On the road, Frank and The Bride are pulled over by a cop (Louis Cancelmi), who attempts to rape The Bride but gets shot by Frank. She then proceeds to bite his tongue out.

Wiles and Malloy continue their pursuit of the duo. They catch up to Frank and The Bride in Niagara Falls, where Wiles tries to warn The Bride and stop her from continuing her crimes with Frank. Wiles admits to Malloy that he was working with Ida when she was alive, as they were going to take Lupino down together. He feels guilty over the belief that he led her to her death. He retires and allows Malloy to take the lead on the case.

Frank and The Bride end up at a drive-in theater, where he proposes to her. He admits that he was not honest earlier about who she was before she died, and says that he didn’t even know who she was. Frank gets shot by Clyde, who has tracked the duo there, as well as Malloy. The Bride takes Frank’s body away.

The Bride brings Frank back to Euphronius. She is reluctant to bring Frank back to life since there’s a chance he will not remember The Bride, as the same thing happened to Euphronius when she tried to revive her own husband. Clyde shows up and shoots The Bride, followed by the cops who come in and see her holding a gun. Malloy orders the officers to go after Clyde, while Euphronius is left with the bodies of Frank and The Bride. Shelley appears one last time, seemingly moving from The Bride’s body to Euphronius.

Outside, Clyde is arrested. Malloy looks up and sees lights coming from Euphronius’s lab. The last thing we see are the hands of The Bride and Frank coming together.

During the credits, Lupino is arrested, and the female rioters inspired by The Bride celebrate.

wiki_plot.text:
Speaking from the afterlife, Mary Shelley says she has a story she wanted to tell after Frankenstein, but could not because of her death. To tell it, she possesses Ida, a woman living in 1936 Chicago, who in her trance publicly discusses the criminal activities of the crime boss Vito Lupino. Lupino's henchmen Clyde and James discreetly take her aside, pushing her down a flight of stairs to her death.

Elsewhere in Chicago, Frankenstein's monster, AKA "Frank", arrives at the house of scientist Dr. Cornelia Euphronius. Having read about Euphronius' work on reanimation, he enlists her to create a companion for him after a century of loneliness. Euphronius and Frank choose Ida's corpse and successfully revive her, but she loses her memory in the process. Frank takes advantage of this and states that she is his bride and lost her memory in an accident.

Frank and Ida see a movie featuring Frank's favorite actor Ronnie Reed and then go dancing at a club. As they leave, two men attempt to assault her, and Frank kills them. Frank tells her to leave him, but she decides to run away with him. They stow away in a train to New York City, killing a police officer who discovers them after Shelley causes her to have an outburst. Meanwhile, Detective Jake Wiles and his assistant, Myrna Malloy, investigate the murders and eventually follow them to New York.

While the pair are in hiding, Frank tells her that her name is Penelope Rogers. Penelope causes chaos in a screening of Revolt of the Zombies and they seek refuge from the police and an angry mob at a high-class party. Frank runs into Ronnie Reed and expresses his adoration, but is dismissed. Frank begins to dance like Reed does in his films, Penelope joining him, as do party-goers possessed by Mary Shelley. Detective Wiles and the police arrive at the party, but they fall back when Penelope holds Reed at gunpoint and calls out men in attendance for abusing women. Wiles recognizes her real identity as Ida. Penelope kills a police officer, and she and Frank escape the city in a stolen car.

Penelope and Frank's crime spree becomes well publicized, and Lupino recognizes her in a newspaper. He executes James for failing to silence her and dispatches Clyde to kill her again, ordering Clyde to bring him her tongue as proof of death, to add his collection of victims' tongues that he keeps in jars. Meanwhile, Malloy makes a connection between reports of murders and sightings of the pair in cities where Reed's films were set. This prompts Malloy and Wiles to travel to Niagara Falls, where they find the couple. Wiles confronts them and informs Penelope of her previous identity as Ida before she shoots him in the foot. Fleeing, an angered Penelope takes the injured Frank to a drive-in, where he tells her the truth of her origins.

Wiles explains to Malloy that he and Ida were planning to take down Lupino and expresses guilt that his inaction led to her death. He decides to retire and promotes Malloy as his replacement. Malloy tracks the couple to the drive-in. Frank apologizes for his actions and affirms his love for Penelope/Ida, who decides to call herself the Bride. As he proposes, Clyde fatally shoots him, but the Bride escapes with Frank's body, returning to Euphronius' laboratory, followed by Malloy.

Euphronius refuses to reanimate Frank, saying that her attempts to reanimate her husband went wrong, leading her to have to kill him. Clyde breaks into the laboratory and fatally shoots the Bride before fleeing. The police arrive and Malloy orders them to search for Clyde, leaving Euphronius with the Bride's and Frank's corpses. Encouraged by Malloy and Shelley, Euphronius decides to revive the couple. Outside, the police arrest Clyde. Malloy sees bright lights shine from the laboratory. Inside, the revived corpses hold hands.

During the credits, Lupino and those involved are apprehended by Wiles and Bride-inspired female rioters with his tongue jars smashed.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1964, three Mississippi civil rights activists disappear without a trace during the summer. Federal bureau supervisor Roy K. Moore demands swift answers from regional agents. Moore sends ruthless Brooklyn mob enforcer Greg Scarpa south to assist. Scarpa uses physical coercion upon a local Ku Klux Klansman inside a warehouse. The mobster strikes the suspect repeatedly until he talks openly, giving coordinates where victims lie buried under thick red soil.

In Hattiesburg in 1966, civil activist Vernon Dahmer helps local Black citizens register to vote safely. Klansmen ride past his home at midnight and throw burning gasoline cans while opening fire. Dahmer helps his family escape safely through a rear window, but he dies from burns and smoke inhalation the next morning. As his grieving wife Hattie mourns beside neighbor Rebecca Brewer outdoors, a young Black FBI agent, Wayne Strider, arrives to investigate. 

Strider moves south with his supportive wife Allison. Moore and Agent Everett Rhodes assign Strider to direct efforts. The local residents refuse federal interviews due to fear of local deputies. Moore assigns Scarpa to partner with Strider.

Strider believes strict legal bounds bring true justice through proper courtrooms, while Scarpa mocks rules and uses coercion to obtain total compliance. Scarpa recites quotes from Malcolm X to justify ruthless choices. Together, they traverse small rural towns searching for active Klan operatives. Scarpa grabs suspects off streets and drags them into blinding spots, where he threatens them at gunpoint to extract names.

Strider watches in dismay as Scarpa breaks federal laws without hesitation, but terrified witnesses begin leaking critical names about the night bombing. The evidence points directly toward Sam Bowers and his local gang. Scarpa corners Bowers alone and forces a confession using physical force. The federal agents raid hidden hideouts across county lines near midnight, while the sheriff deputies facing evidence can no longer protect the Klan killers.

Bowers and multiple Klan members are arrested for Dahmer's death. Strider achieves justice but feels greatly unsettled by federal hypocrisy, pondering his future career path. He realizes systemic prejudice runs through federal law enforcement agencies. Scarpa collects his cash payout from federal agents before leaving town and returning to New York. The Mississippi community honors Vernon Dahmer, with Hattie vowing to continue registration efforts for local voters daily. Strider accepts that law enforcement demands tough compromises every day, and justice arrives only when people push beyond ordinary legal bounds.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in Gotham City, where actor Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries) is heading to set for a new project. He and his agent Hildie (Nancy Carroll), business manager Frank Fitzpatrick (Eddie Marsan), and best friend/fellow actor Corey Bowery (Joshua James) watch as Matt is nominated for an Oscar for one of his recent movie roles. Everyone celebrates.

Matt is hailed as a hot young up-and-comer that moved from Coast City with Corey from humble beginnings. The guys go out at night to a club, Vesuvius. Matt is spotted by an actress, Mia Torrez (Joana Ribeiro). Corey warns Matt that she’s dating notorious mobster Markos Szabo (David Dencik), but he disregards this and hooks up with Mia.

Matt wakes up to find Szabo and his goons in the apartment. As payback for sleeping with his girlfriend, Szabo takes a switchblade and gruesomely carves up Matt’s face. At the hospital, he is told by Frank and Corey that it would not be a good idea for Matt to pursue legal action against Szabo since he has a ton of control over people in Gotham. Matt gives Frank power of attorney and has him use money to pay for Matt’s facial reconstructive surgery, but they bleed him dry and make his face look worse.

Mia goes on the news and makes it sound like Matt drugged and assaulted her, while other people from his old neighborhood start to spread rumors that he had a bad reputation in high school. Making things worse, the jury at the trial decides not to charge Szabo with anything. Hildie also drops Matt as a client. With his life in ruins, he is forced to move to a crappy apartment in the Burrows, the poor part of Gotham, and everyone now sees him as a freak.

Matt later finds an ad for Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), a scientist whose research specializes in using nanites to repair nerve and tissue damage, though her benefactors ripped her off and took credit for her work. Matt tracks Caitlyn down and talks to her about his situation. Since her work is untested on humans, she initially declines to help treat Matt. However, Caitlyn later changes her mind after talking to her fiance, Detective John Borelli (Max Minghella), and contacts Matt.

Matt starts trials by taking small doses of Caitlyn’s serum, which helps repair his face until he looks handsome again. Matt decides to make his public comeback at the premiere of a movie he was originally set to star in. He shocks everyone with his reappearance, and Hildie even tries to get him back onboard. When Matt starts responding angrily, the side of his face starts drooping like it’s melting. He runs and hides before running back to Caitlyn.

Although Caitlyn tries a small dose to help Matt, he becomes desperate and injects himself with nearly her entire stash of nanites. Matt’s skin bubbles and morphs oddly until he goes back to normal. At his apartment, Matt discovers that the cuts on his body heal quickly, and even deep cuts that draw a lot of blood eventually seal back up, and the blood returns to his body.

Matt takes a trip to Coast City to visit Corey. On his flight back, he sees a news report of Szabo getting a license for a casino, and he discovers Frank is now working with Szabo. Matt gets angry again, and his eyelids start to seal together without him being able to fix it. He grabs small scissors and goes into the bathroom to cut his eyelids open. They don’t heal and he has to go back to Caitlyn, who helps calm him down until his eyes look normal again.

Caitlyn runs tests on Matt’s body and observes his behavior. After seeing that his body responds to his emotions, she has him bring up his feelings of repressed anger towards everybody that ruined his life, and his face briefly morphs into Szabo. While Matt sleeps, Caitlyn observes him, and he turns into her, feeling himself in his sleep. When she brushes his back, Matt morphs into Frank, which freaks her out.

Matt later goes to find Frank in his office to confront him about working with Szabo. Although Frank tries to weasel his way out, he becomes intimidated by Matt and lets it slip that Corey was involved in getting witnesses for the trial to work in favor of Szabo. When Frank’s secretary returns, Matt tries to shut Frank up, but his hand expands in Frank’s mouth, and he pulls Frank’s tongue and throat out, killing him. Matt hides the body and morphs into Frank so that he can slip out of the building. Frank’s body is later discovered, and John begins an investigation.

Matt goes onto the set of a show that Corey is working on. He gets into his trailer and gets him to admit that he got paid off to rig the jury. Corey weeps and apologizes, and Matt appears to hug him in forgiveness…but then he turns out to be smothering him with his own stomach. Matt assumes Corey’s identity to act out a scene with none other than Mia. After aggressively kissing her during the scene, one of the crew members follows Matt-as-Corey back to the trailer, where he finds the real Corey dead. John starts to suspect Szabo having something to do with it, and the mobster threatens John and Caitlyn.

Caitlyn goes to Matt’s apartment to express her concerns over how the nanites are affecting his body. Matt admits that he is falling for Caitlyn and even kisses her, but she is adamant about being with John. As she leaves, Matt sees one of Szabo’s goons, Sal, following Caitlyn. Matt morphs into her to trick Sal, and then mutates his arm into a giant club to smash Sal’s head in. Matt then assumes Sal’s identity.

Matt goes to Vesuvius to face off with Szabo. He kills one guy in the bathroom as Sal before going to the dance floor. Mia sees him and he starts to freak her out by shapeshifting into Szabo’s other goons. They go out onto the dance floor to try and take care of Matt, but he keeps tricking them. He uses parts of his body to create spikes that slice and stab his enemies before eventually causing a panic. Mia makes it to Szabo’s office, but Matt infiltrates it by posing as one of the other goons, Patches. Szabo shoots both Patches and Matt. Mia tends to who she thinks is Patches but is really Matt. She bites off a chunk of his flesh but it expands in her throat and suffocates her. Matt takes Szabo down by carving into his own face the same way Szabo did to him and letting his blood spill onto Szabo’s face, knowing the nanites would find their way back to Matt’s body and essentially melt Szabo’s face off.

John later goes to Matt’s apartment in the aftermath of the Vesuvius murders. Caitlyn later returns to her apartment and is seemingly greeted by John, but it’s really Matt posing as him, as he has murdered John to be with Caitlyn. Seeing that he’s too far off the deep end, Caitlyn decides to terminate the nanites, even if it kills Matt. She tases him, which causes the nanites to react in a volatile way, causing Matt’s body to expand and mutate unnaturally. He basically begs Caitlyn to go through with the execution, and she terminates the nanites. Matt’s body melts and sinks into the sewers.

Caitlyn’s research and materials are seized by the police, and Matt is presumed dead. She goes out on the streets and looks around at everyone, thinking any one of them could be Matt. She gives money to a homeless man, who is really Matt and he returns to the sewers. It appears as though Caitlyn followed him and wants to be with him now, but this is just Matt having grown strong enough to project her body. He returns to his new form, a disgusting and grotesque blob of flesh with his face barely hanging on. Matt can only scream in rage as he has now become…CLAYFACE!

wiki_plot.text:
After being nominated for an Academy Award, actor Matt Hagen attends a party with his childhood friend and fellow actor Corey Bowery. There, he meets actress Mia Torrez and spends the night with her despite Corey's warning that she is the girlfriend of crime lord Markos Szabo. The next morning, Szabo and his men ambush Matt and disfigure his face with a knife. Although Matt reports the attack to the police, Szabo avoids prosecution due to a lack of evidence and control over the corrupt Gotham police. Mia later falsely claims in a television interview that Matt had drugged her. Unable to find work due to his appearance and Mia's allegations, Matt runs out of money and returns to his childhood home in the Gotham City slums.

After multiple botched surgeries, Matt learns of Caitlyn Corr, a doctor who is developing a nanite treatment capable of rapidly healing damaged tissue and skin. Caitlyn initially hesitates to use Matt as a test subject, but her fiancé, detective John Borrelli, who is investigating Szabo, encourages her to help him. The treatment initially succeeds, allowing Matt to return to public life with his face apparently restored. When his face begins melting during a red carpet event, however, Matt panics and returns to Caitlyn. Against her wishes, he injects himself with a larger dose of nanites, seemingly curing the problem.

Matt subsequently discovers that he can instantly recover from any injury. Although thrilled by his abilities, Caitlyn grows concerned. While flying home after visiting Corey, Matt learns from a news broadcast that his former manager, Frank Fitzpatrick, now works for Mia and Szabo. Matt briefly loses control of his powers but, with Caitlyn's guidance, discovers that he can alter his facial features and voice to impersonate anyone. He confronts Frank, who admits to betraying him to conceal his embezzlement of Matt's earnings, and reveals that Corey helped him ruin Matt's reputation. Unable to fully control his powers, Matt accidentally kills Frank and assumes his appearance to escape, then tracks down and willingly murders a remorseful Corey by suffocating him inside his body.

John begins to suspect Szabo of the killings, prompting Szabo to threaten both John and Caitlyn. When Caitlyn visits Matt, he confesses he loves her, but she hesitates to reciprocate due to her relationship with John. After one of Szabo's men follows Caitlyn, Matt kills him and infiltrates Szabo's club, massacring the gang before confronting Szabo and Mia. Matt forces part of his body into Mia's throat, suffocating her. He then cuts his own face in a manner identical to how Szabo's men had disfigured it and lets his blood drip onto Szabo's face. As Matt's wounds regenerate, the nanites in his blood crush and dissolve Szabo's face, killing him.

With Szabo's criminal empire destroyed, John visits Matt to verify his whereabouts. Caitlyn realizes that Matt is responsible for the murders and returns home to tell John everything. After the conversation, she discovers the real John's corpse and realizes that she has been speaking to Matt in disguise. Convinced that their romantic feelings are mutual, Matt declares that they can finally be together and attempts to kiss her. Horrified, Caitlyn attacks him with a taser and activates the nanites' "kill switch", causing his body to melt away into the sewers, while Caitlyn informs the police. Unable to find any trace of him, the authorities dismiss her account. Matt is declared missing, and Caitlyn abandons her research.

Later, Caitlyn gives a dollar to a homeless man, unaware that he is Matt, who survived and is living in Gotham's sewers. Using his clay-like flesh, Matt creates a replica of Caitlyn and acts out a scenario in which they reconcile and kiss. As he transforms into a hulking form, Matt roars in rage.

After his teenage son, Krzysztof Dymiński, goes missing in May 2023, Daniel searches Poland's Vistula River, torn between fear that his son is dead and hope that he may still be alive. CCTV footage taken on the morning of his disappearance shows Krzysztof standing on a bridge, but not whether he jumped or walked away, and Daniel continues to investigate long after the police and local media have stopped searching.

Except for a final shot, the film uses no images of Krzysztof. The film's soundtrack includes a snippet of William Basinski's "The Disintegration Loops," which plays over the final scenes.

spoiler_text.text:
Brooklyn, 2016 – Party promoter Peter Green (Jordan Firstman) goes out with a group of his friends, which includes Sophie (Cara Delevingne), Devon (Nigel Whyte), and Percy (Sam Wilkes). They hit a nightclub, where the friends all get high. Peter meets two British women, Leonora (Paris Petitjean) and Edison (Kirby Howell-Baptiste), who are both flirty with him even though he tells them he is gay. Peter goes to hook up with a guy named Dan (Jack Cameron Kay), and Leonora goes to join them. Dan convinces Peter to engage in a threesome. Peter later ends up dancing in the club even after most people have left.

Ten years later, Peter is still partying and doing drugs. He lives with a Russian roommate, Nicky (Eldar Isgandarov), and works with Sophie in the party-promoting business. Peter tries to get Sophie to stand in for him at a party, but she is too busy and he ends up going and does drugs, while also selling them. The next day, Sophie waits for Peter to arrive for a meeting with two potential partners, but Peter is still too high from the night before and is unable to sit straight or keep his eyes open. Sophie later meets with Peter to cut him out of the business, even though he calls her out for also being an addict and that people can’t stand her.

Peter returns to his apartment to find Edison is there with a young boy named Arlo (Reggie Absalom). Edison explains that he is Peter’s son that he fathered with Leonora, whom Peter doesn’t remember until he recalls that he and his friends made her an inside joke because she kept saying “innit babes”. Edison continues that Leonora told her boyfriend Felix that Arlo was his, until he found out the truth and brutally beat her up. Leonora was in and out of institutions until she recently committed suicide, leaving Edison with no other option but to bring Arlo to Peter, or let him be abused by Felix. Edison leaves Arlo with Peter for what is meant to be a few hours.

Peter takes Arlo out to get pizza, but the boy didn’t tell him that he was lactose intolerant, so he starts to throw up. Even though he gets Arlo into the bathroom, it makes Peter accidentally throw up on Arlo’s head. Peter tries to form some kind of connection with Arlo, learning about his interest in music such as house.

Peter then brings Arlo to an apartment party that Edison said she was going to be at. There, the two meet a music artist that Leonora met and whom Arlo remembers. Ultimately, Peter is told that Edison has left. The next morning, Peter gets in touch with Edison to learn that she has already gone back to London, arguing that she had no choice but to leave Arlo there since Leonora made her promise that he would go back to Peter.

Peter starts to take parenting duties seriously and takes Arlo out to buy clothes (most of the shirts Peter owns are too vulgar) and bonds with him over club music, even buying him an expensive Elliot Smith record. He even makes Nicky move downstairs with their neighbor Evelyn (Colleen Camp). Peter’s friend group, which includes Devon, Saffron (Saturn Risin9), Almi (Miss Benny), and Hana (Alaska Riley), arrives at the apartment and meets Arlo. They are charmed by him since he is already familiar with trans women/”dolls” because a lot of Leonora’s friends also were. They also take time to “cancel” Sophie for being a bitch on social media.

Pushed by Saffron’s encouragement, Peter gets Arlo to play as a DJ at one of his parties, under the moniker “Night Shift”. He does a good job but Peter gets him out early to avoid Arlo getting in trouble. He also sells drugs to people on the side.

Peter takes steps to enroll Arlo in school, needing paperwork from the UK to move forward. He also brings Arlo to see a social worker, Oscar (Diego Calva). Peter starts a romantic relationship with Oscar, despite his initial reservation about dating the parent of one of his cases. While at the park, Arlo gets into a fight with another boy, but Peter gets him off the other kid before things get worse.

Arlo is later brought to perform at another party, but Saffron and the others have taken too long to get done, so he is going on with a crowd that is more fucked up, which Peter was worried about. Arlo briefly plays, but Peter gets him out. Arlo gets separated from him briefly, but Peter gets him out safely. They are spotted by Sophie on their way out.

The next day, Sophie arrives at Peter’s apartment on a bender. She apologetically admits that she impulsively called child services on Peter as a result of her stress and how he and the others have cut her out. A CS agent named Vanessa (Angela Fornero) arrives at the apartment to tell Peter that as a result of the allegations of negligence, Arlo must be sent back to the UK, pending an investigation. Peter has to break the news to Arlo, who is angry but ultimately goes with Vanessa.

Peter travels to the UK and meets a lawyer, Lydia (Vicki Pepperdine), who was recommended by Vanessa. She is sympathetic to Peter’s story, but acknowledges that his history of drug use and selling is going to build a strong case against him. She does also inform him that Felix has been nailed by authorities and is under investigation for stealing child support benefits and child abuse.

Peter and Lydia go before a judge, where he denies having sold drugs. He gives a moving testimony about how becoming a father to Arlo has changed his life, and how much he loves the boy. Lydia tells him that it seems good so far, and she offers Peter a place to stay for a while.

The two return before the judge, who brings up Peter’s recent drug transaction through Venmo (captioned “let’s research mama” after an infamous tweet) and because Saffron’s Instagram handle is “KundleJenner69” (“kundle” being gay slang for ketamine). It is decided that Arlo will be placed in foster care with a close friend of Leonora’s who cares for him and already has kids his age. Peter is also forced to accept that he must remain without contact from Arlo and does not even get to say goodbye to him.

One year later, Peter has given up partying and is still in a relationship with Oscar. Saffron visits him at the bar where he now works, where Peter says he is clean and that he and Sophie (who is also sober) have patched things up and still occasionally talk.

Peter is woken up to a phone call from Sharon, Arlo’s guardian. Since it is his birthday, she allows Peter to talk to him on the phone. Sharon has also agreed to arrange for Peter to visit in the future. Peter talks to Arlo for a few minutes before hanging up. Peter cries in Oscar’s arm as he comforts him.

The last scene is Peter leaving a bodega and walking home, where he hears music from a nearby house party, and he smiles fondly before continuing his walk.

wiki_plot.text:
Gay party promoter Peter Green lives a hedonistic, drug-fueled lifestyle at various clubs around New York City. At one party, he meets British tourists Leonora and Edison. While Peter is having sex with a man, Leonora joins them, leading to a threesome. 

Ten years later, Peter, now in his thirties, is still partying, to the chagrin of his business partner Sophie. When Peter arrives to a business meeting high, Sophie fires him and takes control of his promoting. Edison unexpectedly arrives at Peter's apartment with ten-year-old Arlo, whom she reveals is Peter's son, resulting from his tryst with Leonora. She further explains that Leonora was married to a man named Felix at the time of Arlo's conception, and initially led Felix to believe Arlo was his, though Felix became physically abusive toward both of them when DNA testing revealed this to be false. Leonora has recently committed suicide, and Peter is Arlo's only living relative. Edison leaves Arlo in Peter's care while she ostensibly runs errands, promising to retrieve Arlo in no more than two hours. Peter reluctantly spends the day with Arlo and allows him to sleep in his apartment overnight; the following morning, Peter discovers that Edison has returned to London.

Peter and Arlo bond over their love of club music, and Peter soon begins to adapt to parenthood. He introduces Arlo to his friends, whom Arlo quickly wins over. Peter takes steps to enroll Arlo in school, meets social worker Oscar to help Arlo adjust to his circumstances, and attempts to reconcile with Sophie, whose business is struggling without his help. Encouraged by Peter's friend Saffron, Arlo proves to be a talented DJ and convinces Peter to let him perform at one of his parties. Peter reluctantly agrees, but leaves with Arlo early into the party. Peter and Oscar begin to spend more time together, and a romance forms between them.

Short on funds, Peter resorts to selling drugs again in order to afford Arlo's health insurance. He later promises to let Arlo DJ at another club, but his set is delayed until late into the night. Peter abruptly leaves with him after seeing several people in the crowd overdose, during which the two briefly become separated. Peter retrieves him, but a vindictive Sophie sees them and calls child protective services. She confronts Peter at his apartment the following morning, where she frantically apologizes, claims her actions were the result of a drug-induced rage, promises to get sober, and offers to help him divert CPS' suspicions, but he furiously orders her out. Concerned for Arlo's well-being, CPS removes him from Peter's care and returns him to England. Peter travels to London to appeal, telling the judge that Arlo has inspired him to change his life for the better. Although moved by Peter's testimony, the judge rules that, due to Peter's past criminal record and suspicious money transactions recently found on his Venmo account, Arlo must stay in England, where he will be adopted by Leonora's friend Sharon. She additionally asserts that any communication between Arlo and Peter is strictly prohibited for at least a year, after which the amount of contact permitted between the two will be solely determined by Sharon. A devastated Peter returns to New York alone.

A year later, Peter has stopped partying, works as a bartender, studies psychology, and is still with Oscar. One night, he receives a phone call from Arlo, who is doing well with his new family in England. Sharon promises to allow Peter to visit Arlo in the future. After the call ends, Oscar comforts Peter as he cries. While leaving a bodega, Peter looks through the window of a nearby building and briefly glimpses a party. He stares for a while before walking away.
