spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in 1992 at an Acme lab, where experiments are being conducted on Looney Tunes like Daffy Duck (Eric Bauza). Dr. Lorre (Bauza) knows something shady is going on, so he leaks a message to an unknown contact before bidding Tweety (Bauza) farewell. Lorre evades guards in his escape but is cornered outside. He is forced to jump down a cartoon black hole for imprisonment, but he promises the truth will come out.

30 years later, somewhere in the desert outside Albuquerque, NM, Wile E. Coyote is up to his usual plotting to capture and eat the Road Runner. He uses Acme metal balls and a magnet glove to try and trap Road Runner, which works at first until it causes Wile E. to pull a truck onto him. He then tries to use rocket skates, but this backfires again and causes Wile E. to get stuck to a missile on a jet. The pilot fires the missile at the rocket skate, and Wile E. eventually crashes to the ground and gets the missile dropped on him.

Wile E. returns to his cave, defeated once again after decades of failures. He then sees a commercial on TV for lawyer Kevin Avery (Will Forte) of Avery, Jones, and Maltese, who represent cartoons that have endured physical trauma due to malfunctioning Acme products. Wile E. hatches an idea and makes his way to the city.

Cartoons co-exist with humans in the city. Other toons like Porky Pig (Bauza) have frequently been injured by Acme products, but the company is known for creating a bunch of life-changing products that people use all around the world. Kevin runs his firm alongside Dottie Jones (Martha Kelly) and Sal Maltese (Tone Bell), with Kevin’s niece Paige (Lana Condor) also helping as an intern, but the firm itself is not very successful and usually ends up dealing in settlements with the toons. Wile E. shows up to Kevin’s office and tries to communicate (with signs) his situation regarding Acme products. Kevin thinks the defective rocket skates aren’t enough for a big case, until Wile E. dumps his entire stash of busted Acme gadgets. When Kevin decides he can’t go up against Acme on such a big scale, Wile E. plants the stash in Kevin’s evidence box, leading to one of the toons in his employment to file the lawsuit for every single Acme product.

Acme’s head legal counsel, Buddy Crane (John Cena) is informed by his assistant Bill Pelicanos (P.J. Byrne) about the lawsuit. Kevin and Wile E. arrive at Acme, with Kevin not pleased to see Buddy since they both studied law at Harvard. Buddy and his team of lawyers are prepared to settle with Wile E. for $50K, but he responds by tearing up the contract and setting it on fire. This means a trial is moving forward.

With two weeks to go before the trial, Kevin, Paige, Dottie, Sal, and Wile E. all try to get Road Runner to testify as a witness to all the pain Wile E. endured when using Acme products, but they fail to catch him. The trial begins with Judge Troppogrosso (Luis Guzman) presiding over the case. Buddy already charms the court while Kevin and Wile E. have an embarrassing first day, since Buddy argues that Wile E.’s injuries are self-inflicted.

Back at his office, Kevin gets a phone call from an unknown whistleblower, who answer with a familiar voice: “Ehh…what’s up, doc?” The caller informs Kevin to go to a specific address to find a contact that will provide him with what he needs for the case.

Kevin is joined by Wile E. and Paige as they drive to the address. They are led to a backyard where Daffy is painting a portrait. When Kevin mentions Acme, this triggers Daffy to go looney, as he is at an institution for other toons who are nuttier than most. Daffy gives Kevin and Paige a box with Acme paint (which Dr. Lorre had stowed away) while the orderlies try to rein in the toons.

The trio discover that the Acme paint creates a secret tunnel. Kevin finds a message on the wall from Dr. Lorre, warning Daffy about something called “Project Sisyphus”. Wile E. then spots a real train coming down the tunnel, so he grabs Paige and Kevin before they get crushed by the train. They return to the office, where Kevin thinks that the case is too big for them to take on. Paige is disappointed in her uncle for giving up so easily. Kevin then goes over his files, where he settled for less and less with many of Porky’s cases. He decides to change his mind.

Foghorn Leghorn (Bauza) is the CEO of Acme. After learning of the ongoing case with Wile E., he warns Buddy not to let things get out of hand, or else other secrets may come to light.

Kevin and Wile E. go back to their motel room. Kevin overhears some commotion and notices Wile E. constructing some kind of contraption. He then sees a blueprint on Wile E.’s wall, revealing his true intentions are to use the trial as a trap for Road Runner so that he can finally catch and eat him. Kevin is mad about it but lies to Wile E. that Road Runner will be at the trial.

Paige pays a visit to Granny (Candi Milo), who was married to Dr. Lorre until he disappeared. She shows Paige that Lorre had developed useful Acme products until the news heads at the company forced him to start working on Project Sisyphus. Most of the people on that project have disappeared or have been forced to work for Acme, such as Tweety so that they won’t hurt Granny.

Buddy sends Bill and other Acme cronies (including Tweety) to capture Road Runner with their own methods. They drop a mountain of bird seed over a pool of glue to try and capture him, but it backfires on them when Road Runner flees and triggers an explosion that douses everyone in glue.

Kevin, Paige, and Wile E. play the caller’s message and play it back to hear the “Looney Tunes” theme. This leads them to the grounds of a carrot festival to meet the whistleblower…who is, of course, Bugs Bunny (Bauza). Through a flashback that he pulls onscreen, it is revealed that cartoons like Daffy tested out the good Acme products, until the news heads formed Project Sisyphus and started testing out products on the cartoons, causing them severe pain and misfortune. This led to them creating products that would be sold globally. Bugs has to flee before he is caught by Acme’s spies, but he wishes the heroes good luck.

Per Bugs’s suggestion, Kevin summons Acme’s head of public relations: the Tasmanian Devil (Jim Cummings). While Taz appears to be ready to give up some valuable information, Buddy and Bill quietly have Taz ejected from the courtroom. This leads Buddy to convince Troppogrosso to declare a mistrial due to a lack of evidence, effectively dismissing the case. However, when Kevin and Wile E. return to the office, they find a group of reporters and learn that the case has gone all the way to Congress after Kevin had told the press outside the courthouse about Project Sisyphus, and they want to hold the Acme Corporation accountable for their deeds. This brings the case straight to D.C.

Wile E. only agrees to join Kevin at the senate hearing after he lies that Road Runner will be there. Later, Sal calls Kevin to inform him that the firm is now completely broke because of all the money spent on the trial. In his frustration, Kevin admits to Wile E. that he lied and berates him for all his efforts, saying that he will never catch Road Runner. Wile E. leaves, defeated.

On the streets, Wile E. thinks he sees Road Runner, but it’s just a trap set by Tweety and another Acme thug. Kevin catches up with the rocket skates as he sees Wile E. in danger. Tweety and the thug cause the road to flip and also shoot explosive eggs at them, but Kevin is able to help throw them off their trail. However, he gets separated from Wile E. and crashes into a sign, knocking himself out.

Kevin wakes up disheveled but goes to the hearing without Wile E. Buddy catches Kevin in the bathroom and tries to bribe him with a settlement to walk away from the case, but Kevin refuses. He is forced to face the senators (one of whom is Elmer Fudd) and the Acme team. Kevin gives a speech just as Wile E. enters, where he admits that they are up against something bigger than them, but Wile E. has never given up even after so many failures, so Kevin has been inspired by him. The hearing begins with Kevin talking to Foghorn about Project Sisyphus and how it hurts cartoons. Foghorn argues that pain is necessary for progress, and it doesn’t matter because they are cartoons and they can endure a ton of pain.

When it seems like that’s the end, Road Runner actually shows up to testify. Kevin uses yes-or-no questions for the bird to reply, while Wile E. tries to use his contraption to catch his nemesis once and for all. However, Road Runner not only admits that he was a witness to Wile E.’s pain and suffering, but he also considers the Coyote a friend and even asks him if he is going back to the desert. Wile E. is touched and decides against setting off the trap.

Ultimately, while the senators are moved by the testimony, they ultimately dismiss the case due to a lack of sufficient evidence. After Buddy and Foghorn rub it in to Kevin and Wile E., Kevin and Paige encourage Wile E. to set off his trap. It leads to a Rube Goldberg style device with Acme products that end up forming a cage that drops on top of Buddy and Foghorn, humiliating them while the heroes leave the courtroom proudly.

The trio prepare to head back to the office as failures, only to find dozens of toons outside wanting to file lawsuits against Acme for all the trauma they’ve endured, thus saving the firm. Bugs then provides Kevin and Paige with video evidence of Acme’s Project Sisyphus tests on the toons. This is enough to have Buddy and Foghorn properly arrested. Dr. Lorre is also freed from captivity, allowing him and Tweety to reunite with Granny.

Kevin and Paige drive Wile E. out into the desert to bid him farewell. Wile E. leaves Kevin with a keepsake from his blueprint since they are now friends. Road Runner shows up to greet Wile E. before they jump into yet another big chase.

The ending text states that Paige is now a partner at the firm, which has now overseen many cases with toons against Acme. Wile E. is still out in the desert but still pops over to Albuquerque when he misses his friends. He still hasn’t caught Road Runner…but maybe someday, he will.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1992, in a world where cartoon characters co-exist with humans, Acme Corporation scientist Dr. Lorre leaks a message to an unknown contact before being captured and imprisoned inside an Acme portable hole.

Thirty years later, Wile E. Coyote fails to catch the Road Runner and sees a television ad for Avery, Jones & Maltese, a personal injury law firm in Albuquerque specializing in cartoon violence cases involving Acme products. Wile E. meets with senior partner Kevin Avery, looking to sue Acme for the various defective devices used in chasing the Road Runner. While Kevin's niece and intern Paige is eager to take Acme to court, Kevin prefers to settle to avoid a risky trial. However, Wile E. rejects the settlement offered by Acme's lawyer Buddy Crane, forcing a trial.

The firm tries to subpoena the Road Runner to testify, but he evades them. Meanwhile, Acme CEO Foghorn Leghorn warns Buddy to prevent the trial from revealing any corporate secrets. After a poor first trial session, Kevin receives a tip from an anonymous whistleblower to meet with former Acme employee Daffy Duck, who conveys the warning Lorre sent him in 1992 about "Project Sisyphus". Kevin admits to Wile E. that he tries to settle all cases due to having lost multiple trials early in his career, but Wile E. encourages Kevin to believe he can beat Acme the same way Wile E. believes he will catch the Road Runner. Though this inspires Kevin, he soon discovers Wile E.'s motive for the lawsuit is to capture the Road Runner in court. Acme attempts to catch the Road Runner, believing he will testify against Wile E. given their past, but the Road Runner evades them. Meanwhile, Paige learns from Lorre's wife Granny that, before his disappearance, Lorre did product development for Acme, who now force their pet Tweety to serve as Acme's mercenary.

The team discovers the whistleblower is Bugs Bunny, who reveals Project Sisyphus is a product testing program formerly headed by Dr. Lorre, using cartoon violence to improve Acme's products for humans. When the program drove its test subjects insane, Lorre tried to object, but was silenced, and Acme pivoted to testing in the wild on unsuspecting clients like Wile E. Off Bugs' suggestion, Kevin tries to get Project Sisyphus on the record by questioning Acme's Head of PR Tasmanian Devil on the stand, but Acme's legal team sabotage him and Judge Troppogrosso dismisses the case.

However, Kevin reveals the conspiracy to the press, prompting the government to call a congressional hearing in Washington, D.C. Wile E. only agrees to join when Kevin claims the Road Runner will be there. The night before the hearing, Kevin admits the truth after being badgered about it and berates Wile E. for his obsession with the Road Runner, prompting Wile E. to storm out. While wandering the streets, Wile E. narrowly evades Tweety's attempt to kill him. Kevin tries to rescue him, but gets knocked out and separated when Wile E. abandons him once again, still offended.

Kevin rejects a last bribe attempt by Buddy and gives an impassioned speech at the hearing, admiring Wile E.'s determination despite repeated failures. Wile E. arrives, having overheard, and reconciles with Kevin. Kevin gets Foghorn to publicly admit to Project Sisyphus, but Foghorn argues that cartoon characters are not important enough for anyone to care if they are harmed. However, the Road Runner arrives and testifies to the harm Acme products have caused Wile E. over the years and further explains as Wile E.'s friend that he cares for and misses him, moving Wile E. to spare him. Senator Elmer Fudd declines to pursue federal charges due to Wile E. being the sole plaintiff. As Buddy and Foghorn gloat, Wile E. activates the trap he had set for the Road Runner, caging and humiliating the Acme team.

Back in Albuquerque, the firm is inundated with cartoon characters also seeking to sue Acme for damages. Further leaks from Bugs launch a federal investigation that exposes the full extent of Project Sisyphus and leads to the arrests of Foghorn and Buddy. Dr. Lorre is freed and reunites with Granny and Tweety. Wile E. bids goodbye to Kevin and Paige, who is now a partner at the firm, before reuniting with the Road Runner and resuming their chase.

spoiler_text.text:
The film starts with Andy Sachs (Anne Hathaway) going to an awards ceremony with her colleagues at The Vanguard. However, just before Andy is announced to accept an award, she and her whole team receive news of their termination via text. Andy goes to get her award but gives an impassioned speech over the firing and how journalism is still as important as ever.

At Runway, Miranda Priestley (Meryl Streep) is dealing with the fallout of a scandal due to the company appearing to endorse a sweatshop company called SpeedFash. She is aided by Nigel (Stanley Tucci), as well as her new assistant Amari (Simone Ashley)(the new Emily), as she attends a fashion event in an attempt to divert attention away from the situation. Miranda is also now married to a quartet member named Stuart (Kenneth Branagh). She gets a call from Irv Ravitz (Tibor Feldman), the chairman of Runway, who wants her to handle the debacle as soon as possible. Irv’s son Jay (B.J. Novak) gets a text with a video of Andy’s speech, which he shows to his father.

Andy is shown living in a crappy apartment and gets help from her friend Lily (Tracie Thoms). She gets a call from Irv, who was moved by her speech and is offering her a new job back at Runway in the Features department to essentially help Miranda. Andy runs this by her work colleagues, who encourage her to go for it.

Andy returns to Runway and reunites with Nigel, but Miranda hardly remembers her (even as “one of the Emilys”). The three go to Dior, where Emily (Emily Blunt) now works after leaving Runway. She is stunned to see her old colleagues in a new higher position. The group tries to negotiate, during which Andy notices tensions between Miranda and Emily. Emily wants advertising in Runway for Dior to keep them afloat. Miranda makes it clear to Andy that rehiring her was not Miranda’s idea and makes her take the train back home.

Back at Runway, Andy meets Charlie, AKA “Charlie The Chair” (Caleb Hearon)(the new Andy), as well as her own personal assistant, Jin Chao (Helen J. Shen). She also has lunch with Nigel, who says that Runway is barely a magazine anymore since everything has gone digital, and even Miranda has to resort to posting clickbait articles or short-form content. Andy also sees that Miranda has had to deal with HR complaints (she has to hang her own coat instead of tossing it at her assistants).

Andy stays up late to write an article that helps sway opinion on Runway back towards the positive side, especially with Irv. She is disappointed that Miranda doesn’t show gratitude for her work. Andy learns from Charlie that Miranda has always wanted an interview with Sasha Barnes (Lucy Liu), a recently divorced billionaire who took a huge portion from her ex-husband Benji (Justin Theroux). Andy grinds hard with the articles but isn’t getting the views Irv wants. When backed into a corner, Andy lies to Miranda and says that she got a meeting with Sasha, but she makes extensive phone calls to actually get in touch with Sasha and scheduling an interview.

Andy visits Emily for a brief catch-up. She tells Andy about how she’s divorced with two kids and how she believes fashion is now more lucrative in retail. Emily also makes a comment about Andy’s eyebrows.

Lily takes Andy to go look for a better apartment. They go to an open house, where Andy meets Peter (Patrick Brammall), who helped designed the building. They hit it off, which Lily notices.

Once Andy nabs an interview date with Sasha (“the holy grail”), she and Miranda travel to her villa for a sit-down, where Sasha reveals she is happier and more successful after leaving Benji and is engaged to a new guy, which she allows Runway to break to the public.

Andy’s friend Talia (Rachel Bloom) from The Vanguard is talking to a publisher for Andy to write a tell-all book about working for Miranda, but she is afraid that Miranda would find out and crucify her.

Over the weekend, Miranda invites Andy to her lake house where she has invited Irv, Jay, and other celebrity guests like Ronny Chieng, Karl-Anthony Towns, and Jenna Bush Hager. Miranda talks to Andy privately about how Irv is planning to promote Miranda to Global Head of Content, while the Features Department will be getting a significant budget increase.

Andy, Miranda, and Nigel go to a birthday celebration for Irv, with Peter joining Andy as her date. They also discover that Emily is dating Benji Barnes, though it’s clear she doesn’t love him (and he is also a giant idiot). Things take a sharp turn when Irv collapses from a fatal heart attack in the middle of the party.

After Irv’s death, Jay takes over as chairman and arranges a meeting with Miranda and other executives over the future of Runway. Jin hides her phone by their table to record their entire conversation and bring it back to Andy. She finds out that Jay intends to gut most of Runway in a cost-cutting effort. As a result, Miranda has to start doing things like flying economy instead of first class. The stress of the situation causes Andy to lash out at Peter, and he decides to leave until she’s chilled out.

As everyone travels to Milan for Fashion Week, Andy goes behind Miranda’s back to get help from Emily so that they can arrange a meeting between Benji and Jay in an effort to get Jay to sell Runway to Benji. However, Andy eventually feels compelled to come clean to Miranda, but she quickly calls it a betrayal. Andy doesn’t know what she’s talking about until Emily admits that she only agreed to help Andy so that Benji can buy Runway for Emily, as payback for Miranda pushing for her to leave the company and go to Dior. Miranda defends her actions by saying that Emily lacked creative vision.

At a gala dinner, Miranda speaks to Benji, who has plans to turn Runway into an AI-driven medium, which doesn’t sit right with Miranda. Meanwhile, Andy tells Talia that she will not do the book on Miranda, and she proceeds to make some phone calls.

The Fashion Week event brings in Lady Gaga to perform music, which Miranda did as a reluctant favor since the two of them do not get on very well. As Miranda is set to deliver a big speech on the importance of Runway, she instead decides to let Nigel read it since he wrote it and she feels as though she has taken him for granted.

Jay goes to Benji and Emily’s villa to discuss the sale, only for him to get a phone call and have him change his mind since he got a much better offer from another buyer. It turns out to be Sasha, who swooped in to save Runway and also gives Miranda the promotion she was promised. As Andy and Miranda leave Sasha’s villa, Miranda says she knows all about the tell-all book and encourages Andy to write it and not skimp on any details.

After returning to New York, Andy goes to see Peter and reconcile with him. She also later meets with Emily, who has dyed her hair blonde and has been dumped by Benji, and also has gone to work for Coach. Emily admits that she did call Andy one time after their time at Runway in an attempt to be friends, but Andy thought it was a pocket dial. They agree to start a friendship right there.

Andy returns to Runway with a much nicer office, and sees that Amari, Jin, and Charlie have all gotten promotions as well. She also learns from Nigel that it was he who sent Irv and Jay the video of her speech so that she can get rehired, saying Andy is “always his girl”. Andy then goes to deliver a new article to Miranda, who responds with her typical indifference, but she has a smile on her face when she actually reads it.

wiki_plot.text:
Two decades after leaving Runway magazine, Andrea "Andy" Sachs has become a respected global journalist based in New York City. However, her entire newsroom is abruptly laid off by text message during an awards ceremony. Meanwhile, Miranda Priestly, Andy's old Runway boss, is under fire for publishing a puff piece about a fashion brand that uses sweatshop labor. 

To improve the magazine's credibility, Irv Ravitz, who owns Runway's parent company, Elias-Clarke, and is Miranda's boss, hires Andy as the features editor without Miranda's knowledge. An uncharacteristically listless Miranda struggles to navigate modern fashion media. Although she retains some tyrannical office behavior, HR complaints have blunted her imperiousness. By contrast, she enjoys a close relationship with her husband, Stuart.

Miranda's right-hand assistant, Nigel Kipling, tells Andy that people no longer read Runway's print edition, forcing the brand to embrace online clickbait and cheaply made short-form content to retain advertisers and generate profit. One key advertiser is Dior, which employs Emily Charlton, Andy's former Runway co-worker. Emily leverages the controversy over the Runway puff piece to secure free advertising and a Dior article, which Miranda assigns to Andy. During the interview, Emily and Andy spar over how modern fashion has raised retail prices and shuts out middle-class consumers.

After writing serious articles that gain minimal traction, Andy improves her Runway standing by brokering a coveted interview with Sasha Barnes, the reclusive divorcée of Silicon Valley billionaire, Benji Barnes. Irv promises to make Miranda global head of content at Elias-Clarke but suffers a fatal heart attack at his 75th birthday party before officially announcing the promotion. His son, Jay, takes over Elias-Clarke and puts Miranda's promotion on hold while bringing in management consultants to restructure the magazine and recommend cost cuts. To Andy's surprise, Miranda bears with it. Meanwhile, Andy's romantic interest in Peter stalls when she unintentionally dismisses his job as an apartment renovator while fretting over her own career. Considering her options, Andy explores writing a tell-all book about Miranda. A publisher offers her a lucrative contract, but Andy is conflicted. 

During Milan Fashion Week, Andy devises a plan to save Runway by finding a wealthy patron to buy it from Jay. The patron is Benji Barnes, Emily's current boyfriend. Miranda is furious, knowing Emily secretly plans to assume her position at Runway. Miranda admits to pushing out Emily from Runway, saying she lacks creative vision. Miranda acts graciously over losing her position, but during discussions with Benji, his intent to replace Runway's staff by AI alarms her. 

To prevent Benji and Emily from destroying Runway, Miranda directs Andy to find a competing buyer. Andy convinces Sasha to buy not just Runway but all of Elias-Clarke; Jay accepts her offer, cancelling his deal with Benji. Miranda realizes she has taken Nigel for granted over the years. To make amends, she asks him to deliver the gala's keynote speech in her place, while she and Andy finalize the deal with Sasha, who gives Miranda the promotion Irv promised her.

As the Runway staff return to New York, Miranda admits to Andy that the latter's idealism inspired her to fight back. She also reveals knowing about Andy's plans for a tell-all book and encourages her to write it, including the negative aspects of Miranda's life. Andy reconciles with Peter and also with the defeated Emily, who is now working at COACH fashion and whom Benji broke up with. Nigel reveals that he prompted Irv to rehire Andy. Miranda gives Andy a nicer office and returns to work with a renewed imperiousness.
wiki_plot.title: The Devil Wears Prada 2

reviews.text: I loved this brilliant movie. It’s smart and trippy and aggressive and funny and ambitious. It’s worth making the time see and decide for yourself what you make of it. For me? 10/10 🪏

Fossil Fools was hackneyed 25 years ago when it was an independent minimalist production, and I can't even begin to express my misgivings with a Kenny Rockwell-funded larger-than-life mega-production where the overblown sets and special effects scream louder than the actors ever could. We get it - Compson was a buffoon! Rockwell was a sociopath! Do you have anything else to say?!
But with that said, it's pretty evide…
movies do not have the power to change the world
“wait, is this fucking play about us??”

“you’re both right. you’re all right. now what?” 
art won’t save the world. 
but it’s probably too late for anything to pull the world out of this mess partially of our own making, yet one also massively worsened by thousands of moronic men who’ve spent generations growing their wealth at its expense and who remain fundamentally impossible to oppose. we’ve glued ourselves to the seats on an unstoppable train they own…
It feels like a whole movie of Mark Ruffalo’s scenes in Mickey 17

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in the mansion of Digger Rockwell (Tom Cruise), a notorious oil baron. He owns and operates Rockwell United, which drills for oil in Alaska and Greenland. Digger lives alone with his dying cat Maggie, though he also has some staff members nearby, including his assistant Lina (Emma D’Arcy).

Digger is contacted by Sandy Clarkson (Danny Kirrane), who is working at the oil field in Greenland. Sandy brings up how he mentioned two weeks earlier that a crack has formed in the ice, which has grown to almost 30 feet since then. Sandy suggests shutting the operation down for safety, but Digger refuses. Moments later, he is visited by both his half-sister Emma (Sandra Huller) and Dr. Nirav Ganesh (Riz Ahmed), plus two other men. It has been reported that the Greenland oil field has exploded, implicitly killing Sandy and everyone else there. The result is an ice shelf the size of Maryland, which Ganesh calls “Judy”, that is heading towards Europe.

Digger and Ganesh meet with U.S. President Compson (John Goodman), as well as other military men and officials, like Vice President Eddie Fryman (Michael Stuhlbarg). Ganesh explains that Judy’s trajectory will head towards Norway within three days, causing a devastating tsunami with untold casualties. The men agree to set up a firewall to prevent word getting out to the public and causing a panic, instead hoping the ice shelf will just drift off somewhere and melt. Compson then speaks privately to Digger about his struggle with rectal cancer.

Suddenly, a tree falls down randomly in front of Digger and Compson. Then a large man emerges from a trap door to fix the tree. It is revealed that the whole story is part of a play called “Fossil Fools”, directed by a woman named Hannah (Sophie Wilde), though Digger and the other characters are based off real people. Digger is played by an actor named Curtis Markson, while Compson’s actor is named Doug. Between takes, Curtis tries to get in touch with his daughter Hope (Flora Higgins), who has gotten on a plane out of Jamaica that is heading into a dangerous storm. Everything up to now is part of the dress rehearsal, and their first preview is happening later that day. A producer named Kenny (Jesse Plemons) also frequently checks in on Curtis and offers to help locate Hope since he works for a security company.

As the rehearsal continues, Digger joins Compson, Eddie, Ganesh, and other military brass as they witness Judy’s impact with Norway, horrifying them. With Compson being admitted to a hospital, Eddie must step in with a response. Digger informs Eddie of his new position. Digger later talks with Emma about his upcoming trip to Europe to meet with European Parliament, and she tries to encourage him.

Ganesh joins Digger on a plane to Europe. Although Ganesh tries to stress the severity of Judy’s impact, Digger goes off on a diatribe about the tuna that has been served to him, which does calm Ganesh down after he tries it. Digger goes up before Parliament and takes responsibility for the disaster, but also throws back in everyone’s face that, as much as they claim they want to switch to more sustainable energy sources, they are all dependent on oil. As Digger’s rant grows, someone throws a microphone at his head, while the rest of Parliament devolves into just saying “blah blah blah”.

Later on, a drunken Ganesh informs Digger and Compson that an even larger ice shelf, which Digger dubs “Kremlinova”, has broken off and is heading toward Alaska. Compson goes on a rant about war with China and Russia before deciding to nuke Kremlinova, even though Ganesh warns that will just make smaller icebergs that make things worse.

Digger joins Compson, Eddie, and others in flying a plane to drop missiles onto Kremlinova, which does what Ganesh said would happen by making smaller icebergs. Digger’s character eventually pushes Curtis to his limit, and he clashes with Hannah onstage as he feels that the story has become too over-the-top, and that the real Digger was a more composed and soft-spoken man. Kenny then steps in and reveals himself as Kenny Rockwell, Digger’s nephew. He agrees with both Curtis and Hannah in regards to how the play is depicted. While he acknowledges that his uncle was less cartoonish than the play makes him out to be, Kenny recalls watching the play 15 years earlier and seeing people cheering at the catharsis of the final scene, since the real Digger and Compson really did doom the planet, and even Kenny agreed with their reactions. With this, the rest of the show goes on.

In the epilogue of the play (which is now the actual preview with an audience), five years have passed since the Kremlinova disaster. Digger, Emma, Lina, and any of their remaining associates have been exiled to an oil rig in Alaska, and Eddie, now POTUS, has cut Digger off from any sort of bailout. Lina informs Digger that all of their food has spoiled, while the rest has been taken by crew members who escaped. When Digger looks in the freezer, he is horrified to discover that they have kept Compson’s corpse frozen. Digger then kneels down outside to pray, and then appears to see that the freezer has been restocked with plenty of food (but that’s just his own delusion). Digger goes to the front of the boat to spread Maggie’s ashes and is met by Kyle (Teddy Hawley), Emma’s son meant to represent Kenny, at which point Curtis’s phone goes off so he can briefly answer it and learn that Hope was located. After some final words, Digger jumps into the ocean to drown himself. The entire audience cheers at his demise.

The show wraps, and the cast and crew celebrate. Curtis is met by his wife Agatha (Annabel Mullion), and they both thank Kenny for helping to track down Hope’s plane. The actors then go up onstage to give their final bow. The audience members then wear masks before going outside, as the streets are now flooded and there are armed police and robots patrolling the streets.

wiki_plot.text:
Aging oil magnate Digger Rockwell colludes with U.S. President Compson to allow Digger's company, Rockwell United, to extract oil in Alaska and Greenland. Despite repeated warnings about methane beneath the Greenland field, Digger proceeds with extraction operations. Soon after, he learns that the unexpected explosion of one such pocket has dislodged a massive ice shelf and sent it toward Europe. Environmental Safety Chief Dr. Nirav Ganesh warns that its collision with Norway in three days will trigger devastating tidal waves across the North Sea. Rather than inform the public, Compson and Digger establish an information firewall, gambling that the shelf might drift into the Atlantic Ocean and melt. They also discuss Compson's deteriorating health due to rectal cancer.

A prop failure reveals that all events depicted thus far are scenes in a satirical play, titled Fossil Fools, with actor Curtis Markson playing the lead role of Digger. The cast are conducting a dress rehearsal before the play's imminent premiere. Between scenes, Curtis learns that a plane carrying his daughter Hope has disappeared after encountering a category six hurricane. Producer Kenny offers to help locate her through his private intelligence network.

Continuing the play, the ice shelf strikes Europe, flooding major Northern European cities. The United States and Rockwell United are summoned before a fictionalized version of the European Parliament. Vice President Eddie represents Compson, who is undergoing surgery, and promises American assistance. Though accepting responsibility for the disaster, Digger argues that neither he nor his company can be blamed for society's dependence on oil, since he is merely fulfilling global demand. His speech provokes the attendees into fighting among themselves rather than confronting him. Later, a drunken Ganesh warns Digger that an even larger ice shelf has broken away from a Russian glacier and is heading toward Alaska.

Digger and Ganesh inform the sickly Compson. In drug-addled delusion, Compson proposes launching nuclear weapons at China as a distraction, but Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Fitzgerald recommends targeting the ice shelf instead. Ganesh warns that the strike will fragment the shelf without slowing it down. Nevertheless, Compson authorizes the attack, and Ganesh's prediction proves correct.

Meanwhile, Curtis grows increasingly troubled by the play's satirical excesses. During rehearsal, he breaks down and accuses the production of distorting real events and trivializing the suffering of those who were harmed. Kenny, the real Digger's nephew, explains that he watched an earlier production of Fossil Fools years ago. He subsequently decided to purchase the rights to the play and stage his own production in the hopes that it would help give the public a constructive and cathartic way to process its collective grief. Understanding the significance of his performance, Curtis completes the rehearsal.

Following the ice shelf disaster, Digger and his family are exiled to a converted offshore platform. Five years later, Eddie has succeeded Compson as president after his death, withdrawing all funding and military protection from the platform, which prompts most of Digger's employees to abandon him and steal his food, gold, and boats. Increasingly delusional, Digger attempts to bully God into providing food for the remaining occupants. When this fails, he scatters the ashes of his cat Maggie, shares a brief moment with Kenny (named Kyle in the play), and commits suicide by jumping into the polluted ocean.

The audience watching the play applauds Digger's death and Curtis's performance. Curtis's wife Agatha arrives to congratulate him and reveals that Hope has been found safe, thanks to Kenny. Theater management then announces a "Level 4" condition outside. Audience members put on respirators and leave the theater, emerging into a flooded, devastated city patrolled by soldiers, robots, and drones.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens at a wrestling match. A man named Daniel Kellner (Josh O’Connor) is approached by two agents from the Wardex Corporation, demanding his backpack in exchange for the safe return of his girlfriend Jane (Eve Hewson). Daniel follows the agents to the back of the arena, where they meet with Wardex CEO Noah Scanlon (Colin Firth) and his other cronies. Jane is returned to Daniel, but Scanlon wants a device that Daniel had stolen. He threatens to activate the device, forcing Scanlon’s gunmen to back down and allow Daniel and Jane to escape.

On his way out, Daniel gets in touch with his contact, Hugo Wakefield (Colman Domingo), a Wardex employee working against them along with a team of people. They are in the process of constructing some type of set, and Hugo tells Daniel to lay low. Jane directs Daniel to a convent that she used to be part of so that they can stay hidden.

Back at Wardex, Scanlon and his team use their technology to try and track Daniel down. Scanlon brands him a spy, turning him into a fugitive from authorities.

In Kansas City, meteorologist Margaret Fairchild (Emily Blunt) is watching her show with her boyfriend Jackson (Wyatt Russell). A cardinal flies in through the open window, which Margaret notices. She then starts speaking in Russian to Jackson, but when he asks her about it, she has no memory of speaking another language.

Margaret leaves early because she is set to go on air earlier than usual. She gets pulled over by a cop for going too fast. Before Margaret can give the cop her license and registration, she starts to tell him deeply personal info about himself and what he should do to make his wife happy. The cop is so stunned that he lets Margaret go.

At the station, Margaret talks to some of the other crew members about personal info, such as knowing that one of the female staff members is being abused. When the cameras roll on Margaret, she freezes up and starts appearing to speak in an alien language. After she finishes, Margaret faints and the crew rushes to her side.

Daniel and Jane are picked up by a friend named Dave Santiago (Tommy Martinez). He takes them to a farm house for them to hide out. Jane demands to know what Daniel is hiding, so he shows her files that he stole from Wardex, which contain video clips of people from the company experimenting on extraterrestrial life forms.

Viral footage of Margaret’s incident hits Wardex. While at the hospital with Jackson, the nurse asks her about an incident from her childhood that Jackson brought up, since he mentions her talking about weird dreams like seeing animals or a “Hansel and Gretel house in the woods”, but Margaret doesn’t want to talk about it. Margaret sees guys in suits that the nurse says identified as FBI, but Margaret knows they are not FBI. She and Jackson sneak out of the hospital and break her phone after she is contacted by Hugo. She realizes she needs to head north to find Daniel, and an exasperated Jackson drives her.

Hugo contacts Daniel about Margaret. While everyone else hears alien gibberish, Daniel understands what she’s saying as “Don’t be afraid of what you don’t know”.

Scanlon uses a machine and an alien device that allows him to “dive” into the minds of others. He attempts it at first with Daniel but is quickly blocked out. Scanlon then uses it on Jane. She tries to break the hold on her by squeezing her cross necklace into her palm, but Scanlon maintains his hold on Jane and makes her conceal a knife for when Daniel returns.

Margaret calls Daniel to warn him that she knows Scanlon’s men are arriving at the farm house to come for him and Jane. Daniel sneaks past the gunmen and steals one of their cars. He crashes through the farm house to pick up Jane, leading to a chase. Scanlon tries to make Jane kill Daniel, but the agents ramming into their car causes the link to break. Daniel and Jane cause the car to go off a cliff and into the lake, allowing them to escape from the gunmen’s sight.

Margaret and Jackson stop at a gas station, since people believe that World War 3 is imminent. Jackson calls for authorities to pick them up, but Margaret knows what is happening and she steals Jackson’s car to go find Daniel herself, but she has a child nearby let Jackson know she loves him and that she has to continue alone.

Daniel and Jane stop at a motel to hide out. He is called by Hugo, who informs him that the following day, he will need to go to a specific location – KCXE, the station where Margaret works at. Later that night, Scanlon dives into Jane’s mind again, making him find the location of the motel so he can send more agents after them. When Daniel sees they have been caught, he helps Jane escape with his evidence before he is apprehended by the gunmen.

Margaret makes it to the black site location of the Wardex team, and Scanlon allows her to pass through security since he knows who she is. When Scanlon faces Margaret, he sees his late wife in place of her, causing him to become emotional. Her abilities allow the others to let her and Daniel go. One of Scanlon’s men, the overzealous Casper Boyd (Henry Lloyd-Hughes), grabs his guns and goes after Daniel and Margaret.

Daniel and Margaret are driving away, when they discuss the events that have affected them. Margaret mentions the cardinal, and Daniel says he remembers seeing something similar when he was a child, which is why he is able to understand the alien language. Boyd shows up and tries to ram them into the path of a train. The car locks onto the train, forcing Daniel and Margaret to try and jump onboard as Boyd tries to shoot them. They narrowly avoid getting crushed by another oncoming train. Margaret starts to have an intense panic attack until Daniel calms her down.

Scanlon dives into Hugo’s mind, trying to convince him to end his endeavors, but Hugo thinks that whatever Wardex has been trying to cover up for nearly 80 years has to be exposed now. Two of Hugo’s teammates unwittingly expose themselves to Scanlon, which allows him to track their faces and identify them as other Wardex employees.

Daniel and Margaret are walking down the road when they see a fox approaching them briefly before scurrying off. They are found by two fire trucks thanks to Santiago, who takes the two of them to see Hugo and his team. Margaret is overwhelmed to see that they have reconstructed her entire childhood home. Other people appear to view Margaret like a messiah, but she doesn’t want to be part of something like this. Hugo wants her to tap into a memory from her childhood that she has tried to block out, so that the team may better understand the truth about the extraterrestrial beings.

Daniel and Margaret are connected to a device that makes them relive their memories from childhood. The aliens appeared to them as animals (a deer, a cardinal, a fox) in a form they would be comfortable with, and lured them (or at least Margaret) to the “Hansel and Gretel house”. The aliens experimented on both children, which gave them their psychic abilities.

Scanlon and his goons track the whistleblowers down. However, they are camouflaged thanks to Margaret holding the alien device and making it impossible for the Wardex goons to see them. Daniel and Hugo lead the others out and into a fire truck, allowing them to get out while invisible before the device disintegrates in Margaret’s hands.

Everyone heads to the KCXE station, including the villains. Margaret convinces her boss and the crew to allow her to go on air for a special report. The Wardex goons do everything to shut down the station’s power, including the emergency generator, but Jane arrives and gives Margaret the other hidden device for her to bring the power back. After Daniel uploads the entirety of his video files to the network, Margaret powers everything up again. Scanlon ultimately gives up his pursuit and sits down, while a frustrated Boyd leaves.

Margaret begins the broadcast, which she dubs “Disclosure Day”. Other networks across the country, and soon the rest of the world, are tuned in. Footage of aliens going all the way back to 1947 during the infamous Roswell incident show that aliens were recovered and experimented on for decades. The entire world watches the truth unfolding before them. When the video clips finish, the whistleblowers bring out a recovered alien. It emerges, standing over seven feet tall. It whispers something to Daniel, who relays it back to Margaret. She returns to the camera and prepares to tell everyone the message, starting off by saying, “Listen”.

wiki_plot.text:
As the planet is on the brink of a nuclear war, cybersecurity specialist Dr. Daniel Kellner has stolen material from his employer, a secretive U.S. government contractor known as the Wardex Corporation (Waived Reporting, Development, and Extraction). Daniel's theft includes an artifact of extraterrestrial technology and "The Archive": decades of documents and hard drives containing footage of extraterrestrial encounters dating to the Roswell incident. When cornered by Wardex CEO Noah Scanlon, Daniel threatens him with the extraterrestrial device and escapes with his girlfriend, Jane Blankenship; they hide at her former convent.

Meanwhile, in Kansas City, local NBC affiliate meteorologist Margaret Fairchild is preparing for work when a cardinal flies into her home. The incident stimulates a psychic ability in Margaret to intuit people's thoughts and speak in languages she has never learned. During a live weather broadcast, Margaret unexpectedly begins speaking in an unknown language then passes out. Footage of the broadcast goes viral and draws the attention of Wardex, which identifies the language as extraterrestrial. After being examined at a hospital, Margaret flees Wardex agents who are posing as the FBI.

Daniel explains to Jane that Wardex has been experimenting on extraterrestrial captives and reverse engineering their technology; he is part of a plot to reveal the truth using the Archive. Seeing the clip of Margaret speaking the extraterrestrial language, he understands what she said as if she was speaking English. Scanlon uses one of the extraterrestrial devices to telepathically force Jane to attack Daniel and later track them to a motel. Before Daniel is captured, he helps Jane escape with the extraterrestrial device.

Margaret's psychic ability allows her to locate Daniel at a black site. The two escape with the Archive when Margaret empathically convinces their captors to let them go. One of Scanlon's unaffected men, Casper Boyd, rams their car into the side of a passing freight train; Daniel pulls Margaret out in time for them to climb onto the train and escape.

Margaret and Daniel finally connect with Hugo Wakefield, who leads a team of former Wardex employees intent on disclosing evidence of extraterrestrials to the world. They have reconstructed Margaret's childhood home in order to recover suppressed memories. When they were ten, she and Daniel were simultaneously abducted by extraterrestrials and given complementary powers; the extraterrestrials disguise themselves as harmless animals in order to anonymously observe humanity and eventually awaken their powers.

Hugo's team, along with Margaret and Daniel, enter Margaret's television station to broadcast the truth. Scanlon's team turns off the power, but Jane arrives and gives her device to Margaret, who uses it to restore the power. Defeated, Scanlon and his team stand down, to Boyd's dismay, and watch as Margaret announces "Disclosure Day" to the world.

Daniel uploads the Archive to a satellite feed as the station crew broadcast the footage around the world, with a blindsided national anchorwoman attempting to narrate it. The stunned world stops to watch evidence of extraterrestrial life and the impending war seems to halt. Hugo brings an elderly extraterrestrial he secretly freed from Wardex into the studio. The extraterrestrial whispers to Daniel, who relays the message to Margaret. She returns to the camera and prepares to repeat the message, beginning by saying "Listen."

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens at a cafe, where Charlie Thompson (Robert Pattinson) sees Emma Harwood (Zendaya) reading a book. He quickly googles it to try and spark a conversation with her, but she doesn’t hear him. He tries to talk to her again but she reveals that she is deaf in her right ear and couldn’t hear him since she was listening to music. They agree to do over their introduction.

Charlie and Emma become a couple and are now set to be married two years later. Charlie is writing his wedding speech with his buddy Mike (Mamoudou Athie), while Emma is with Mike’s wife Rachel (Alana Haim) and their coworker Alice (Hannah Gross) and talking about how Charlie is the first guy that Emma has really ever had any feelings for. Charlie goes over some stuff with Mike, like how he is sort of put off by Emma’s laugh and having to be told by Mike not to talk about their sex life.

In the week leading up to the wedding, Charlie and Emma go through a few things. They get into an argument with their dance instructor for not taking things seriously. On their way home, they see their DJ Pauline (Sydney Lemmon) smoking heroin on the streets.

The couple are later joined by Mike and Rachel as they sample wines for the wedding, but the venue staff are annoyed at them treating the place like a bar. When Charlie and Emma bring up Pauline and consider firing her, Rachel suggests a game they call “The Dog Story”, which is about discussing the worst thing they have ever done. It is named because Mike used an ex-girlfriend as a human shield against a street dog in Mexico. Rachel says her thing was that she locked her “slow” neighbor in the closet of an abandoned RV and left him there until a search party had to go find him. Charlie can only come up with that he cyberbullied a kid when he was 14 and made his family move. Emma then confesses that, at the age of 15, she nearly committed a school shooting, and this explains why she is deaf in one ear, because she was practicing and put the gun too close to her head. This hits a nerve with Rachel, who says her cousin was confined to a wheelchair after a shooting.

Charlie starts to grow anxious and has second thoughts about the wedding. He tries to talk to Emma about it, and she recounts how, as a teenager (played by Jordyn Curet), she was bullied and planned to use her father’s rifle to kill her classmates. However, another shooting happened at the mall, claiming the life of one of Emma’s classmates. She would join the other students in anti-gun protests, finally finding other friends and disposing of her dad’s gun. Despite Charlie acting like he is understanding, he still shows discomfort, like throwing away a coffee mug that has a gun design on it.

Rachel tells Emma and Charlie that she’s not going to the wedding anymore despite being the maid of honor, especially since it’s implied Emma got Rachel kicked off a project at work. Charlie goes to talk to her, as he has begun trying to find ways to defend and reconcile with Emma’s confession. He relays a slightly altered story to Mike and Rachel that Emma told him about a neighbor of hers who died in a car accident when they were kids, though Charlie makes it seem like Emma’s mindset was broken over the death of a close friend. This makes Rachel reconsider.

Outside the building, Charlie runs into Rachel’s cousin Sam (Anna Baryshnikov), the one who was paralyzed. He awkwardly tries to introduce himself to her and makes her uncomfortable, saying that she “would love Emma”.

Later at work, Charlie talks to his coworker Misha (Hailey Benton Gates). He asks her hypothetically how she would feel if her boyfriend planned a school shooting when he was a teenager. She says she would probably call the police. Charlie breaks down and goes to a nearby office to cry. Misha goes to console him but he ends up kissing her and almost tries to have sex with her (which she seems to go along with), but he stops himself and apologizes for his behavior.

Emma and Charlie later meet with Pauline to discuss what they saw. She claims she wasn’t smoking heroin and calls Emma a cunt for this, so Pauline gets fired.

The day of the wedding arrives, and Charlie and Emma are married. During the reception, Emma’s father Roger (Damon Gumpton) gives a speech and alludes to the missing rifle. Rachel then gives a passive-aggressive speech to both Charlie and Emma.

During the break, Emma overhears Misha talking about a school shooting, thinking that Rachel talked to her about it. She grabs Misha and brings her to see Charlie. Misha inadvertently reveals that Charlie kissed her, which stuns Emma. They return to the reception, where Charlie gives a painfully awkward speech to Emma about loving her, but he still makes a comment about her laugh and their sex life. Then he mentions trying to cheat with Misha, leading her boyfriend Blake (Michael Abbott Jr) to get up and headbutt Charlie, leaving him with a bloody nose and black eyes. Emma goes home with her parents.

Charlie returns to his empty apartment and dances alone to a song that Emma knows cheers him up. He then goes alone to the diner near his place that he and Emma loved going to. He sits down, and Emma arrives moments later to join him. Before he can apologize for his actions, Emma talks to Charlie as though they are meeting for the first time, giving them a chance to start over. They take each others’ hands and smile.

wiki_plot.text:
At a Boston café, Charlie Thompson approaches Emma Harwood while she is reading, pretending to have read the same book. Emma seems to ignore him, so he returns to his seat and later apologizes for his approach. Emma then explains that she is deaf in one ear and did not hear him and invites Charlie to retry his approach, leading to a date.

Two years later, Emma and Charlie are due to be married in a week. They see their wedding DJ, Pauline, smoking heroin in a public park. While discussing whether to fire her with Mike and Rachel, their best man and matron of honor, Emma argues that everyone has done bad things, prompting the group to confess their worst actions: Mike admits he used an ex-girlfriend as a human shield during a dog attack and Rachel confesses to locking her "slow" childhood neighbor in an abandoned trailer overnight. Charlie is pressured to share that he relentlessly cyberbullied a classmate who later moved away. Emma reveals she planned a school shooting as a teenager and that her deafness, which she claimed was congenital, was caused by firing a practice rifle close to her ear. The confession horrifies the group, especially Rachel, whose cousin Samantha was paralyzed in a shooting.

Charlie starts questioning how well he knows Emma. When pressed, Emma explains that she planned the shooting while depressed and bullied, and had been drawn to online communities focused on gun violence. She abandoned the plan after seeing how a mass shooting harmed her community and turned to gun control advocacy, finding friends and purpose among the activists. They awkwardly continue wedding preparations under growing strain. Emma begins having shooting-related nightmares, while Charlie grows paranoid about her mental state and fixates on violent imagery.

Rachel repeatedly ignores Emma, refusing to communicate regarding a project Emma's office hired her for. When Emma inadvertently suggests to her boss that Rachel be removed from the project, Rachel ends their friendship and refuses to attend the wedding. Charlie persuades her to reconsider, defending Emma in part by lying — claiming Emma witnessed a close friend's car crash as a child. He then awkwardly approaches Samantha, and assures her that she "would love Emma".

At work, Charlie asks his co-worker Misha how she would react if her boyfriend, Blake, planned a school shooting. When Misha says she would call the police, Charlie breaks down. As Misha attempts to comfort him, they kiss; she offers herself to him, but he stops before they have sex and they agree not to tell their partners about the incident. Later, Charlie and Emma have a tense meeting to fire Pauline, during which Charlie remains stressed by his encounter with Misha.

At the wedding reception, a drunken Rachel delivers a passive-aggressive speech, deriding Emma for dishonesty and Charlie for marrying her, heightening Emma's anxiety. In the bathroom, Emma overhears Misha mentioning someone planning a school shooting. Misinterpreting this as gossip about her, Emma confronts Misha; Misha, assuming Emma is referring to her sexual encounter with Charlie, blames Charlie for kissing her. Charlie gives a disastrous speech, apologizing for cheating and assuring guests Emma "didn't do anything". Misha lies and tells Blake that Charlie sexually harassed her. Blake attacks Charlie, and Emma leaves.

A bloodied Charlie frantically searches for Emma; he eventually travels to their favorite diner, where Emma had previously suggested they go after the wedding. Emma soon arrives, and they reintroduce themselves as if meeting for the first time, smiling tearfully at one another.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1989, 40-year old actor Ian Charleson juggles film roles and his reputation for starring in Chariots of Fire while privately battling AIDS, which has begun to show on his body through Kaposi's sarcoma lesions. When Daniel Day-Lewis suddenly storms off the stage during a performance of Hamlet at the National Theatre, director Richard Eyre reaches out to Ian about replacing him. Having long felt dissatisfied with his previous attempt at playing Hamlet, Ian sees this as his second and last chance to do his dream role justice. He accepts the part but discloses his condition to Richard, who reluctantly agrees to keep his secret despite his own concerns for Ian's well-being.

On the advice of a friend, Charleson seeks treatment from Margaret Johnson at the Royal Free Hospital's AIDS ward. Johnson strongly advises against performing the strenuous role of Hamlet, but Charleson persuades her that he will continue treatment while performing. He divides his time between appointments at the hospital and rehearsals for Hamlet at the National, with friends Patsy Pollock and Sean Mathias coming to support and care for him. Ian spars with his friend Derek Jarman, who feels Ian has turned his back on the gay community by hiding his condition, while Ian argues he does not want to be defined in public by his sexuality or illness.

The physical demands of the role combined with the illness take its toll, and Ian is further devastated when his friend and former lover Georgie dies. Eventually, Ian is hospitalized with pneumonia on the eve of the first preview. Richard promises the role is open for him when he recovers, but Johnson forbids him from returning to the stage. Ian meets with his parents and apologizes for not disclosing his sexuality or illness to them.

While recuperating in the AIDS ward, Ian bonds with fellow patients, including Nicholas, an admirer of his and an aspiring actor whose career has been stalled by his illness. Ian organizes a ballroom performance to give Nicholas and the other patients a chance to perform and cheer up the others, which Johnson enjoys. Ian's health stabilizes, but he insists to Johnson that while he could maintain his health for a few more years, he would rather risk dying while playing Hamlet than continue fighting a losing battle with his illness.

Ian reconciles with Derek, pledging to have his sexuality and illness announced to the public upon his death. With Johnson's approval, Ian returns to the National and discloses his illness to the rest of the cast and crew, who are supportive and help assist him backstage so he can power through performances. The production opens to rave reviews. While being comforted by Patsy, Ian is asked to think of a place that makes him happy: he pictures his time rehearsing and performing in Hamlet, as well as the love shown to him by family, friends, and castmates.

A postscript explains Ian made it through 24 performances of his run of Hamlet, passing away seven weeks later. It also reveals Margaret Johnson's AIDS clinic at the Royal Free Hospital vastly improved the quality of life for thousands of AIDS patients, and was renamed in 1992 to the "Ian Charleson Day Centre."

Everest: The Other Side begins with a look into Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson's relationship as they plan to climb and ski down the North Face of Mount Everest. Filming took place over 5 years. In September 2022, Nelson is killed by an avalanche on Manaslu with Morrison and the film crew present. The documentary then shifts to cover Morrison's reaction to his partner's death and his ultimate decision to pursue summiting and skiing Everest's North Face.

Morrison and a team of sherpas, along with the co-director Jimmy Chin, attempt to summit the North Face in 2024. After one of the sherpas, Yukta Gurung, breaks his leg, along with a heavy monsoon season, the team decides to turn back. In 2025, Morrison returns again with the same group. This expedition is successful, and Morrison spreads Nelson's ashes at the top of Everest. 

The names of those who completed the 2025 climb, in addition to Morrison and Chin, are: Carla Perez, Esteban Mena Yanez, Pasang Sona Sherpa, Pemba Sherpa, Roberto Morales, Erich Reopke, Nigma Tenjing Sherpa, Pemba Gelje Sherpa, Pur Bahadur "Yukta" Gurung, and Tenging Gyaljen Sherpa.

wiki_plot.text:
In summer 1949, Klaus Mann calls his sister Erika from an apartment in Cannes, where he shares his dissatisfaction with his writing and contemporary art as a whole. Erika invites him to join her and their father, Thomas Mann, a famed German writer in exile, on a trip to Frankfurt, where Thomas will give a speech and receive a Goethe Prize. Klaus promises to think about it.

Arriving in West Germany, Erika intercepts anonymous letters accusing Thomas of being a traitor to his fatherland. At a press gallery session, with Erika serving as Thomas's translator, it is revealed that he will receive a second Goethe Prize in Weimar. Journalists argue that Thomas will likely be persecuted upon his return to the United States, where he has been living for the past ten years, should he visit East Germany. Thomas replies that Goethe's work and German literature predates the country's separation, and that art does not recognize borders.

At a reception following the ceremony, Thomas is met by two grandsons of Richard Wagner, who ask if he can help rehabilitate the image of the Bayreuth Festival, which he refuses. At the reception's bar, Erika encounters her ex-husband Gustaf Gründgens, a German actor and General Director who became closely affiliated with Hermann Göring, the second most powerful man in Nazi Germany. The two have a brief altercation that ends with Erika slapping him in front of other patrons. Returning to her father's hotel room, she discovers that her brother Klaus has committed suicide. Nevertheless, Thomas insists on continuing the journey as planned.

Arriving in Weimar, the two receive a welcome procession by Johannes R. Becher, a high-ranking cultural official, and Sergei Tiulpanov, director of the Propaganda Administration of the Soviet Military Administration in Germany (SMAD). They have put together a packed programme featuring several banquets, all accompanied by music, including a children's choir singing Becher's "Auferstanden aus Ruinen" ("Risen from Ruins"), conceived as a pan-German national anthem with the repeated line "Deutschland…Vaterland (Germany…Fatherland)". At their hotel room, a dissident begs Thomas to publicly condemn the SMAD for detaining political prisoners at the former Buchenwald concentration camp, only for the man to be taken away by two SMAD representatives. Erika explores the grounds surrounding their accommodation on her own, leaving Thomas to attend several events by himself. Thomas returns to the hotel to find Erika crying and mourning Klaus.

The next day, on their way back to Frankfurt, Erika and Thomas drive past a bombed-out church, which they decide to investigate on their own. Walking into the ruins, they find two men tuning an organ. As they listen to them perform Bach's "Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring", Thomas begins to weep while Erika holds his hand.

wiki_plot.text:
The film opens in a drought-stricken district of Metro Manila, where a country club's service van carrying Chinese guests nearly collides with a crowd of residents queuing for rationed water.

Seventeen-year-old Isabel works as a "tee-girl" at the country club's exclusive, heavily irrigated golf course. She and her fellow tee-girls, all young women in pastel-blue uniforms, are tasked with setting golf balls on the tee for their wealthy patrons so the golfers need not bend down themselves. Alongside them are the caddies, women in pink uniforms and salakot-like hats who retrieve stray balls, including from the course's retention pond. While their supervisor and the golfers enjoy air-conditioned comfort, the tee-girls sleep cramped together despite the hot weather with only electric fans and meager food rations.

A newbie in the job, Isabel is soon assigned to the country club's president, Dr. Palanca. Discovering they share Ilocano roots, Palanca speaks to Isabel in Ilocano and offers his help should she need it, sparking in her an inexplicable fascination with him. Meanwhile, Clara, recently returned from studying in New York, is brought to the club by her uncle, who hopes she will join his golf equipment business and help curb the "brain drain." Disturbed by the subservient treatment of the caddies, Clara is hesitant to accept her uncle's offer.

Isabel is warned by Dr. Palanca's caddie, whom she had also seen earlier asleep with Palanca, that the country club is not safe and that Palanca is not as kind as he seems. Isabel is given a golf club Palanca accidentally left behind and sets out to return it. She wanders through the complex, encountering his dismissive wife, a nanny searching for a missing girl (marked by a dragonfly hairpin), and a fellow tee-girl who catches her touching food left by the guests. Sneaking into a bathing area, she overhears Palanca and Clara's uncle patronizingly discussing his family's land holdings in Ilocos, nearly taken under the 1988 agrarian reform program.

Isabel eventually locates a sleeping Dr. Palanca in his office. She watches through the window as workers fell a pine tree and load it onto a truck bearing Palanca's face—the same kind of truck, she recalls, that was once used to violently evict her own family from their land to make way for development. Realizing Palanca's family was responsible, she raises his golf club as if to strike the sleeping man but ultimately stops herself. Outside, Clara goes into a thicket to retrieve a misfired golf ball to avoid ordering her caddie around. There, she finds the dragonfly hairpin, the missing girl's corpse, and a bloodied golf ball (implied to be the one she was seeking). Clara's uncle callously orders a caddie to help him dump the child's cadaver into the retention pond and drives a shaken Clara away.

Wandering the grounds, Isabel reaches the pond and discovers the discarded body. Her cries for help go unanswered, and as the end credits begin, she wades into the water in an apparent attempt to recover the child, while golfers continue their game in the foreground and the truck hauling the felled pine passes in the background. She does not resurface before the film cuts to black.

wiki_plot.text:
Romanian engineer Mihai Gheorghiu and his Norwegian wife Lisbet, a nursing home worker, are devout evangelical Christians who have recently moved with their five children from Romania to Norway to be closer to Lisbet's family after the death of Mihai's parents. Their next door neighbours are Mats Halberg, the local school headmaster; his wife Mia, an attorney; Noora, Mats' daughter from a previous marriage; and Åke, Mats' widowed and disabled father.

The Gheorghius' oldest children, Elia and Emmanuel, become friends with Noora and proselytize to her, with Elia at one point seemingly walking on water; Elia and Noora's closeness inspires jealousy in Noora's friend Elsa. Frida, a teacher at their school who also works with Child Welfare Services, notices bruises on Elia's body during physical education class, and, suspecting child abuse, reports the Gheorghiu family to Child Services. Mihai admits to police that he spanks the children but he and Lisbet deny having abused their children. Child Services, acting on Mihai's admissions and testimony from Elia and Emmanuel, remove them from their home and put them in foster homes pending an investigation, and a parallel criminal investigation is opened.

The Gheorghius suspect religious discrimination and hire an attorney recommended by their church, but she drops their case after the first meeting with Child Services, finding Mihai too difficult to work with. Lisbet asks Mia to represent them. Mia asks Frida about her report, and comes to believe that there may have been a miscommunication between Frida and the children due to the language barrier. Frida also says that she made an earlier report to Child Services after Judith, the Gheorghius' youngest daughter, told a lesbian classmate that her sexual orientation was contrary to God's will. Mia agrees to represent the Gheorghius.

Frustrated with delays from Child Services, Mihai reaches out to the Romanian embassy and conservative Christian groups, leading to an international campaign to reunite the Gheorghius with their children. Noora sneaks Elia a cell phone, and secretly visits her and Emmanuel at their foster home.

At the final Child Services hearing, Mia attempts to establish doubt as to whether Elia's bruising was caused by parental abuse, the children fighting amongst themselves, or wrestling in physical education class. The attorney for Child Services questions if Mihai believes that corporal punishment is an acceptable form of discipline because of his religiosity and his Romanian culture. The judicial panel decides to conditionally return the children to the Gheorghius, pending a ruling in their criminal trial.

Mia declines to represent the Gheorghius in their criminal trial. Mihai begins to suspect a romantic attraction between Elia and Noora, to his dismay. Fearing that they will be convicted and lose their children forever, the family flees to Denmark. Noora tracks Elia's phone and rushes after them to say goodbye, but arrives just after their ferry has departed. As Noora rushes after, she realizes she's walking on water.
