spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in the Philippines in the 90s. A young girl named Jo (Kailey Crawford) is new at her school. She is doing a family history project, but she is telling fantastical stories about the fabled “Forgotten Island”, Nakali. It is a magic place that her Lola Fatima (Dolly De Leon) told her about. The other kids make fun of her, especially a boy named Reynaldo. Jo responds by attacking Reynaldo and getting herself sent to the principal’s office. Jo meets another girl named Raissa (Kayla Teruel), who gets herself in trouble as well because she defended Jo’s claims about some of the creatures on Nakali, including the Dreaded Manananggal, a scary vampire demon who can split her body in half. From that moment on, Jo and Raissa become best friends.

Over the years, Raissa spends more time with Jo and Fatima, and Jo no longer feels alone. By the time they graduate high school, Jo and Raissa (now played by H.E.R. and Liza Soberano) are still close, but Lola Fatima passes away.

Jo plans to stay close to Raissa when she goes to college nearby, but Raissa announces to Jo that she is going to Caltech in America. Jo is bummed out but still tries to show support for her best friend. She shows up at a party thrown by Raissa’s parents while dressed in a chicken costume from her job. Raissa’s mom embarrasses her with a slideshow of old kiddie pics, but Jo distracts everyone by dancing to “Baby Got Back”…and accidentally setting the lechon on fire. Raissa laughs but everyone else is unamused. Jo later overhears Raissa’s mom telling her how Jo is basically weighing Raissa down.

Jo sneaks Raissa out of the house so that they can have one last hangout by the beach on a van that they accidentally stranded there as kids. They dance and eat their favorite spicy snacks until Raissa has to be real with Jo about them having to go their separate ways. Suddenly, a sand dollar washes up on the shore, something that Lola had always mentioned regarding Nakali. A portal opens up in the sand, which Jo and Raissa know where it leads. Raissa takes Jo’s hand, and they both jump in.

The ladies find themselves in Nakali, but over 12 hours have passed. Half of Raissa’s hair is gone, and a pair of sentient wings are now stuck to her back. Jo is also missing the sand dollar that could get them home. They find a weredog (half-human/half-dog) named Raww (Dave Franco), who is taped to the tree. He claims that he was with them the night before when they ended up in Nakali. The three then have to hide when Manang (Lea Salonga), the Manananggal, is stalking the area, ready to kill whoever took her wings, but they are able to avoid her.

Raww leads Jo and Raissa to a cat creature named Batiba (Jenny Slate), who collects memories from humans who come upon Nakali in order to send them home. She had taken the ladies’ camera with memories from the night before, confirming they were with Raww. Batiba requests Jo and Raissa’s charm bracelets that are tied to memories of their friendship, but they would have to give up every charm and lose each memory in order to get back. The ladies refuse and try to find the sand dollar to get back instead.

Raww brings the ladies to a market that they were at the night before. He ends up going “full dog” because he comes across a stick and cannot think straight. They talk to a demon baby named Bungi (Manny Jacinto), who has a picture document of the night before. Jo had tried some super spicy food, causing her to breathe (and fart) fire, which explains how Raissa’s hair got burnt off. Jo had also breathed fire on the Duwende, noble warriors who Lola had always warned Jo and Raissa to never disrespect…but Jo breathed fire on the king’s butt.

Bungi joins Jo, Raissa, and Raww to meet the Duwende and their king, Truffle Wuffle (Ronny Chieng). They supposedly have the sand dollar since they took something because of the disrespect they endured. Raissa tries to talk to them properly, but Jo cannot help but call them cute and hug Truffle Wuffle. This leads to the Duwende chasing them off, but they end up getting the Duwende’s chest that they think contains the sand dollar. It actually has a shriveled old merman, who turns handsome when hydrated. He is Prince Mermahn (Kevin McCann), who claims that he knows that the sand dollar is at his kingdom.

The group (calling themselves “The Wild Pack”) ride a large red bird, a Sarimanok, toward their destination. Raww starts to regain sentience, and he suggests that Mermahn can’t be trusted. He also seemingly gives Bungi pink eye because he rubbed his tattooed stomach (which is clearly infected) on his face. The others chastise Raww for his behavior.

The group then meets the Katre, a tribe of tree people led by Datu (Jo Koy). They remembered Jo and Raissa for introducing them to human culture, such as karaoke, so they had a big party from the night before. Meanwhile, Jo and Raww bond over being loners. Manang tracks them down and is angry upon seeing Raissa with her wings. Before she can attack, they are saved by Raww, Bungi, Mermahn, and the Sarimanok. A chase ensues, where Bungi gets separated from the group, and Mermahn gets hit with a truth potion the group acquired in the market. The Duwende ride in for another attack, but they are able to get them to collide with Manang to get everyone off their trail.

Mermahn admits that he never knew where the sand dollar was, and he just lied to Jo and Raissa because they were indifferent to his looks and charms the night before. It is also revealed that Raww was working with Batiba to get Jo and Raissa’s memories, since she is a memory demon who takes valued memories from other since she is too scared to make her own, and she has even stolen from Manang. Jo and Raissa go back to Batiba’s cave together, where they see in Batiba’s eyes that Jo hid the sand dollar specifically so that they couldn’t leave since she is still upset over Raissa leaving. Raissa goes to look for the sand dollar and tells Jo that she never wants to see her again when they return home.

Raissa flies to Manang’s domain. She locates the sand dollar where Jo hid it, but Manang tries to attack Raissa. She tells Manang that it was Batiba who stole from her, which only enrages Manang and draws her anger towards Batiba. She gets her wings back and flies toward the cave.

Raissa makes it back to the cave with the sand dollar. When she tries to get Jo to go back with her, Jo says she can’t, because she made a deal with Batiba for Raissa to go back, on the condition that Jo give up all her memories of their friendship. Raissa tries to stop them, but Batiba pushes her back through the portal. Raissa ends up back on the beach, with her plane to California flying overhead. Raissa feels defeated and like she just betrayed her best friend, but her charm bracelet starts to glow, and a portal to Nakali re-opens.

Raissa returns to Nakali and frees Raww to help get back to Batiba’s cave. Raww gets Bungi and Mermahn to help fight back against Manang, who is trying to break into the cave. Raissa gets inside and gets under Batiba’s paws so she can get into Jo’s memories. Nearly all of them are gone until they reach the moment that the girls first met. Raissa talks to young Jo and promises not to forget her. Jo’s adult self responds to Raissa, and she is able to keep her memories. The strength of Jo and Raissa’s friendship had enough magic to prevent them from being forgotten, as well as to get them home. Manang breaks into the cave, but Batiba agrees to give back what she stole from her.

Manang exits Batiba’s cave, now with her memory restored so she can be at peace again. She turns around so her wings can wave goodbye to Raissa before she leaves. The Duwende try for one last attack in a Trojan Horse-like chicken thing, but the Sarimanok knocks them off a hill, sending them crashing. The ladies encourage Batiba to leave her cave and make her own memories, and they bid their friends farewell before returning home.

A few years later, Raissa attends an event at Caltech for Jo’s new comic book based off their adventures in Nakali, where she has made Raissa the heroine, albeit in a love triangle with Raww and Mermahn (which she’s not too thrilled about). Jo is set to go home the next day, but the ladies use their bracelets to take a quick trip back to Nakali. A portal opens up in the school, and they jump in.

wiki_plot.text:
In the Philippines during the 1990s, Jo Yuson presents a story to her class about the island of Nakali (short for "nakalimutan", meaning "forgotten" in Tagalog) and the dreaded manananggal. When a classmate mocks her, Jo attacks him and is sent to the principal's office, where she meets Raissa Molina, another classmate who had defended her. Jo later invites Raissa to a sleepover with her grandmother, Fatima, who tells them about her travels to Nakali. The girls become best friends, making matching charm bracelets that represent significant moments in their friendship. Fatima later passes away from old age, leaving Jo orphaned and heartbroken.

After graduating high school, Raissa reveals that she is attending Caltech in the United States at the wishes of her parents, disappointing Jo, who is trying to make ends meet by working at a fast food restaurant. At the farewell party, Jo overhears Raissa's mother expressing disapproval over their friendship. Jo and Raissa sneak out to the beach, where Jo discovers a magical sand dollar that serves as a portal to Nakali. Despite Raissa's hesitation, they enter together, awakening the next morning with no memory of the previous night. Raissa discovers that half of her head has been shaved and she has grown wings belonging to Manang, a manananggal who attacks them. They escape with help from Batiba, a batibat who offers to send them home in exchange for their bracelets and the memories attached to them, as she perpetually stays in her cave and lives vicariously through the memories of others due to her agoraphobia. The girls refuse and flee with Raww, a were-aspin who claims to have hung out with them the previous night and becomes their guide.

At a market, the trio meet Bungi, a tiyanak who tells them that the "Jewel of the Sea" they seek was stolen by a duwende king. It is then revealed that Jo accidentally burned the chunk of Raissa’s hair the night prior. Their search leads them to Mermahn, a kataw who claims the sand dollar is in his kingdom. Feeling excluded, Raww lashes out until Jo reassures him and shares her fear of being abandoned by Raissa. Following Raww's suggestion, Jo takes them to Kapre Village, where they learn that they had previously saved the villagers from Manang, after which Raissa stole her wings. Manang attacks again, separating Bungi from the group. After escaping, the group learns that Mermahn lied about the sand dollar, while Raww reveals that he works for Batiba, who is actually a demon. He also admits that he had lured Jo and Raissa to Batiba the previous night, after which they relinquished their memories of their time in Nakali.

Batiba recaptures them and restores their memories, revealing that Jo, afraid of losing Raissa, had hidden the sand dollar after Batiba gave it to them to prevent them from being able to return home. Furious, Raissa reveals that going to Caltech was her choice and heads to find the sand dollar, ending their friendship. When she finds it, she is ambushed by Manang, who reclaims her wings, but finds out from Raissa that Batiba has stolen from her. Jo then reveals that she offered Batiba her memories of their friendship in exchange for saving her. Raissa is sent back to the Philippines, while Jo stays behind. Back on the beach, a remorseful Raissa adds a leftover firecracker to her bracelet, sending her back to Nakali. Reconciling with Raww, she enters Jo's fading memories and tearfully admits how much their friendship shaped who she is, reconciling with her. Manang arrives, and Jo and Raissa, aided by Raww, Bungi, and Mermahn, attempt to fight her, but Batiba, finally understanding the value of memories, willingly returns the ones she stole from Manang, causing her to become docile. Jo finally accepts Raissa's decision to attend college overseas, and the girls head home while Batiba finally goes outside.

A few years later, Jo visits Raissa at Caltech to promote a graphic novel she has published based on their adventures. Before Jo heads home, she and Raissa use their bracelets to reopen the portal so they can visit Nakali once more.

spoiler_text.text:
The film starts in the city of Vineland, a sprawling community of anthropomorphic animals. A young goat named Will Harris (Luke Cimity) is taken to a game of Roarball by his mother Louise (Jennifer Hudson). Will is excited to watch his favorite team, the Vineland Thorns, playing the game. When he sees his favorite player, superstar black panther Jett Fillmore (Gabrielle Union), Will tells Louise that one day, he is going to be just like Jett.

Ten years later, Will (now voiced by Caleb McLaughlin) lives alone after Louise’s death. He struggles to come up with rent money for his landlord Frank (Wayne Knight). His best friends are a capybara named Daryl (Eduardo Franco) and an aardwolf named Hannah (Sherry Cola). Will works as a busboy at the diner where Louise used to work, taken care of by manager Carol (Ayesha Curry), and he uses his horizontal goat eyes to help him see what others cannot.

The Thorns have had a bad luck streak with no wins. Jett is particularly frustrated since she hasn’t been at the top of her game like she used to. She complains to the Thorns’ boar manager Florence “Flo” Everson (Jenifer Lewis) about making some kind of change to get the Thorns back on top. Flo says she has an idea.

Will is given until the end of the day to come up with rent money. He goes to sell some old sneakers that belonged to Jett to a sneaker-selling vulture named Sneaky (Joe La Puma), but he only gets $250 for it. Will, Hannah, and Daryl find out that hotshot Roarball player Mane Attraction (Aaron Pierre), a horse with a huge ego who plays for the Lava Court Magmas, is challenging people to a game downtown. Will goes to the court and challenges Mane, even betting his money on the game. Mane laughs him off because Will is a “small”, and “smalls can’t ball”, but Will confidently dunks on Mane twice. Then Mane takes off his chains and quickly wipes the floor with Will, taking his money and humiliating him. As a result, Will has to crash with Hannah and Daryl.

The next day, Will goes to the diner, where everyone is stunned to see that Flo is there waiting for him. She saw his game against Mane, and even though he lost, Will has gone viral for the effort he put into it (and for breaking Mane’s ankles). Flo offers Will the chance to join the Thorns in the back half of their season to help them score a win. Will excitedly signs on, with his dreams starting to come true.

Jett learns that Will is the new player, and she is enraged to find out that a “small” is on the team. Will is disappointed to learn that his idol doesn’t want him on the team. He joins Jett for a press conference, where she mocks him in front of the reporters under the guise of defending him. Will later meets Coach Dennis Cooper (Patton Oswalt), a proboscis monkey, before meeting the rest of the team – distracted giraffe Lenny Williamson (Stephen Curry), struggling single rhino dad Archie Everhardt (David Harbour), anxious and phone-addicted ostrich Olivia Burke (Nicola Coughlan), and eccentric Komodo dragon Modo Olachenko (Nick Kroll).

During the first few games of the season, Jett forces Will to get benched, resulting in the Thorns continuing their losing streak. Mane even makes a diss track about Will that goes viral. Will even plays against Jett in a personal game to earn a chance to play, but she beats him. In the middle of another game, Jett has to sit the game out after a technical foul. Will gets put in and utilizes his small size to seize an advantage and help the Thorns win the game.

The Thorns are set to do a promotional video as a team, with Jett made to “pass the torch” to Will, but she refuses to do so, as she wants to be the “GOAT” forever. The rest of the players are scared to speak up to Jett until Will reminds her that they won their last game when she wasn’t even there.

Will later privately talks to Jett after he helps her escape obnoxious fans and reporters. She admits that she has been obsessed with winning ever since one of her last games, “The Furball Game”, which is called that because she feels she choked during that game. Will brings Jett to the diner, where they have a ton of Thorns memorabilia. He also tells Jett about how the community came together for him after Louise passed away. This inspires Jett to go on a live-stream with Mane, who is trash-talking the Thorns. Jett has something good to say about each individual teammate, which lifts their spirits. She also allows Dennis to take full control as coach, helping them start over as a team.

Dennis encourages the team to utilize their quirks into their playing. He tells Lenny to use his height to his advantage, tells Archie to pretend that the other players are like his daughters so that he can properly defend them, tells Olivia to take her focus off her phone and the internet, and tells Modo to do what he does best – being weird and shocking people. The Thorns experience a winning streak and this helps them grow closer as a team.

Right before a semi-final game, Will follows Jett to a meeting with Flo and overhears them discussing how Flo has sold the Thorns to another city, and that none of the current players will remain onboard. Will tries to get Jett to tell the team beforehand, but she thinks it will just break their focus. They start to lose against a team of arctic players on an ice court, forcing Will to tell the team about Flo’s deal. Jett then takes charge of the game and scores points, even stealing one of Will’s scores just to claim the winning point. This causes the team to split up out of disgust.

Will returns home and prepares to give up until Jett finds him on his court and apologizes to him for how she acted, admitting she was afraid of losing her status as the GOAT and that she was obsessed with winning The Claw, a Roarball trophy. Together, Will and Jett round up the rest of the team for their final game.

The Thorns face off against the Magmas on their court. In the middle of the game, Jett protects Will from an attack by Mane, which causes her to injure her leg. A fight breaks out, where Archie charges into Mane out of anger, forcing him to sit the rest of the game out. Jett convinces the others that she can still play the rest of the game. With just 20 seconds left on the clock in the fourth quarter, Dennis gives the team a specific play to go through. The Thorns put their best work in, and Jett’s leg becomes too hurt to continue. Will gets the ball and gets it through the hoop in the last second, allowing the Thorns to claim their victory. Everyone in Vineland cheers for Will and the Thorns, while Mane is humiliated when his hair gets burned off. Flo attempts to congratulate the team on a win, but Archie’s twin daughters (who have violent tendencies) proceed to chase Flo out of the arena.

The Thorns return to Vineland for a victory celebration, with Will giving a heartfelt speech now that Jett has finally acknowledged him as the GOAT. As they are starting to accept that the Thorns will be leaving Vineland, Modo comes out to reveal that he won the rights to the team and is now team manager, meaning they will stay in Vineland. The entire city cheers, and they join the Thorns in doing a victory bleating (“baaaa!”) for Will.

wiki_plot.text:
In a world of anthropomorphic animals, on his birthday, young goat Will Harris aspires to be like his idol, black panther Jett Fillmore, a roarball player for his homeland Vineland's Thorns.

Ten years later, the Thorns have not yet won all season, with Jett asking team owner, warthog Florence "Flo" Everson, to do whatever she can to complete and make the team by finding a sixth player. Meanwhile, a young adult Will, now working at a diner and practicing roarball, is struggling to pay his apartment rent to his landlord gerbil Frank. After earning money from selling his prized sneakers, Will faces off against an Andalusian horse named Mane Attraction, the lead player for the Lava Coast Magma, by betting the money. Though he has an early lead, Will loses, ends up evicted, and moves in with his friends capybara Daryl and aardwolf Hannah.

The next morning, a video of Will "breaking" Mane's ankles goes viral. At work, Will is signed onto the Thorns by Flo. When Jett finds out, she is enraged and mocks Will during a press conference. Will is introduced by proboscis monkey coach Dennis Cooper to the team: Indian rhinoceros Archie Everhardt, giraffe Lenny Williamson, Komodo dragon Modo Olachenko, and ostrich Olivia Burke. Will is placed on the bench for a few games, but when Jett has a technical foul, she is forced to sit out. Will is subbed in and scores a winning point, gaining the Thorns their first win and the respect of his other teammates. While filming a promotional video, Jett is angered and leaves the shoot, but Will comforts her, and takes her to the diner he used to work at. There, Jett sees that the city supports her, and Will reminds Jett of his mother Louise's ambitions for him to play roarball prior to her death. Carol, the owner of the diner, makes Jett promise to bring home the Claw, the roarball championship trophy, for Vineland. That night, Jett goes on a livestream with Mane and defends her team, allowing Dennis to coach them. After this, the Thorns go on a winning streak and make it to the playoffs.

At a party just before the semi-final, Flo tells Jett that she has sold the Thorns to Sunken City to make herself a profit, and that everyone will be cut off and Jett will never win the Claw. Will overhears this, but Jett forces him to keep quiet. The team starts off poorly, however, and in the final quarter, despite Jett's objections, Will tells them what he overheard. The team is upset and shocked, and Jett starts hogging the ball as they resume play. Although the Thorns win, they quit due to Jett's selfishness. Before the finals, Jett apologizes to Will for her actions and tearfully admits her fear of losing her legacy. With his help, the pair gets the team back together and they face off against the Magma at Lava Coast.

During the game, Mane causes Jett to get a possibly career-ending injury on her leg, and she is forced to walk on crutches. When she gets back out on the court, she is applauded and sits on the bench while watching the rest of the team play. During the final quarter, Archie gets an ejection after defending Will from Mane. Jett decides to step back in, and Dennis gives them a new play. Jett distracts the Magma and passes the ball to Will, who makes the winning shot. As they celebrate, Mane's hair gets burned away, while Flo is chased off the field by Archie's twin daughters, Adi and Ari.

Back in Vineland, the Thorns celebrate with the well earned Claw, where Modo reveals that he won ownership of the team in a game of Uno, much to everyone's surprise and allows the Thorns to stay in Vineland.

spoiler_text.text:
1949, Matsumoto City – Years after the destruction caused by Godzilla, the people of Japan are now running from a flying lightning-spewing monster called Ghidorah. Scientists, including Dr. Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka), Kanji Murakami (Min Tanaka), and meteorologist Makoto Aoyama (Masami Nagasawa), gather after acquiring footage of Ghidorah. It is shown that the beast was formed after a chrysalis from outer space absorbed and fused other animals together. The scientists work with the American military to drop a vacuum bomb on Ghidorah.

In the time since Godzilla’s attack, pilot Koichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki) has married Noriko (Minami Hamabe), and they have raised Akiko (Sae Nagatani) together as a family. Koichi meets with Noda, plus Shiro Mizushima (Yuki Yamada) and Tatsuo Hotta (Miou Tanaka), as they make plans to launch an attack on Ghidorah. Meanwhile, Murakami is shown working and researching recovered fragments of Godzilla’s body, but he also suffers from PTSD after finding the bodies of his family following the bombing of Hiroshima.

The team initiates their attack against Ghidorah. They drop the bomb over the creature and detonate it, but it doesn’t ignite until Koichi and two other pilots drop bombs to light Ghidorah up. This only enrages it and leads to Ghidorah blowing up one pilot mid-air, and then cutting the other one’s parachute after he ejects, leaving only Koichi to try to escape Ghidora’s wrath. The bomber jet drops a lightning rod harpoon on Ghidorah, causing it to get struck by lightning repeatedly and seemingly bringing it down.

However, Ghidorah suddenly mutates and grows two more heads, dorsal plates, and an extra tail, turning it into KING GHIDORAH! The evolved beast swoops down upon the nearby city and uses a gravity beam to lift entire buildings and people, dropping them down onto each other and causing an untold level of devastation.

Somewhere in Sagami Bay, a fishing boat experiences a tremor. Rising from the ocean, much larger and more terrifying before, is Godzilla itself, making its way back toward the mainland.

After their weapons and artillery fail, Murakami decides that the only way to combat Ghidorah is to get Godzilla to fight the three-headed beast in the ruins of Ginza. The plan is to try and lure Godzilla to that area using a resonance device that would attract it, as demonstrated when being used to attract all the crows in the area. Murakami shows Koichi research he’s done on people who were affected by Godzilla’s radiation in Ginza, and the only survivor was Noriko. Her eye has turned yellow, and she has spikes on her shoulders from the “Godzilla cells” in her.

It is shown that Murakami had planned to use this device to lure Godzilla to New York City as revenge for the destruction of his home and loss of his family, as shown in a maniacal vision Murakami has of the great lizard firing a plasma blast toward Manhattan and vaporizing nearly everybody. However, Noda later convinces Murakami to let go of his desire for vengeance.

As the team starts constructing a trap for Ghidorah, Koichi is set to get back in the air, but he is angry with Noda at the thought of using Noriko as part of the mission. When he brings this news to her, she agrees to join so that Akiko can have a future to look forward to. They bring the girl to their neighbor Sumiko (Sakura Ando), who now runs an orphanage. Although Akiko believes her parents will return safely, one of the other girls tries to discourage her since she and the other kids were basically abandoned.

The team waits in Ginza for Ghidorah to arrive as it follows a storm to that area. The beast swoops down as the men deploy balloons near some generators. Lightning strikes them, and the team intends to release liquid nitrogen to freeze Ghidorah in place before lighting it up. Meanwhile, Koichi flies in a plane with Noriko and Murakami, using Noriko’s G-cells and the Resonance Wave to lure Godzilla, leveling the playing field.

The monsters go at it. Ghidorah proves to be a challenge, with each of its heads chomping into Godzilla and dealing serious damage. Godzilla’s tail protrudes one of his dorsal plates, then swings its tail to decapitate one of Ghidorah’s heads. The head bites onto Godzilla’s arm, which it severs and regenerates quickly. The now two-headed kaiju continues to spew lightning at Godzilla, who misses Ghidorah with one of its plasma blasts. Ghidorah ends up using its gravity beam to drop a building on Godzilla and knock it out for now.

The fuel lines for the trap get cut, so Noda rushes in to activate it manually. As he tries to drive away, Ghidorah hits Noda’s car with a lightning blast. The others try to stop Koichi from firing the missile to ignite the fuel after Ghidorah is frozen by the liquid nitrogen, but it’s too late and Noda is killed in the blast. Aoyama informs Koichi but tells him it was Ghidorah’s fault to spare him the guilt.

Koichi then flies down towards Godzilla to use Noriko and the Resonance Wave once again, with Noriko utilizing her mutation to wake Big G up. Godzilla rises once more to finish things. Now that Ghidorah has G-cells as well, it is able to reattach the severed head before producing its own dorsal plates and heat breath. The two monsters load up their blasts, but Godzilla shoots first, causing Ghidorah’s heads to lose control and take the full atomic blast, blowing the beast to kingdom come. The U.S. military arrives and starts firing upon Godzilla until they are ordered to stand down so that Godzilla can be preserved for when it is needed again.

In the aftermath, the team returns home. Murakami arranges for Koichi and Noriko to get away safely, while he destroys his evidence and research of Godzilla. Although Murakami tries to get away, he is arrested by U.S. authorities.

Koichi fears that the U.S. will try to take Noriko and weaponize her G-cells for her own gain. They decide to go into hiding and return to the orphanage to tell Akiko that they are saying goodbye. The little girl wails and tells her parents “Have a safe trip” repeatedly so that they will eventually return. The pain of leaving her is too much for Koichi and Noriko to bear, so they bring Akiko with them and go on the run together.

The last we see is Godzilla swimming back underwater.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1949, two years after Godzilla's defeat and his remains sinking in Sagami Bay, Japan continues its recovery from the effects of the war and Godzilla's attacks. Former kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima has married Noriko Ōishi, a survivor of Godzilla's Ginza attack, who has begun to display physical mutations as a result of exposure to Godzilla's cells ("G-cells"). Their neighbor Sumiko Ōta, now operating an orphanage, helps them raise their adopted daughter Akiko. Kenji Noda, director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau, assembles a team including returning crew members Shirō Mizushima, Seiji Akitsu, and former destroyer captain Tatsuo Hotta to prepare for future threats.

Matsumoto is attacked by a dragon-like creature, which is capable of flight and firing electrical beams from its mouth. Scientists, including Hiroshima bombing survivor Kanji Murakami and his assistant Akira Hagiwara, document the attack and report their findings to Noda. The creature arrived in a meteorite as a gelatinous organism before consuming local wildlife and adopting its current form. Combining the words "chimera" and "hydra", they name it "Ghidorah". Meteorologist Makoto Aoyama tracks Ghidorah through weather patterns, as it seems to be attracted to lightning storms.

Kōichi volunteers to lead an attack against Ghidorah while it's dormant, with reluctant support from the United States. The plan involves dropping a new fuel-air bomb from a Nakajima G5N Shinzan bomber escorted by Douglas AD Skyraiders, but Ghidorah survives the explosion and kills the other escort pilots. The bomber deploys harpoons equipped with Narukami rods into Ghidorah's back, attracting a series of lightning strikes that seemingly kill it. However, Ghidorah revives and evolves into a larger, three-headed, double-tailed monster. Now called "King Ghidorah", it gains the ability to lift and smash buildings with a "gravity beam", and continues attacking cities across Japan, killing thousands.

As Ghidorah continues its rampage, Godzilla completes his regeneration and resurfaces near Kōzu-shima. Murakami argues that forcing the monsters to fight each other is the only way to defeat them, regarding Godzilla's return as "divine providence". However, Murakami secretly plots to have Godzilla destroy New York City to avenge his family, who died in the Hiroshima bombing, by using a device called the Resonance Wave Amplifier. As Murakami's plan requires Noriko to operate the amplifier due to her connection to Godzilla, Kōichi flees with his family to prevent Noriko from being used as a weapon. However, after they pass through the devastated Matsumoto, Noriko chooses to volunteer for the plan. Noda persuades Murakami to abandon his vengeance.

The bureau determines the ruins of Ginza to be the ideal battleground. They build generators and traps to entice and occupy Ghidorah, while Kōichi pilots Murakami's Kawanishi H8K seaplane to lure Godzilla with Noriko and the amplifier on board. In the ensuing clash, Godzilla uses his tail to sever one of Ghidorah's heads, but the severed head bites Godzilla's arm, forcing Godzilla to tear off his own arm to free himself. Godzilla's arm regenerates, but Ghidorah ultimately incapacitates him, burying him beneath rubble. The bureau manages to freeze Ghidorah with liquid nitrogen, before covering it with fuel to create a deadly temperature fluctuation. When the trap's fuel lines are severed, Noda activates it manually. As he drives away, Ghidorah strikes his vehicle with a beam, causing it to crash. Kōichi fires a rocket from his aircraft into Ghidorah to ignite the fuel, inadvertently killing Noda; to spare Kōichi further guilt, Aoyama instead tells him Noda was killed by Ghidorah. Kōichi and Noriko use the amplifier to resuscitate Godzilla, while Ghidorah reattaches its severed head, which has absorbed some G-cells, and develops dorsal spines and a heat ray. The monsters unleash their energy beams, but Godzilla's beam hits Ghidorah first, and Ghidorah is killed.

After Godzilla's victory, the U.S. military commences bombarding him, but receives orders to preserve him for potential future use as a weapon. They cease fire, and Godzilla returns to the ocean. Fearing the military's intentions, Murakami burns his research notes and destroys the amplifier. He attempts to flee with Hagiwara, but they are apprehended by American soldiers and arrested for "possessing classified information". Kōichi, realizing that the military could also exploit Noriko's G-cells, goes into hiding with her, and they plan to leave Akiko behind for her own safety. However, after saying goodbye to her, they decide to take her with them and go on the run together.

spoiler_text.text:
* The film is preceded by a short starring Lilo and Stitch
LILO AND SCRATCH
Stitch (Chris Williams) is enjoying an afternoon with Pudge the fish (the one who “controls the weather”) when Lilo (Maia Kealoha) brings in a pink cat-like creature that she named Scratch. When Lilo leaves for a moment, Scratch attempts to eat Pudge, so Stitch eats her first. Lilo pulls Scratch out of Stitch’s mouth and goes to get a cake for her new pet. Stitch and Scratch then proceed to fight each other after it’s revealed Scratch is also an alien. They cause chaos around the neighborhood, including running into Lilo’s bully Mertle and her cronies. Eventually, Scratch accidentally drops herself into the ocean. Stitch has a change of heart and saves Scratch from drowning. The two return home as buddies, and Lilo brings Scratch a cake. When Lilo leaves again, the two aliens find a briefcase and open it. It plays a hologram of Jumba (Piotr Michael), who created Scratch (Experiment 818), and the briefcase has a button that would send Scratch back to her alien planet. Stitch presses the button but Scratch destroys the briefcase.

The short is dedicated to Daveigh Chase, the original voice of Lilo.

HEXED
The film opens with a narration from teenager Billie Doe (Hailee Steinfeld), who tells of a magical realm inhabited by witches and wizards. Before the realm could properly exist in harmony, things descended into chaos. Only the Chosen Witch can perform the Moon Spell that will bring balance to the realm once more.

Years earlier, we see a baby Billie with her single mother Alice (Rashida Jones). After putting Billie to bed in her crib, Alice leaves the room. Billie is still awake and motions toward the window, causing sparks from her hands to push the window open. A portal then opens in her room, and two ravens fly out to try and take Billie. Alice hears the commotion and rushes upstairs to protect her daughter. Billie inadvertently blows up one of the ravens, causing the other one to retreat back through the portal. Alice puts a gemstone around Billie’s wrist to suppress her magic, and she packs up and flees the house with Billie, moving to Ohio.

In the present day, Billie is an unpopular and troublemaking teen. She sneaks into her school to steal the class pet owl and set it free. Alice, who has raised her daughter strictly, finds out Billie stole her car and demands she return home. When she does, Alice scolds her, but Billie expresses a desire to feel like she belongs somewhere.

The next day, Principal Huggins (Brett Gelman) brings Billie into his office because he has security footage of her stealing the owl. To make things worse, the owl flew into electrical wires and died. Huggins threatens Billie with expulsion and to show everyone the video of her. She swipes his laptop and runs to the bathroom to try and delete the video. Billie accidentally breaks off her gemstone, which causes her magic to come back. She cannot control it and causes a mess in the bathroom, and Huggins gets hit with all of it. Billie is expelled, and Alice angrily picks her up.

After an argument, Billie goes to her room. She tests out her magic again and opens the portal to the other realm. Alice goes to try and talk to her but sees Billie get sucked through the portal. Billie ends up in Hexe, the magical realm. She meets a talking book named Elias Quire (Stephen Fry) and his quill companion Ms. Quill (Tracey Ullman). After learning of Billie’s feelings of being an outcast, the two grant her access into Hexe.

Billie is amazed at seeing other witches and wizards, though she freaks some people out with how excited she is. However, Billie draws attention to herself when she starts flying, something she does unintentionally. Constable Beans (Samson Kayo) and his partner try to arrest Billie, but she is saved by Alice and a sentient cauldron that Billie names “Bucket”. They escape the authorities, but as Alice reveals that she is also a witch, she tells Billie that the ruler of Hexe, Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster), is Alice’s mother and supposedly the only witch known up until now who could fly. Alice is captured by Celeste’s minions, Morphlings (half human/half ravens), and her overly loyal Grand Councillor Hieronymous (Dan Stevens) but she leaves Billie with Bucket to find an old friend of Alice.

Alice is brought back to Celeste’s castle and put back in her old room. Although Celeste seems happy to see her daughter again, Alice wants to get Billie to go back home. Celeste responds by locking Alice in the tower.

Billie and Bucket walk through a swamp and encounter a multi-eyed monster that chases them until they make it to the other side. They come across a trailer belonging to a three-eyed cat named Beef Roger Crummchuk (Walton Goggins). He was Alice’s former familiar/best friend, but after she left, he became bitter and remained in the swamp. Although Beef initially refuses to help Billie, she is able to convince him to join her in getting her mom back, as well as to find someone who can help Billie perform the Moon Spell when the Haven Moon rises, as Celeste wants to do the spell to prove she’s the Chosen Witch. Beef takes Billie to find the Descendants of the First Witch of Hexe.

On the way, Billie continues to try and test her magic, but it doesn’t work so well. Alice escapes from her tower and manages to track down Billie and Beef. Alice wants to get a portal to go back home. Beef brings the mother and daughter to a village inhabited by familiars. He disguises Billie as a possum and Alice as a piglet (to her annoyance). They sneak into a pub to find an owl named Nigel (Henry Winkler), who carries a stone that opens the portal to worlds outside of Hexe. Billie tries to get Nigel, but another argument with Alice leads to their disguises wearing off. Beef holds off the nasty familiars so they can escape with Nigel.

Celeste tracks down Billie and Alice, and it is revealed that Celeste placed a curse on Alice’s body that suppresses her magic. Seeing that the curse is causing her mother pain, Billie uses her magic to push Celeste back so she can escape with Alice, Beef, and Nigel. Everyone returns to Beef’s trailer so he can undo Alice’s curse.

During the ritual, Billie enters Alice’s mind and sees memories of how Alice was always protecting her. Billie then sees Alice as a child and how Celeste placed the curse on her to try and keep her from outshining her, since Celeste saw early on how Alice could also fly. Billie talks to Alice’s child self and comforts her, allowing her to remove the curse from Alice’s body.

As the Haven Moon is set to rise, Celeste makes another attempt to go after her daughter and granddaughter. It seems as though she used the Morphlings to abduct Alice, so Billie goes after her. It was merely a ruse with Celeste disguised as Alice so that she can place a new curse on Billie. Alice and Beef show up, but Celeste rebounds one of Beef’s spells back at him, killing him. Alice gets Billie out and Nigel gives them the portal to return home.

Alice brings Billie back outside their house, but Billie is unconscious. Alice goes into her mind to reaffirm her love for her daughter, allowing them to remove the curse. They are seen by Huggins, who is now terrified of the Does.

Celeste prepares to perform the Moon Spell in the town square, but by now, everyone sees how cruel and corrupt she is. Billie and Alice use the portal to drive their car back to Hexe and interrupt the ceremony. Beef also comes back to life (although he’s now on his ninth life) and brings the familiars with him (Bucket is also there). The final showdown begins as Billie and Alice battle Celeste and the Morphlings, but Celeste absorbs one of their powers to become half raven. Billie tries to perform the Moon Spell, but it’s not working. That’s because the real Chosen Witch was Alice all along. After holding Celeste back, Alice performs the Moon Spell, which empowers the other witches and wizards and finally brings balance to Hexe.

Celeste is locked up in the tower, with only Hieronymous there to keep her (unwanted) company. Billie and Alice have decided to remain in Hexe as Princess and Queen. As everyone celebrates their new reign, Billie and Alice go flying together to find other magic folks with their powers.

During the credits , Billie and Alice return to the human world with Beef and Bucket to replace Beef’s figurines that Billie broke. They freak out the human clerk as he witnesses them doing magic.

wiki_plot.text: After being expelled from school, an impulsive and unconventional teen girl named Billie discovers magical abilities that take her from suburbia into Hexe, a realm of witches. With her cautious mother Alice catching up to her, she investigates family secrets connected to the world of witches.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens with a young Mabel (Piper Curda) attempting to free several classroom animals by smuggling them all in her backpack. She is caught, and during the commotion, a fire alarm is set off and is in trouble.

Mabel is dropped off by her parents to her grandmother (Karen Huie)’s house. While at first Mabel is silent and angry, her grandmother convinces her to go with her to a local forest glade, sit on a rock, and be still. Animals then come out and Mabel is inspired by nature.

Over the years, Mabel continues to spend time with her grandmother and helps as many animals as they can find. Instead of going to college, Mabel opts to stay behind at a local college to be with her grandmother. This continues until her grandmother gets sick and eventually passes away, with her grandmother giving her her jacket during one of their final walks.

Mabel now lives alone in her grandmother’s house and is fighting for the glade. Mayor Jerry Generazzo (Jon Hamm) claims all the animals have left, and it’s time to build a freeway and destroy the glade. Mabel and Mayor Jerry are constantly at odds, with Mayor Jerry running for re-election and Mabel objecting to all of his developments. Mabel protests the freeway by standing on the dam where dynamite has been put into place, and the Mayor gives her 48 hours to get signatures. After an entire day of rejection, Mabel campaigns to an old man by helping him out and talking about her advocacy, only to find out that he had his hearing aid out and wrote a grocery list instead of his signature on her petition.

Mabel runs back to Beaverton University and interrupts her professor Dr. Sam (Kathy Najimy) in the middle of class to talk about protecting the glade. Mabel remembers the dam and is convinced she needs to find a beaver to convince the community to return to the glade.

After a full night of waiting, a beaver arrives. Mabel follows the beaver which is then taken in a van. She chases and tracks the beaver down and ends up back in a secret lab at the university, where she sees the beaver using a card key to enter. Mabel is caught… and the researchers at the lab are Dr. Sam and her colleagues. The beaver is a robot developed after many years of research, and Dr. Sam has made multiple other robotic animals under the Hoppers program. The Hoppers program enables humans to enter the consciousness of a robotic animal to communicate and get up close with their respective species.

Mabel quickly sees this as an opportunity to save the glade, so she hops into the beaver from earlier against Dr. Sam’s wishes and flees from the lab. An owl then snatches her up and drops her deep into the glade.

Mabel awakens and is amazed by being able to understand all the animals. She finds a lazy beaver named Loaf (Eduardo Franco) and saves him from a bear named Ellen (Melissa Villaseñor), only to find out that she was allowed to eat him under “pond rules”. Mabel is then taken by the animals to meet King George (Bobby Moynihan), the “King of the Mammals” who moved all the animals into a big community “super lodge”. Mabel learns about “pond rules” and how the community all live and work together. During this, Conner (Sam Richardson), one of Dr. Sam’s colleagues, hops into a robotic bird to observe Mabel.

After Mabel tries to tell George about the glade, she soon realizes that the reason the animals left was Mayor Jerry erecting false trees that emit noise only animals can hear to keep them out. When Mabel tries to destroy the tree, Conner tries to get her and bring her back to the lab to prevent interfering with nature. He fails and Mabel successfully destroys the tree, convincing all the animals to return. The animals then come back and rebuild the dam and inhabit the glade.

Mabel bonds with George as they talk about their lives, and she finds out George only became King because of his father casting him out. George then asks Mabel to become the “Paw of the King” and be his personal advisor.

Mayor Jerry is shocked to see all the animals back and installs even more fake trees after blowing up the dam. An enraged Mabel convinces George to hold a meeting with the “Animal Council”, composed of several monarchs of other branches of animals, such as a Frog king, a Fish queen, a trio of Snake queens, and an Insect queen butterfly with her son caterpillar.

When the council immediately dismisses Mabel’s concerns, she goes on a big speech about how Mayor Jerry won’t stop after destroying the glade and will come for all the other animals next. This convinces the Insect Queen to “squish” and kill Mayor Jerry with the help of all the other animals. When Mabel tries to defuse the situation, she accidentally kills the Insect Queen and becomes a target herself along with George. They flee the superlodge and while George is upset at Mabel for undermining his authority, he agrees to help her save Jerry after Mabel talks about her feelings and insecurities about having no power to change anything. The two then reunite with Tom Lizard, Ellen, and Loaf. During this, the Insect Queen’s caterpillar son Titus (Dave Franco) cocoons and turns into a butterfly. He takes his spot as the new Insect King and vengefully demands that the council call for an apex predator to squidh Mayor Jerry.

The next day, Mayor Jerry prepares to go to his re-election campaign rally, oblivious to the birds circling him. Mabel and George sneak into his car and use the text to speech on his phone to communicate with him. During this, the birds bring out the “apex predator” – a shark assassin named Diane (Vanessa Bayer), who they intend to drop on Mayor Jerry’s car to kill him. Dr. Sam and her colleagues also get involved in the chase and try to get Mabel to hop back. Eventually, Mabel and George manage to stop the attack from Diane, but the car drives off a bridge and crashes.

Dr. Sam finally gets an unconscious Mabel to hop back, horrifying George as he finds out the truth. The Council then strikes and takes all of them to Dr. Sam’s lab. Jerry and Mabel wake up to them being tied up and Dr. Sam and her colleagues being held hostage, being forced to create a robotic clone of Jerry. They find out the Council’s plan – Titus will hop into the Jerry clone, attend his rally, and play noise from the fake trees to massacre the humans and destroy their brains.

Mabel and Jerry reconcile and find common ground, and then makes Jerry hop back into the robot beaver to free them both and reunite with their allies. At the rally, Mabel tries to reason with Titus, but he refuses to back down and says that after killing the humans, he will also rule over the other animals.

The trees then start going down, but Titus runs up the final remaining tree to activate it. His face is then ripped off and he is unable to activate Jerry’s locked phone as the tree falls and destroys the robot with it. Titus is then eaten by the Frog King.

During the chaos, a wildfire starts spreading across the glade. While they are no longer able to communicate due to the transmitter breaking, George decides to help Mabel and commands his subjects to tear down the dam to flood the glade and extinguish the fire.

Jerry decides to reroute the freeway, declares the glade a protected wildlife preserve, and works with Mabel to help clean it up. With her goal to save the glade complete, Mabel graduates from college and goes back to the lab. While the Hoppers program being exposed led to Dr. Sam and her colleagues being removed, Mabel asks Dr. Sam for a job and she is hired to be her assistant for their future studies.

Mabel then goes back to the glade and finds George sitting on the same rock she used to sit with her grandmother on. She joins him, and while they can no longer talk to each other, they remain friends, with George using her phone to talk via text to speech.

wiki_plot.text:
After attempting to free the class pets from their habitats, six-year-old Mabel Tanaka is suspended from school. Frustrated, her mother leaves her with her grandmother, who lives near a glade. Inspired by her grandmother's love of nature, Mabel develops a deep appreciation for wildlife. Thirteen years later, after her parents move away and her grandmother dies, Mabel continues caring for the glade. Beaverton's mayor, Jerry Generazzo, announces plans to route part of his beltway through it, claiming the animals have already left. Mabel, now a student at Beaverton University, unsuccessfully campaigns to stop the project.

While trying to lure the animals back, Mabel discovers that her biology professor, Dr. Sam Fairfax, and colleagues Nisha and Conner have secretly developed the "Hoppers" program, which allows humans to inhabit robotic animals. Ignoring Sam's warning about interfering with wildlife, Mabel hops into a robotic beaver and escapes the lab.

Mistaken for a real beaver, Mabel is brought before George, also a beaver and the Mammal King, who shelters the glade's displaced animals in an overcrowded dam. She discovers Jerry had installed an artificial tree that emits sound waves audible only to animals, driving them away. After Mabel destroys the tree, animals return to the glade. Growing closer to George, she prepares to reveal her identity, but Jerry destroys part of the glade with explosives and installs more sound-emitting trees.

Mabel and George convene the Animal Council, whose members include the monarchs of the insects, fish, amphibians, reptiles, and birds. Though initially indifferent, the Council agrees to help after Mabel warns that Jerry will eventually threaten all of their habitats. However, her speech instead inspires them to assassinate him. While trying to dissuade them, Mabel accidentally kills the Insect Queen, a monarch butterfly. She and George escape as the animals destroy the robotic bodies Nisha and Conner used to spy on the meeting, exposing the humans' deception. The Insect Queen's son, Titus, crowns himself king and assumes control of the Council.

Although initially upset by Mabel's recklessness, George agrees to help protect Jerry. Joined by Loaf the beaver, Tom the lizard, and Ellen the bear, they locate Jerry and force him to drive to the glade in hopes of stopping the project. Seagulls working for the Council attempt to kill him by dropping a shark named Diane onto his car, but the group escapes. When Jerry still refuses to abandon the beltway, an angry Mabel reveals their location to both the Council and the scientists. They arrive and unhook her from the robotic beaver, causing her to faint and revealing her identity to George.

When Mabel awakens, the Council has taken everyone hostage and forced the scientists to build a robotic clone of Jerry for Titus to inhabit, impersonate the mayor, and use the sound trees to massacre the crowd attending Jerry's re-election rally at the glade. Before leaving, Titus condemns Mabel for stealing the technology, deceiving the animals, and using them for her own goals, while Jerry also calls her out for provoking the conflict. Realizing her obsession with saving the glade had only worsened the situation, Mabel reconciles with Jerry, who reluctantly hops into the robotic beaver to help her escape.

At the rally, Mabel fails to persuade Titus to abandon his plan. Jerry, the animals, and the scientists attempt to unhop him, but the effort fails. During the struggle, Titus destroys the robotic beaver, which causes Jerry to be unhopped, and Mabel chases him up a sound tree to retrieve Jerry's phone after knocking it into the branches, tearing away the 3D printed latex mask covering Titus's robotic face and preventing him from using facial recognition to unlock the phone and activate the attack. Enraged, Titus tears down the tree while revealing his plan to have the insects exterminate every other species, turning the Council against him. The falling tree destroys the robot and ignites a wildfire that spreads toward the city. After Titus is eaten by the Amphibian King, the Council, with an ant queen as the new Insect Queen, joins Mabel, George, and the other animals in dismantling the dam, flooding the glade and extinguishing the fire.

Jerry reroutes the beltway, and the glade is designated a protected wildlife preserve. Mabel graduates from college, and although the Hoppers program is defunded because of her actions, Sam hires her as an assistant. Mabel and George remain friends, communicating through text-to-speech software.

spoiler_text.text:
The film starts as the sun rises on District 12. Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) is woken up on his birthday by his little brother Sid (Smylie Bradwell). Meanwhile, the rest of Panem is gathering as the Reaping is set to start for the 50th Hunger Games, or the Second Quarter Quell, which means there will be twice the usual number of Tributes.

Part I: The Birthday
Before heading to the Reaping, Haymitch stops at a shop where twin sisters Maysilee and Merrilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) work to buy some sweets. He then goes to visit his girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak) by a tree where she sits near some geese. She gives Haymitch a flint striker as a birthday gift, with an inscription from Lenore Dove just for him.

The citizens come together in the town square as Capitol escort Drusilla Sickle (Glenn Close) arrives to announce the Tributes. The two girls selected are Louella McCoy (Molly McCann) and Maysilee. The two boys are Wyatt Callow (Ben Wang) and Woodbine Chance (Serafin Mishiev). As the Tributes are called up, Woodbine attempts to run, and he is shot dead by the Peacekeepers. In the ensuing chaos, Woodbine’s mother runs to his body. Lenore Dove intervenes when the Peacekeepers try to pull her off her son, which prompts Haymitch to jump in before she is hurt, and he is forced to become the next Tribute. Drusilla orders Lenore Dove to be shot, but Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons) steps in to suggest dramatizing the moment instead of shooting someone else and not being able to broadcast it. Drusilla agrees, and the four Tributes are brought up. Haymitch hugs Sid and their mother Willemae (Kara Tointon) goodbye, and Maysilee has to part from a distraught Merrilee.

As the Tributes board the train to the Capitol, Lenore Dove runs after Haymitch and blames herself for him being chosen. Maysilee tries to keep a tough demeanor in the face of the others, but she gets into it with Drusilla, leading to both of them slapping each other before Drusilla starts whipping Maysilee. Plutarch makes her stop so that the girl is still camera ready.

The District 12 teens are brought to meet the other Tributes. District 1 Career Tribute Silka Sharp (Laura Marcus) antagonizes Maysilee, while Panache Baker (Jhaleil Swaby) targets Haymitch. They are joined by Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), who preps the Tributes to put on a show for the Capitol citizens.

The Tributes are put in a parade before the citizens. The people mock the Tributes by tossing smoke grenades into the crowd, which spooks the horses and causes them to run loose. Haymitch is thrown from his chariot while Louella is dragged to her death. Haymitch runs to her body and then stands before President Snow (Ralph Fiennes), giving him a sarcastic slow clap before the Peacekeepers subdue him.

Haymitch is later attacked by Panache under the belief that he tried to crash his chariot into Panache’s, leading to all the Tributes grabbing weapons. It is noted that they could have taken the Peacekeepers because they were unarmed. Haymitch is then brought to Plutarch’s home where he meets Snow. He sees Haymitch’s token (the flint striker) and identifies Lenore Dove from her initials. Snow brings up Lucy Gray and how she just disappeared after he previously trained her. He asks Haymitch if anyone in District 12 talks about her, but he says they don’t. As a result of his act of defiance, Snow threatens Haymitch’s family and promises him a slow and painful death in the arena.

Part II: The Rascal
Haymitch, Maysilee, and Wyatt later meet their mentor, Wiress (Maya Hawke), victor of the previous Hunger Games, along with Mags (Lili Taylor), victor of the 11th Games, who offers condolences to Haymitch for Louella. They tell the Tributes how the arena is like one big machine. They also meet a girl (Iona Bell) who has been drugged and made to be Louella’s body double. The others call her “Lou Lou”.

Haymitch is later approached by Ampert Latier (Percy Daggs IV), son of Beetee (Kelvin Harrison, Jr), victor of the 34th Games. Ampert suggests forming an alliance (the “Newcomers”) against the Career Tributes (from Districts 1, 2, 4, and 5) to better stand a chance. Haymitch later meets Beetee, who tells him that Ampert being a Tribute is punishment by the Capitol for Beetee interfering with their communications system. Beetee recruits Haymitch for a sabotage plan. While training, Haymitch is also friendly with a District 6 girl named Wellie (Rada Rae).

The Tributes are then made to give their interviews with Caesar. They are styled by Magno Stift (Billy Porter) and dressed by Effie Trinket (Elle Fanning). Haymitch plays up a “bad boy” persona to better appeal to the crowd. Afterwards, he is pulled aside by Plutarch, who gives him a phone to speak to Lenore Dove. She has been captured by Peacekeepers and is being held at a base, and she still blames herself for Haymitch’s predicament, but he reaffirms his love for her. Plutarch reveals he is sympathetic to the Tributes and their plight.

The Games are set to begin. The 48 Tributes are brought up into the arena. As the event begins, they charge towards the cornucopia to grab their weapons. Panache quickly takes a swing at Haymitch but misses. Wyatt takes a hatchet to the back to protect Lou Lou. Haymitch flees into the woods to separate from everyone else. By the end of the night, 20 Tributes, including Wyatt, are confirmed dead.

Haymitch stops to drink from a lake but realizes too late that the water is poisoned. He grabs some charcoal tablets (which he learned about from Snow) and uses it to puke up the poison water. Haymitch is then reunited with Lou Lou after he stops her from eating something that could potentially be poisoned. Haymitch then sees that some of the flowers are flammable, while he possesses a fireproof cloak. Lou Lou walks towards flowers with poison pollen, which she succumbs to. Haymitch tries to prevent the Capitol from extracting her body, leading to them sending electric butterfly mutts to shock him into letting her go. When they won’t stop, Haymitch wraps the cloak around himself and ignites the flowers to scare the butterflies off.

Ampert finds Haymitch so that they can carry out their sabotage plan. Using an explosive sunflower, they plan to shut down the Capitol’s cameras in the arena by flooding the place. Haymitch enters a hidden hatch where the butterflies were retreating, and he places the bomb down before the Peacekeepers can stop him. Haymitch escapes drowning, but when he tries to find Ampert, he finds the boy being mauled by rabid squirrel mutts. Haymitch fights them off with fire but fails to save Ampert, as well as failing to uphold his promise to Beetee that he wouldn’t suffer.

The lights and cameras go off for a moment but quickly go back. Snow figures that Haymitch was behind the sabotage, and he orders for a volcano to erupt, wiping out a good part of the arena. Haymitch hides under the cloak and envisions Lenore Dove with him. Meanwhile, Snow interrogates Plutarch, who denies having any involvement in the attack. Snow intends to have Haymitch killed immediately, but Plutarch suggests drawing it out for him to make for better entertainment. Snow asks Plutarch if he’s considered becoming a Gamemaker.

Part III: The Poster
Once the dust has cleared, Haymitch goes out looking for survivors. He is ambushed by Panache and two other Careers. Haymitch kills the other two until it’s just him and Panache, but he ends up getting a poison blowdart to the neck, courtesy of Maysilee. She confirms to Haymitch that the eruption wiped out most of the Tributes, leaving the two of them, plus Silka, Wellie, and Maritte (Sky Francis).

Haymitch convinces Maysilee to explore the perimeter with him and see if they can find a way out. They try to pass a hedge but end up attacked by berry-shaped leeches. After escaping, they set fire to the hedge to burn the leeches and move forward. Haymitch finds the arena’s power generator and the giant force field protecting it.

Haymitch and Maysilee decide to part ways so that they don’t have to watch each other die. However, the sound of a cannon (Maritte dying) brings them back in a panic. They are then attacked by a flock of waterbird mutts, who aggressively peck at them. Haymitch fights them off, but they prove fatal to Maysilee. Haymitch stays by her side as she dies. He watches her body get extracted.

The cannon fires once more after Maysilee, and Haymitch hears Wellie’s bell token ringing. However, it’s Silka, who killed Wellie and took it off her. She chases Haymitch with her hatchets and prepares to kill him. He leads her to the force field, where she throws one of the hatchets at Haymitch, but the blade bounces off the force field and hits Silka in the chest, killing her. Haymitch is declared the victor, but as he is about to be extracted, he gets another exploding sunflower and ignites it, dropping it down into the power generator to blow the whole thing up.

Haymitch is later recovered and brought back to the Capitol. Caesar gives a recap to the audience, making it seem like Haymitch acted selfishly in order to win, leaving him feeling guilty as he has to see his fellow District 12 Tributes die again. There is no mention of his acts of rebellion.

Upon returning to District 12, Haymitch finds that his house has been set on fire by the Capitol, with Willamae and Sid perishing. Haymitch later attends a funeral for them, plus Maysilee, Louella, and Wyatt.

Haymitch is told that Lenore Dove has been freed. They reunite by the tree, but Haymitch discovers that she ate a sweet planted by Snow. They are unable to make her vomit the poison, and Lenore Dove slowly succumbs to it in Haymitch’s arms.

Haymitch moves into the Victors’ Village descends into alcoholism and isolates himself from everyone, including his friends Burdock Everdeen (Scot Greenan) and his wife Asterid (Grace Ackary). When they try to get him out, he goes as far as to attack them so they never see him again. Plutarch visits a distraught Haymitch before he goes on his victory tour. He urges Haymitch to keep fighting against the Capitol so that someday, it may finally be brought down, and so that the deaths of his loved ones will not be in vain. Haymitch spends the next few years working against the Capitol. From a distance, he watches Burdock and Asterid with their baby girl…Katniss.

Decades later, after the downfall of the Capitol, the older Haymitch (Woody Harrelson) stands at the memorial for all of the victims of The Hunger Games. He is joined by Katniss and Peeta (Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson), who wish him a happy birthday. Haymitch then goes by the tree with the geese so that he can sit and remember his time with Lenore Dove.

wiki_plot.text:
Haymitch Abernathy lives in Panem's District 12 with his widowed mother and younger brother, Sid, whom he helps support by assisting a bootlegger. His girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird, is a member of the Covey, formerly-itinerant artists forced to settle in District 12.

The reaping for the milestone 50th Hunger Games, dubbed the Second Quarter Quell, falls on Haymitch's sixteenth birthday. To mark the anniversary, each district must provide four tributes instead of two. Tribute Woodbine Chance flees District 12's reaping, but Peacekeepers kill him. In the ensuing chaos, Haymitch protects Lenore Dove from the Peacekeepers, and is accordingly selected as Chance's replacement by tribute escort Drusilla Sickle and television director Plutarch Heavensbee. The other District 12 tributes are Wyatt Callow, the oddsmaker for his bookie family; Haymitch’s neighbor Louella McCoy; and the mayor's daughter Maysilee Donner, who has an identical twin, Merrilee.

During the tribute parade in the Capitol, a chariot accident kills Louella. Haymitch mockingly applauds President Snow while standing over Louella's body. He is later summoned to Heavensbee's family estate, where Snow threatens him and his family in response. To conceal the death, Snow replaces Louella with a body double, whom the District 12 tributes nickname "Lou Lou".

With no viable District 12 victors available, the Capitol assigns District 3 and 4 victors Wiress and Mags as mentors. Districts 1, 2, 4 and 5 make up the Career alliance, while the other districts nickname themselves the "Newcomers". During training, Beetee, a former victor forced to mentor his own son, Ampert, as punishment for rebellious activities, recruits Haymitch into a covert plan to sabotage the arena, assisted by Ampert, the Newcomers, Wiress, Mags, and Heavensbee, who is sympathetic to the tributes. Most of the Newcomers are unaware of their part in the plan. Haymitch adopts a "rascal" persona in the pre-game interviews to attract sponsors.

When the Games begin, Wyatt is killed by District 1's Silka while protecting Lou Lou, who finds her way to Haymitch, but dies after inhaling toxic pollen. Haymitch separates from the Newcomers and meets up with Ampert to carry out the sabotage. Their explosives flood the arena's underground passages, but fail to permanently disable its systems. Ampert is killed by carnivorous squirrel mutts, then Snow cleanses part of the arena with a volcanic explosion before interrogating everyone who contacted Haymitch prior to the Games, with Beetee taking the blame. To keep his cover, Plutarch proposes to Snow to preserve Haymitch and use him as an example to quell future dissent.

Haymitch reunites with Maysilee, who kills Panache to save him. The two find a power generator at the arena's edge and discover the generator's protective force field. Waterbird mutts fatally injure Maysilee, who dies in Haymitch's arms. Afterwards, Silka pursues Haymitch to the arena's edge. When she throws her axe, Haymitch ducks, allowing the axe to rebound against the force field and kill Silka. Haymitch detonates his remaining explosives in a final attempt to destroy the arena then loses consciousness.

After recovering in the Capitol, Haymitch discovers that the Games have been edited to hide his acts of rebellion, instead portraying him as selfishly cunning. He returns to District 12 to find his home in flames and his mother and brother murdered on Snow's orders. Haymitch reunites with Lenore Dove and unknowingly feeds her a poisoned gumdrop planted by Snow. As she dies, Lenore Dove urges Haymitch to prevent another "sunrise on the reaping". Devastated, Haymitch retreats into isolation at the Victors' Village, distancing himself from his friends, including Burdock Everdeen. Some time later, Plutarch visits and encourages Haymitch to continue his resistance. Over the following years, Haymitch descends into alcoholism while mentoring the succeeding District 12 tributes. One day, Haymitch watches Burdock and his wife Asterid with their newborn daughter Katniss while hiding from them. 

Years later, with the Capitol overthrown and the Games abolished, Haymitch finds peace with an adult Katniss and her husband Peeta Mellark.

spoiler_text.text: A true account of an unknown actor who believed he wasn’t meant to just write “Rocky”, but to play Rocky Balboa. Facing constant rejection, Sylvester Stallone risks everything, refusing to give up the lead role against impossible odds.

wiki_plot.text:
In the early 1970s, Mike Stallone struggles to make it as an actor in New York City, living on the edge of homelessness while juggling low-paying jobs and auditions. Sleeping outside one night, Mike finds and adopts a puppy that he names Butkus. He reluctantly stars in a softcore pornography film to help pay his rent.

Mike starts to date his coworker Sasha Czack, and introduces her to his father, Frank. Frank is dismissive of his son's acting aspirations and sees him as unintelligent, much to Sasha's disgust. She encourages Mike to start using his real name, Sylvester, and to try his hand at writing scripts. Sylvester and Sasha marry and relocate to Los Angeles. A friend introduces Sylvester to film producers Robert Chartoff and Irwin Winkler, who have little interest but meet with him as a courtesy to discuss his idea for a union movie. On the way out, Sylvester sneaks one of his scripts, Paradise Alley, into their secretary's pile. Impressed with the quality of his writing but finding that particular script unsuitable for production, Chartoff and Winkler encourage Sylvester to share any future writing.

When Sasha becomes pregnant, the couple find themselves in greater financial difficulties, and Sylvester is forced to sell Butkus. Drinking at a bar, he sees the Muhammad Ali vs. Chuck Wepner championship fight, and is moved by Wepner, the underdog, lasting fifteen rounds, far longer than expected. He goes home and stays up all night writing a new screenplay, Rocky. Chartoff and Winkler love the script, but bristle at Sylvester's demand for a lead role. 

After extended attempts to buy him out with an inflated script fee, they finally persuade United Artists to approve a reduced budget and cast Sylvester as Rocky Balboa, with the condition that he can be replaced if the project falls behind schedule. Low-budget director John G. Avildsen is hired, and the script's setting of New York City is changed to Philadelphia to avoid the costs of a unionized production. Sylvester uses his script fee to buy Butkus back.

Principal photography begins at a grueling schedule. Sylvester sustains injuries to his legs and hands and catches the flu, all of which complicate the filming schedule. Avildsen insists on a single take for most scenes, which Sylvester finds challenging. Chartoff and Winkler resort to raising some of their own funds to make up for an unexpected shortfall. Avildsen tells Sylvester that the film so far is "good," but not great, lacking a truly moving performance from him to tie it together. When filming Rocky's argument with his future manager Mickey Goldmill, they agree the scene as written is not working. Sylvester channels his frustrations with his father into an ad-libbed monologue, giving the film Avildsen's desired emotional climax.

Rocky completes production. Despite a small premiere in New York City, the film becomes a runaway success and wins multiple Academy Awards.
