spoiler_text.text:
The film opens with a brief montage of a couple, Joe and Angela (Seth Rogen and Olivia Wilde), with sounds of them laughing and joking together. Cut to the present, where Joe is teaching music at a conservatory. When the lesson is over, he awkwardly pushes his bike out of the building to ride it home.

Joe and Angela have a daughter, Maggie, who is at a sleepover for the night, and they live in Joe’s family’s old house, something that he feels insecure about. Joe arrives to find Angela anxiously setting up their place because she invited their upstairs neighbors, Pina and Hawk (Penelope Cruz and Edward Norton). Angela wants to make a good impression, but Joe is preparing to confront the other couple about how loud it is when they have sex.

Pina and Hawk arrive in the middle of Joe and Angela’s bickering, but Angela assures them that everything is fine. Hawk notices a piano in the room, which belongs to Joe, but he is defensive about it being used since Joe used to play in a band before getting married. Pina is a sexologist, and Hawk says he is a firefighter, though Joe constantly refers to him as a “fireman”. Angela quickly starts to worry because they only have champagne to serve because Joe forgot to get wine, as well as Pina not eating any of the charcuterie. Joe gets out a bottle of wine meant for a special occasion.

While Joe is a bit of a dick to Pina and Hawk, they admire his brutal honesty. He excuses himself to smoke a joint, and Pina asks to join him. They end up chatting and bonding, while Hawk hangs out with Angela and discusses the house’s architecture and decorations. Pina takes a single hit of the joint and gets high quickly. She tells Joe how Hawk was a patient of hers before they started dating, and she had already been in a failed marriage. Pina also shows that she has a tattoo of two birds to represent her and Hawk.

The couples reconvene in the living room as Angela gathers tequila shots for them. Hawk finds a record of Joe’s old band, but he once again refuses to allow anyone to hear his music. Joe starts to complain about Pina and Hawk’s sex noise, which Angela tries to shut him up for, but the two are understanding over the honesty. They reveal that Joe had actually come to their apartment while they were having sex and pounded on their door to get them to shut up. Angela is embarrassed but Joe blows up over the situation.

Joe brings up a growling noise that they have heard, which brings Pina and Hawk to admit that they have group sex with their friends Kai and Vanessa, as well as various other people. Joe and Angela become curious and ask the couple about their sex parties, seemingly interested in joining. They go into full detail of the types of acts, consent, and the overall feeling of “surrendering” their bodies to people outside their relationship, as well as things that they would not do (like double penetration).

The conversation takes a turn when Hawk brings up how Angela walks in front of the window naked. Joe confronts her over this, which Angela admits doing because she enjoys being looked at. Pina chimes in and says she notices Joe looking at her breasts in the elevator when they run into each other.

Pina and Hawk admit that they did accept Angela’s invitation because they were hoping to initiate group sex with her and Joe. After some awkward back-and-forth, the couples switch partners. The mood is ruined when, after some dancing with Pina, Joe falls over and hurts his back. Hawk does a quick move to set Joe’s back in order, though he just complains about the pain. Joe starts being rude again to Hawk, mocking his real name (Howard Wilson Kelly), until Hawk reveals that he came up with the name himself after his wife passed away. Joe makes it worse by making a joke about it.

Everyone calms down after Pina blows up on Hawk for not listening to her, since she had told him that she knew Joe and Angela would not be ready for sex with them. It comes out that Joe and Angela have not had sex in over a year, bringing to light all of their personal issues like Joe’s feelings of failure in music and how it’s made Angela feel miserable as a result. She recounts the first time she and Joe met, watching him play with his band at a bar and how she ran from home to see him since she made her bad date drop her off. Pina tells the couple that they should either try their relationship over, or accept that it’s completely over instead of sticking around for Maggie’s sake. Joe and Angela both seem to agree it’s the case with the latter.

Joe and Angela privately discuss what they should do next. When they go back to the living room, they see that Pina and Hawk have already left. The couple remain quiet for the rest of the night, but Joe goes into his office and starts to play the piano for the first time in ages. Angela joins him and lays her head on his shoulder.

wiki_plot.text:
In San Francisco, musician, Joe, arrives home from his job as a band teacher at a conservatory, to discover his stay-at-home wife, Angela, has invited their upstairs neighbors, divorcée, Piña, and widower, Hawk, over for dinner at their apartment. Joe and Angela's marriage is rocky, and they bicker constantly, most recently over the loud sex sounds they often hear from upstairs. Joe plans to confront the couple, but Angela, who is desperate to impress the neighbors, demands he keep calm and quiet.

Piña and Hawk arrive at the apartment as Joe and Angela are mid-argument. Unprepared to host a dinner party, Angela makes several awkward mistakes, such as not having any wine, and not checking Piña's dietary restrictions. Meanwhile, Joe openly antagonizes the couple, but is surprised to see they are impressed by his brutally honest nature. The group eventually warm up to one another, although Joe still resents his neighbors.

Later that night, Piña and Hawk apologize for the noise they make during sex, and reveal to Joe and Angela that they participate in sex parties, which is the reason for the noise; Joe and Angela are titillated by this discovery, but Joe grows angry again when he learns Hawk has seen Angela naked through a window. Breaking the tension, Hawk admits that he and Piña came to the dinner party hoping to invite Joe and Angela to have group sex with them. Joe and Angela are eager, but Piña, who is a psychotherapist and sexologist, is unsure after seeing the couple fight throughout the night. Instead, they decide to swap partners. However, Angela is too nervous to initiate sex with Hawk, while Joe falls while dancing with Piña, and hurts his back.

Another argument erupts between Joe and Angela, and he berates their neighbors. Piña gets the couple to talk about their relationship, and learns of the resentment they have for each other and the fact they have not had sex in a year. Piña suggests the couple should separate instead of sticking together for the sake of their daughter, Maggie, or find a way to reframe their relationship, as the current status appears to have run its course. Joe and Angela seemingly agree to separate, and discuss their next moves, but upon returning from the kitchen, discover Piña and Hawk have left. Joe returns to his office and plays his piano, which he had previously refused to play, with Angela eventually joining him.

In 1932 Granada, Carlos, a young man from a wealthy family, is refused membership of an exclusive social club after its members vote against his admission using a blackball ballot because of rumours about his homosexuality. His father, Vicente, urges him to deny the rumours and seek admission again. His sister, Valentina, describes the restrictions she faces as a woman, while his mother suggests that he leave for Madrid. In a club at night, Carlos dances to a seguiriya and encounters a mourning elderly woman who identifies him as her missing son, but Carlos flees afterwards.

Carlos appeals to the club's committee and, when questioned, denies being homosexual. In the wake of the botched Sanjurjada, the Casino is stormed by a mob. After the building is destroyed and covered in snow, Carlos escapes using the painters' scaffolding and walks up a snowy mountain, where he encounters a boy with a young woman and a group of skiers and is addressed by the personified Snow, whose voice is that of the elderly woman he met earlier. Realising he has died and wasted his life living in secret, Carlos begs the voice to return to the world of the living, to no avail.

In 1937, during the Spanish Civil War, Sebastián, a young village trumpeter, survives an attack by Italian aircraft on a community preparing to welcome them. His mother is killed. After fleeing the attack, he is forced to join the Nationalist forces to survive. He is assigned to guard Rafael Rodríguez Rapún, a wounded Republican prisoner of war, and obtain information from him. Rafael had belonged to Federico García Lorca's theatre company, La Barraca, and had been the poet's lover. As Sebastián gets to know Rafael, his homosexual desire is aroused, bonding closer with him as Rafael introduces Sebastián to Lorca's poetry.

Nené Romero, a popular cupletista entertaining the troops, acquaints herself with Sebastián and introduces him to queer role models such as Edmond de Bries. As a last request Rafael asks Sebastián to recover a manuscript of Lorca's play La bola negra from an apartment in Alcalá 96 and preserve it. Rafael is taken with other prisoners for a summary execution ('), and Sebastián is placed in the firing squad, killing Rafael. In 1939, Sebastián survives the war and retrieves the manuscript, although dropping a few of the pages on the floor.

In 2017, Alberto López Azcuna, a historian and former playwright, is researching queer dissidence in the music of Rosa Eskenazi while visiting Athens. His estranged maternal grandfather dies and leaves him an inheritance should he meet a lawyer in Cantabria. In Madrid, Alberto lives with his boyfriend, Juan Pablo. Alberto struggles to communicate with his mother, Teresa, who resents her father's abandonment of her. Teresa urges Alberto not to travel to Cantabria and intends to sell the house she inherited. Alberto's part of the inheritance turns out to be the remaining manuscript of La bola negra, believed to have been left unfinished by Lorca. Carlos is revealed as La bola negra's protagonist, the first explicitly gay character in Lorca's work. Alberto investigates the origins of the play and seeks the help of Lorca scholar Isabelle Durand.

Alberto's grandfather is revealed to be Sebastián, who went on to live in the countryside with another man while allowing the villagers to believe that they were cousins. Although estranged from his family, Sebastián had followed Alberto's theatrical career from a distance, attending a performance and keeping press cuttings. Alberto meets his grandfather's surviving partner, who tells him that Sebastián would have been proud of him. Isabelle corroborates the manuscript's authenticity, and Alberto and Teresa opt against selling Sebastián's house as they begin to reconcile.
wiki_plot.title: La bola negra

wiki_plot.text: Madden depicts the life and career of John Madden, from his tenure as head coach of the Oakland Raiders and his relationship with team owner Al Davis (Christian Bale) to his transition into sports broadcasting and his role in developing the Madden NFL video game franchise. The story explores Madden's friendship and professional partnership with Davis, including the Raiders' victory in Super Bowl XI, as well as the personal and professional challenges surrounding his retirement from coaching. After leaving the sidelines, Madden becomes a television commentator before collaborating with Electronic Arts founder Trip Hawkins (John Mulaney) to create a football simulation video game. The film also depicts Madden's marriage to Virginia (Kathryn Hahn) and Davis's relationship with his wife, Carol (Sienna Miller), while examining how Madden's personality and approach to football shaped his subsequent career.

wiki_plot.text:
Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin, known as Mando, and his foundling Grogu, work for the New Republic to hunt down neo-imperialist warlords of the former Galactic Empire. After a successful mission, Mando is tasked by New Republic commander Ward to find the mysterious warlord Commander Coin. The New Republic has been offered intel on his whereabouts by the Hutt Twins, siblings and successors to the deceased crime-lord Jabba, in exchange for rescuing Jabba's son and heir Rotta from the moon Shakari. Mando reluctantly accepts the assignment, and receives a new Razor Crest ship as pre-payment.

Upon arriving at Shakari, Mando discovers that Rotta is a popular gladiator in a fighting pit owned by crime-lord Janu. Rotta, desperate to step out of Jabba's shadow, enjoys his status as a self-made fighter and refuses to be rescued by Mando, saying that his next fight will repay his debt to Janu and set him free. Mando tracks Janu down and offers to buy Rotta's freedom, but Janu refuses, intending for Rotta's final fight to be a match in which he will continue fighting monsters until death. Mando returns to Rotta, who refuses to believe him, instead calling on security. Mando is subdued and must fight Rotta in the arena. He defeats Rotta, but surrenders rather than killing him. He tells Janu that this fight has fulfilled Rotta's debts, and that Janu must now set him free. Realizing that his plan has been thwarted, Janu floods the arena with monsters, forcing Mando and Rotta to work together to defeat them. Rotta breaks the arena's security systems, which sets the surviving monsters free, before escaping. Aided by Zeb Orrelios, Mando and Grogu pursue and capture Rotta.

Rotta claims that the Twins only want him so they can kill him, preventing him from potentially claiming control over the Hutt Cartel. When Mando explains that he needs to give Rotta to the Twins in exchange for Coin's whereabouts, Rotta tells him that Janu and Coin are the same person. Trusting Rotta, Mando and Zeb raid Janu's compound and bring him back to Ward, who takes him in for questioning but warns that the Twins will not take kindly to Mando's breaking his promise to deliver Rotta to them. Mando returns to Nevarro with Grogu. He enlists four Anzellans to modify the Razor Crest and helps Rotta go into hiding via a gunrunner. At night, Mando and one Anzellan are captured by bounty hunter Embo, who delivers him to the Twins on Nal Hutta; Grogu and the other Anzellans follow.

Mando is brought before the Twins, who have intercepted Rotta and are intending to slowly torture him for hundreds of years. To punish Mando for breaking his contract, the Twins remove his helmet and drop him into a pool of water which houses Amanin and the giant Dragonsnake. Defeating the Amanin, Mando recovers his helmet and escapes with the help of Grogu and the Anzellans, but is mortally envenomated by the Dragonsnake in the process. Unable to fit aboard the small Anzellan ship, Mando stays behind on Nal Hutta, holding off his pursuers to cover Grogu and the Anzellans' escape as he succumbs to the venom. Grogu also chooses to stay behind, tending to the dying Mando and eventually saving his life using an antidote made by a friendly fisherman. Mando, now fully recovered, decides to go after the Twins instead of fleeing Nal Hutta, reasoning that they would still pursue him and Grogu.

Mando and Grogu break into the Twins' palace using the gunrunner ship and battle their way through their droid security force, before being intercepted by Embo. Mando duels Embo while Grogu frees Rotta, who fights the Twins; the fight eventually drops himself, the Twins, and Embo into the Dragonsnake pit. Grogu saves Rotta with the Force while Embo escapes through the tunnel Grogu created earlier, leaving the Twins to be eaten alive by the Dragonsnake. The Anzellans return, bringing Ward and a New Republic squadron with them, to destroy the Twins' palace and droids.

Ward confirms Mando's suspicions that Janu and the Twins were working together, and Rotta chooses to stay and work with the New Republic. Mando and Grogu leave in the Razor Crest, where Mando teaches Grogu how to pilot it.

spoiler_text.text:
1966, Gary, Indiana – A young Michael Jackson (Juliano Krue Valdi) joins his older brothers Jermaine (Jayden Harville, later Jamal R. Henderson), Marlon (Jaylen Lyndon Hunter, later Tre Horton), Tito (Judah Edwards, later Rhyan Hill), and Jackie (Nathaniel Logan McIntyre, later Joseph David-Jones) to play music and sing under the strict tutelage of their father Joseph (Colman Domingo). They also live with their mother Katherine (Nia Long) and sister LaToya (Jessica Sula). Joseph is set on making a success out of his boys due to his frustrations with the way they currently live.

Over the next few years, the Jackson brothers perform at shows with Michael at the front singing. Although they do a good job, Joseph wants them to keep practicing and not take breaks. When Michael speaks up after one show, Joseph beats him with a belt in front of everyone else. Michael escapes into stories like “Peter Pan” and wishes he were like his hero.

Joseph dubs his sons “The Jackson 5” and has them performing at other venues until they are spotted by Suzanne de Passe (Laura Harrier), who works for Motown. She meets Joseph about signing the boys. The Jacksons go to Motown and meet producer and Motown president Berry Gordy (Larenz Tate). When Michael is in the recording booth, Berry tells him to keep still since he likes to move his feet when singing. Michael’s feet remain still but his body continues to move as he sings. The Jackson 5 come out with classic hits like “I Want You Back” and “ABC”, while Michael views Berry as more of a father figure than Joseph.

1978, Los Angeles – Michael (now played by Jaafar Jackson) meets with Quincy Jones (Kendrick Sampson) as he begins working on his latest album, “Off The Wall”. Michael asks the executives to make it seem like his solo album was his idea when discussing it with Joseph. He later records “Don’t Stop Til You Get Enough” in the studio with Quincy. By now, Michael has a huge number of fans who swoon upon seeing him, but he also uses his fame to visit sick children. He also rescues a chimp named Bubbles from an unsafe environment. Michael is also set up with a bodyguard named Bill Bray (KeiLyn Durrel Jones).

Michael becomes insecure about his appearance after he develops vitiligo on his skin, and he also gets a rhinoplasty to make his nose more slender. When Joseph sees him, Michael says it was for his sinuses.

Joseph continues to try and control his sons’ careers, seeing himself as the reason they have any success at all. When it becomes clear Michael doesn’t want to go along with his plans for a family tour, Joseph tries to guilt him until he walks out and leaves with Bill, being greeted by a mob of fans outside the gates. They stop somewhere, where Michael expresses love for his family but also a desire for creative freedom. Michael ends up joining his brothers on the Triumph Tour.

1981 – Michael and Bill meet with a group of men at a record company, including entertainment lawyer John Branca (Miles Teller), who has handled acts like The Beach Boys. When Michael sees that Branca is set on letting him do his own thing creatively, Michael immediately agrees to work with Branca. His first act is to have Branca fire Joseph as manager via fax. When Joseph shows this to Katherine and threatens to “whup” Michael, Katherine says he is too old and frail to be whupping anybody.

As Michael and Branca begin working on his next album, Michael aims for it to be the biggest album ever. He looks for inspiration and sees a news report on the rising gang violence between the Crips and Bloods. He gathers people at the studio to shoot the “Beat It” music video as a way to bring others together.

The album gets further into development with tracks like “Billie Jean” and “Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin'”. Michael and Branca have trouble settling on a title for the album until they land on “Thriller”, due to Michael’s fascination with horror films like the ones featuring Vincent Price. The two go to visit Walter Yetnikoff (Mike Myers), president of CBS Records, to try and get the video for “Billie Jean” to play on MTV, but Walter thinks it’s a tough sell because MTV doesn’t want to play black artists. At Michael and Branca’s urging, Walter calls the MTV president and threatens to pull all of CBS’s artists (which includes Billy Joel, Bruce Springsteen, and Cyndi Lauper) from MTV. The video quickly gets played, and Michael’s star continues to rise.

At a party to celebrate the success of “Thriller” (which indeed does become the highest selling album of all time), Michael reunites with Suzanne and Berry, both proud of his success, as well as his mother and brothers…and a loud, drunken Joseph. Joseph later sits with boxing promoter Don King (Deon Cole) to discuss setting the Jacksons up for another tour, with Michael at the center of things. Joseph manages to guilt Michael into agreeing to the tour so that he does not disappoint his family.

Michael joins his brothers in shooting a commercial for Pepsi. Things take a bad turn when the stage pyrotechnics go off and set Michael’s hair on fire. He is rushed to the hospital, where he is told that the back of his scalp will suffer permanent damage. All Joseph cares about is if Michael will be good to hit the stage again in no time.

Michael recovers with help and support from Katherine and Branca. When he is ready to go back to performing, he joins his brothers on their Victory Tour, but on their final night, Michael announces that this will be their last tour, despite Joseph’s intentions to go worldwide. Katherine smiles proudly as she hears the announcement. Michael performs “Human Nature” and walks past Joseph, who tries to get Michael to reconsider, but Bill makes it clear that Michael is done with Joseph.

1985, London – Michael goes to Wembley Stadium as he starts his Bad Tour and performs “Bad” in front of a huge cheering crowd.

The final text promises that Michael’s story will continue.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1966, steel worker Joseph Jackson assembles his five sons Jackie, Tito, Jermaine, Marlon, and Michael into the musical band The Jackson 5, with Michael on lead vocals. After months of grueling rehearsals, the Jackson 5 perform until Suzanne De Passe discovers them in Chicago in 1968, and they are signed with Motown a year later. They become a huge success, allowing them to move out of their house in Gary, Indiana, and into the Hayvenhurst mansion in Encino, California, in 1971. Motown founder Berry Gordy believes Michael has more potential as a solo artist.

In 1978, Michael signs with Epic Records for his first solo album as an adult, Off the Wall, with Quincy Jones producing. Joseph restricts Michael's solo career, believing he is solely responsible for his children's fortunes, and forces him to accompany his brothers on the Triumph Tour. Feeling insecure about his appearance and developing vitiligo, Michael undergoes a rhinoplasty to shrink his nose. Following an argument with Joseph, he is advised by his bodyguard and close friend, Bill Bray, to forge his own path. In 1981, he hires John Branca as his attorney, who helps him fire Joseph via fax.

Michael visits children's hospitals and experiments with ideas for his next album. After watching a news report on the Crips–Bloods gang war, he hires members of both gangs to appear in his music video for "Beat It". Thriller breaks worldwide sales records while Michael delivers a groundbreaking performance of "Billie Jean" at Motown 25. In New York, Michael and Branca convince the CBS Records president, Walter Yetnikoff, to have MTV, which does not play videos by black artists, play Michael's music videos.

While Michael enjoys his success, Joseph meets with the boxing promoter Don King and proposes the 1984 Victory Tour to reunite his sons. King offers Joseph a PepsiCo sponsorship deal, provided that Michael tours with the Jacksons. While the Jacksons film a Pepsi commercial, a spark from the pyrotechnics sets Michael's hair ablaze, resulting in third-degree burns and nerve damage. He and Branca sue PepsiCo for damages, with the settlement proceeds going to the burn center where he was treated. While hospitalized, Michael meets the other patients as he considers whether to participate in the Victory Tour.

Michael agrees to tour with his four older brothers. At the Victory Tour's final show at Dodger Stadium that December, they perform "Human Nature" and "Working Day and Night". Michael announces it is the last time the Jacksons will perform together, severing his ties with Joseph. In 1988, Michael performs to an ecstatic crowd at Wembley Stadium as part of his first solo tour, the Bad World Tour.

wiki_plot.text:
Thousands of years ago, a tribe of Minions, different from the one that would go on to serve Gru, are on a hunt to serve the world's greatest villains. James, an artistic Minion with a passion for storytelling and drawing, quickly develops a close friendship with two others: Henry, a two-eyed minion who enthusiastically supports James, and Ed, a minion who cannot hear and communicates using sign language and becomes close to them. Among the many masters the Minions serve is a Russian warlock who is killed by a Rabbit monster after Henry summons it from his spell book, which Ed then takes along with them and they inadvertently kill their masters in various ways like a cyclops, a mummy, a pirate, a queen, and an emperor.

Eventually, the tribe stumbles across a bank robbery and decides to chase after the robber to become his henchmen. However, the robber is revealed to be an actor, filming a chase scene for a 1927 movie titled The Good, the Bad and the Stupids. Though filmmaker Max is furious with the Minions, studio executives Frank and Elwood Bright are enamored by their antics. Max hires the Minions to star in his films and soon become a global Phenomenon, appearing in several silent films like Tiny Barbarians with Chainsaws, Look Behind You and Then Down, and They Came from the Stars to Hit You with a Frying Pan! Part Four: Target Miami Beach, and living a glamorous life of Hollywood stardom.

When sound film is introduced, the Minions are unable to adapt to the new technology due to their incomprehensible language. Resulting cuts in of a war film and costing the studio millions in failed material, the Minions are fired and forced to rest in an abandoned factory. Not wanting to give up on his passion for storytelling, James comes up with an idea to make his own movie titled Minions & Monsters, where the Minions would fight against giant monsters. The leader of the tribe, Dick, rejects James's idea and leads the rest of the Minions back towards finding a new evil master, but Henry and Ed break away from them to help James make his film a reality. They pitch it to Max, who encourages James to work on the movie, providing him with a film camera. To help James bring his film to fruition, James uses the warlock's old spell book to summon a Cthulhu monster for the movie. In doing so, the trio releases a small, green monster named Gary Orkam Oliver Magma Ichabod "Goomi" the Deceiver who offers to help him find the perfect monsters for his film, leading them to a frozen fortress at the bering sea, where they free sea monsters Howard the kraken and Phillips the piranha under the false pretense of using them as stars in James's movie. In reality, he aims to use them to summon Irene, a large, orange, multi-eyed blob monster, in order to destroy the world and get revenge.

Meanwhile, Dick and the other Minions are hired by Dort, apparently an alien robot on a mission to invade Earth. While beginning his quest for world domination, Dort falls in love with women's rights activist Debbie, enlisting the Minions' help to romantically pursue her. While James and his crew begin production on his movie, Henry overhears Goomi's plan to Howard and Phillips and tries to alert James, but only for the monsters to kidnap him and convince James to use him as a sacrifice in filming the scene where Irene will be summoned. Just as filming begins, Goomi and the monsters conjure Irene, and she begins wreaking havoc, chasing Henry through the streets in the process.

When Dort and the other Minions witness Irene during his date with Debbie, Dort seemingly flees, leaving the Minions to fend for themselves. Irene succeeds in swallowing Henry, and James drives a milk car through her to rescue him. Greg and the Minions try to destroy Irene, but to no avail. As she repairs herself, Dort reappears with Dick and the other Minions in spacecraft, showing his true identity as an alien robot, and they successfully turn Irene into stone. James and Henry cast an undo spell to send Goomi, Howard and Phillips back with the spell book. The public hails the Minions and Dort as heroes. Ed has captured the entire battle on film, allowing the Minions to complete James's movie. Months later, Minions & Monsters debuts in theaters and receives a standing ovation from the audience while Dort starts a family with Debbie with a toddler robot boy and a baby robot girl.

In a film museum, tour guide Olivia, who tells the story of James and Henry, finishes her story before it is revealed that the entire plot, including the tour, is a film within a film directed by James and Henry. In the mid-credits, the spell book falls into the hands of Gru's Minions and is tested by James, Henry, Kevin, Stuart and Bob, as well as one of Gru's adoptive daughters, Agnes.

The film starts on the island of Motunui, where Gramma Tala (Rena Owen) telling a group of children a tale about their land. Thousands of years ago, the mother island Te Fiti was formed and brought life across the ocean and surrounding islands. One day, the legendary shapeshifting demigod Maui (Dwayne Johnson) stole a tiny green stone that is the heart of Te Fiti. This caused her to disappear, cutting off all the magic brought by her. A volcanic monster named Te Ka emerged. Maui tried to fight the creature, only to get knocked out and causing him to lose his magic fish hook that grants him his powers.

While the other children are terrified by the monsters, Moana (Emma Puahi-Shapazian), daughter of Chief Tui (John Tui) and his wife Sina (Frankie Adams), is enchanted by the story. Moana later goes by the ocean and spots some birds trying to grab a helpless little turtle. Moana carefully guides the turtle back to the water. This causes the Ocean to come to life and interact with Moana. Tui warns his daughter not to go past the shore.

As Moana grows, she learns about the ways of the people in Motunui (“Where You Are”) as she prepares to one day become the new chief. She also bonds with her animal sidekicks, Pua the pig and Heihei the rooster. When she is 16, Moana (now played by Catherine Laga’aia) continues to go by the Ocean with Gramma Tala. She show Moana that she has the heart of Te Fiti, which she recovered the day Moana first interacted with the Ocean. Moana also wants to put her stone on the highest mountain, as the previous chiefs have done.

Moana sees that the coconuts in the area are starting to spoil rapidly, and the villagers are struggling to grab any fish in the ocean. Moana suggests that they sail beyond the shore to find a solution, but Tui does not want Moana leaving the village. Sina explains to Moana that Tui once went sailing during a storm with his cousin, and the ensuing waves caused an accident that killed Tui’s cousin. He never forgave himself and wants to prevent Moana from suffering the same fate. Moana gets Pua and attempts to sail on her own (“How Far I’ll Go”), but her boat is quickly destroyed and she is washed up back on the shore, found by Gramma Tala.

Tala tells Moana about a cavern up in the mountain. She travels up there and finds a drum, as well as what look like old sails. Moana bangs the drum, and some torches turn on by themselves. She then sees a vision of her ancestors, as they were all voyagers and wayfinders (“We Know The Way”). Realizing that her people are capable of sailing, Moana tries to tell this to her father, but Tui says Gramma Tala has told him about this before, and he refused to listen. Another villager then comes to get Tui and Moana because Tala is ill.

The family gathers in a tent, where Gramma Tala is on her deathbed. She speaks to Moana one last time, giving her a necklace to carry the heart of Te Fiti inside, and telling her what to do when she finds Maui. Moana hops on a new camakau and heads off on her mission (“How Far I’ll Go (Reprise)”). The lights in the village go out, and a manta ray spirit manifests in the Ocean, indicating that Tala has passed since she earlier told Moana that she wants to come back as a manta ray.

In the morning, Moana discovers that Heihei has stowed away on her boat. As she tries to navigate her way toward a star constellation where she thinks Maui is located, Moana ends up crashed on a small island. Maui emerges and tries to take her boat for himself. He is covered in tattoos, and the one on his chest, “Mini Maui”, interacts with him the most. After he brags to her about who he is (“You’re Welcome”), Maui traps Moana in a cave and prepares to sail away, along with Heihei as a “boat snack”. Moana finds a way out of the cave and forces Maui to help her restore the heart of Te Fiti since it’s all his fault anyway, with help from the Ocean.

On their way to find Te Fiti, Moana and Maui find themselves confronted by the Kakamora, tiny little coconut-like pirates. They attack the camakau while trying to make a grab for the heart. One of the Kakamora gets it, and Moana takes it upon herself to retrieve it. After evading blowdarts and other dangers, Moana gets the heart back and manages to steer her boat out of the Kakamora’s path, causing their ships to collide into each other.

Moana continues trying to improve her wayfinding skills, even though Maui is still cynical about the whole mission. Their next stop is to find the crab creature Tamatoa (Jemaine Clement), a scavenger that collects all the treasures that fall to the bottom of the ocean. Tamatoa resides in the Realm of Monsters, which is accessible through an opening in the ground. Sure enough, Maui’s hook is on Tamatoa’s shell. Moana dresses up as a trinket to get the crab’s attention while Maui tries to get the hook. Moana tries to praise Tamatoa as some kind of legend, which gets him to start singing about his love for treasures (“Shiny”). When Tamatoa spots Maui, he taunts the demigod over a tattoo on his back depicting a woman throwing a baby away. Moana distracts Tamatoa by making it seem like she’s going to give him the heart, but she tricks him with a fake rock. Moana and Maui escape via a geyser, which hits Tamatoa and makes him fall on his back.

As they continue their journey, Moana gets better at voyaging and bonding with Maui, while back on Motunui, the villagers continue to struggle, and Tui seems to have sadness over Moana’s absence. Maui also has to get used to having his fish hook back since his shapeshifting powers aren’t 100% yet.

Moana asks Maui about the tattoo on his back. He reveals that his birth mother got rid of him by throwing him in the river. He was found by the gods and granted his abilities to become Maui. He gave gifts to humanity in the hopes that they would love him. Maui wanted to use the heart so humans can have the gift of creation, but he realizes he’s made a mistake.

The duo reach Te Fiti, where Te Ka emerges and tries to attack by hurling fireballs. Maui shapeshifts into a hawk to fly past the beast, even getting her wet so that her lava arms can harden. However, Te Ka proves to be too powerful, severely damaging the hook and preventing Moana and Maui from reaching their destination. Maui feels that he is useless without the hook, so he leaves Moana. Feeling defeated, Moana tells the Ocean that it chose wrong by picking her, and she gives the heart back to it.

Moana is visited by the spirit of Gramma Tala, who encourages her to finish her mission. With her spirits restored, Moana dives back into the water and recovers the heart.

Moana sails back toward Te Fiti, and Maui returns to help her. Moana evades Te Ka’s attacks, but when she goes to the island, she sees that Te Fiti is nowhere to be found. That’s because Te Ka IS Te Fiti, now corrupted without her heart. Knowing what she has to do, the Ocean clears a path for Moana (“Know Who You Are”). Te Ka calms down as she realizes what Moana is doing, and she allows Moana to restore the heart. Te Fiti is brought back to her former glory, and Maui apologizes for his actions. The mother island grants him a restored fish hook. Moana and Maui part ways as friends.

Moana returns to Motunui and is greeted by her family. She undergoes the village’s ceremony so that she may become chief. Instead of placing a stone on the mountain, Moana puts a conch shell. Her first act is to lead the villagers on a voyage across the sea (“We Know The Way (Reprise)”), accompanied by Maui.

wiki_plot.text:
Long ago, on the Polynesian island of Motunui, the inhabitants worship the goddess of nature, Te Fiti: a living island who brought life to the ocean using a pounamu stone as her heart and the source of her power. Maui, the shape-shifting demigod of the wind and sea and master of wayfinding, stole Te Fiti's heart and gave humanity the power of creation. Te Fiti disintegrated, and Maui was attacked by Te Kā, a volcanic demon. Maui lost both the heart and his magic fish hook to the depths of the sea before he disappeared.

A thousand years later, the ocean chooses Moana, the daughter of Motunui's chief Tui, to return the heart to Te Fiti. Tui and Sina, Moana's parents, try to keep her away from the ocean to prepare her to become the island's chief. Sixteen years later, blight strikes the island, killing vegetation and shrinking the fish catch. Moana suggests going beyond the island's reef with her pet pig, Pua, to catch more fish and explore the oceans, but Tui forbids it.

Moana tries to conquer the reef but is overpowered by the tides and shipwrecked. Moana's grandmother, Tala, shows her a secret cavern of ships and reveals that Motunui's people were voyagers until Maui stole Te Fiti's heart; the ocean was no longer safe. Tala explains that Te Kā's darkness is destroying the island, but it can be cured if Moana finds Maui and has him restore Te Fiti's heart. Having been given the heart by the ocean, Tala gives it to Moana. Tala later becomes gravely ill and tells Moana to find Maui.

Moana sets sail on a camakau from the cavern along with her dimwitted pet rooster, Heihei, who stowed away on it. They are caught in a typhoon and shipwrecked on an island, where she finds Maui stranded. She demands Maui return the heart, but he refuses and traps her in a cave before leaving on her boat. She escapes and confronts Maui, who reluctantly lets her on the camakau. They are attacked by Kakamora, coconut pirates who seek the heart, but Moana and Maui escape.

Moana doesn't see Maui as a hero since he stole the heart and cursed the world, and convinces him to redeem himself by returning the heart. However, Maui first needs to retrieve his fishhook from Tamatoa, a giant coconut crab, in Lalotai, the Realm of Monsters. While Moana distracts Tamatoa, Maui retrieves his hook, only to find he can no longer control his shape-shifting. He is overpowered by Tamatoa, but Moana manages to help them escape. Maui reveals his first tattoo was earned when his human parents abandoned him as an infant, and the gods granted him his powers out of pity. After reassurance from Moana, Maui teaches her the art of wayfinding, regaining control of his powers, and the two grow closer.

They arrive at Te Fiti's island, only to be attacked by Te Kā. Moana refuses to turn back, and the confrontation badly damages Maui's hook. Unwilling to lose his hook again, Maui abandons Moana, who loses hope and tearfully asks the ocean to find someone else to restore the heart. The ocean obliges and takes the heart, but Tala's spirit appears, inspiring Moana to find her true calling. Moana retrieves the heart and sails back to confront Te Kā. Maui returns, having had a change of heart, and buys Moana time to reach Te Fiti by fighting Te Kā, thereby destroying his hook. Upon being unable to find Te Fiti, Moana realizes Te Kā is Te Fiti, but corrupted without her heart. The ocean clears a path for Moana, allowing her to return the heart to Te Fiti, who heals the ocean and the islands from blight. Maui apologizes to Te Fiti, who fixes his hook and Moana's boat before falling into a deep sleep and becoming an island.

Moana bids farewell to Maui and Te Fiti, then returns home and reunites with her parents. After placing a shell on top of the stack of stones placed by all previous chiefs, Moana takes up her role as chieftess and wayfinder, leading her people as they resume voyaging, accompanied by Maui.

Various vignettes of college football games are shown highlighting the top performances of several top college athletes during the early 1940s. Their standout performances make them celebrities on their own campuses and single them out as exceptional athletes. Then a surprise attack by the Japanese on December 7th 1941 at Pearl Harbor seems to change the everyday priorities of the American public, and recreational activities like football and other sports seem to be reassessed by the general public as to their relative importance.

Four top American football players enlist in the United States Marine Corps after the attack on Pearl Harbor. While preparing for the Battle of Okinawa, they play a football game, the Mosquito Bowl, that later become famous.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens as the voice of fashion designer Sam Anselm (Michaela Coel) speaks bitterly to an unseen person, saying they deserve neither love nor hate. We then see pop superstar Mother Mary (Anne Hathaway) as she performs her song “Burial” to an adoring crowd.

Mary has been preparing a comeback tour after suffering a fall onstage during her last performance, something that was rumored to be a suicide attempt. Days before her big show, she suffers a panic attack over the dress she has to wear for her show, and she travels to London.

Mary flies to see Sam, whom she hasn’t seen in over a decade. Sam’s assistant Hilda (Hunter Schafer) guides Mary to Sam. Mary tells her that the dress doesn’t feel like her, so she wants Sam to design something new and something that feels closer to her style. Mary mentions that her show will be preceded by a younger singer named Miel Contrera (Alba Baptista), giving Sam the impression that Mary wants to upstage her.

Sam requests Mary show her the dance that she wants to accomplish in her dress, though she refuses to let Mary play the song out of spite. Mary does the dance all the way without music. Sam then comes up with a vision for a dress with a train made from previous dresses.

Mary later asks Sam why she doesn’t listen to her music. She expresses her feelings over being shut out of Mary’s inner circle once she became more famous, and Sam felt cast aside despite doing so much work for her. Sam also recalls attending one of Mary’s shows and admitting it was an amazing show, but Mary never appeared to acknowledge her.

Sam then tells Mary about how she got a tooth extracted and saw a red ghost-like figure, which manifested as some type of cloak that mesmerized Sam until she let it go out of her house. Mary becomes scared, as she tells Sam that she saw the same red ghost before. Mary recalls meeting a fan named Imogen (FKA Twigs) and joined her for a seance with other women like Nikki (Kaia Gerber), Tessa (Jessica Brown Findlay), Kyla (Isaura Barbe-Brown), and Emily (Atheena Frizzell). The women speak a chant and summon a spirit that possesses Imogen. She takes Mary’s hand and cuts it. The red ghost later appeared before Mary and tried to enter her wound, but she escaped. During her last concert, the ghost appeared again, causing Mary’s fall and injury.

Mary tells Sam how she is haunted by the spirit, no matter how hard she has tried to repress it. Sam decides to put Mary through a ritual to remove the spirit from her body. She uses her dressmaking tools and creates a circle in the room. She gets Mary to remember their previous collaborations and the dresses Sam used to make for her. Mary cuts her chest open with scissors, and Sam is able to pull the spirit out, which comes out like a giant red cloth. The rest of Sam’s team arrives and is shocked at what they are seeing.

After Mary recovers, Sam starts to make her dress. Mary is escorted to her vehicle before departing, but she apologizes to Sam for having wronged her.

Hilda later comes to Sam and tells her about her vision of Mary wearing her dress, which includes a halo that Sam also came up with. We then see the red dress crafted from the fabric made from the red spirit.

wiki_plot.text:
Mother Mary, a world-famous musical artist, prepares to mount a comeback performance in the wake of an onstage accident. Overwhelmed during a costume fitting, she flees to the English countryside to seek out fashion designer Sam Anselm, her estranged lover and collaborator. With three days until Mary's show, Sam begrudgingly agrees to design her a dress.

Tensions rise as they make preparations at Sam's barn-turned-workshop, and Mary struggles to explain her vision for the dress. Sam questions her about the upcoming performance and her accident, which some suspect was a suicide attempt. She refuses to listen to Mary's new song, forcing her to perform the choreography without music. Suggesting a long train made from her previous iconic dresses to be torn away onstage, Sam recognizes that Mary is desperate for personal and artistic clarity.

Old resentments are laid bare as a vengeful Sam forces Mary to confront the end of their close creative partnership: despite them launching Mary's career together, Sam was denied credit and cut out of her inner circle. Sam explains that she has not listened to Mary's music since being visited by a ghost. At a concert after their estrangement, her bitterness toward Mary resulted in a broken tooth, and she awoke after having it removed to discover the wound had released a spectral figure of red cloth.

Mary reveals that she saw the same ghost after a séance with her team where Imogen, a fan possessed by a mysterious spirit, cut open Mary's hand. That night, the red ghost appeared to Mary and attempted to enter her wound, but she escaped. Exhausted by her demanding tour, she was confronted by the ghost during a concert and severely injured, falling as the spirit inhabited her. Though recovered from the accident, she remains haunted by the ghost now inside her.

Sam leads a reluctant Mary in a ritual to exorcise the spirit, using her dressmaking tools and invoking their past collaborations. Taking Sam's shears, Mary slices open her own chest and Sam pulls out the ghost, turning the spirit of their mutual trauma into harmless fabric. Mary apologizes for having wronged Sam and her team rushes her to the show, while Sam is inspired to craft the red fabric into a dress. Her assistant Hilda describes Mary taking the stage, shedding her original costume and dedicating her song to Sam, who envisions Mother Mary in the finished dress.

The film shows nighttime interviews with 24 Israeli soldiers and intelligence officers, conducted by Yuval Abraham over three years on rooftops in Tel Aviv. Shown only as dark silhouettes with their voices distorted to hide their identities, the interviewees describe the AI systems and mobile phone surveillance used to identify targets in Gaza and their role in the mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Some draw simple maps and diagrams to illustrate their points. Interspersed with the interviews are shots of Tel Aviv at night. One interview is interrupted by an air raid siren, and a rocket from Gaza is seen streaking overhead. An introductory sequence summarises the October 7 attacks.

A soldier explains that "NAZA" is a military acronym for Nezek Agavi (), meaning "collateral damage". Each potential target, such as an individual Hamas member, is assigned a NAZA value representing the expected number of civilian deaths from an airstrike. "We say 15 NAZA. We don't say 15 people killed and certainly not that 15 children and women will be killed." According to one interviewee, targets with values below 20 required no special authorization, while approvals could be granted for higher values, up to 500 in one case. The combined NAZA values of all potential Hamas fighters add up to "all of Gaza", one source says. An interviewee adds, "At the start of the war, we bombed everything. NAZA wasn't an issue." During efforts to drive Palestinians from northern Gaza, maps used color-coded quadrants to track progress. An interviewee says the objective was to destroy as much as possible before questions about the legitimacy of military operations could arise.

"Annihilation zones" were designated from Tel Aviv, and Palestinians learned their boundaries by being shot when they entered them. "Whoever you decided to kill was considered a terrorist," a man explains. One interviewee recalls Israeli snipers firing on starving people at a food distribution point and illustrates the incident with a stick-figure drawing. Bodies were left lying in the streets until they were eaten by dogs. A female soldier recounts how when injured people were left lying on the ground, she would drop another bomb on them to kill them.

Most interviewees describe killing from a distance as routine office work and themselves as merely "cogs" in a machine. They say: "If I hadn’t been there, someone else would have done it." Or: "I trust the system, and I do my job as part of the system." Or: "My role is technical. I’m not supposed to express any moral or principled position." They say the most reliable targets were often not Hamas fighters themselves but their homes, where their families were present. Every building in Gaza is numbered and the storeys of each building are recorded. The relevant buildings were identified by AI surveillance of communications systems in Gaza, by a system known as "Lavender". This analyses vast amounts of data from the Israeli-controlled phone network to extrapolate the likelihood that any given individual is a "Hamas operative" – thus creating potential targets for elimination, each with an associated NAZA number. An interviewee says the system has an accuracy rate of 85%. One interviewee calls this system a "factory of targets". However, the Lavender system also made mistakes; among the 70,000 phones it had earmarked, "It once marked an 80-year-old woman. They bombed her house with her entire family in it."

An interviewee explains that intelligence personnel were able to access the cameras and microphones of any phone in Gaza, including those of children. The phrase "Where's Daddy?" refers to hacking into a child's phone to determine when their father will be home, enabling an airstrike to kill the entire family. The name came about because checking children's calls for words like “Daddy” and “return” had proved a particularly effective strategy. An interviewee describes the practice bluntly: "You hack her [i.e. the child's] phone and then kill her." A soldier says that while Hamas sometimes does use human shields, it is absurd to speak of human shields when airstrikes are used to kill them at home alongside their families. "It’s just not true. We bomb them in houses because that’s how we find them,” he says. “They just come home to sleep. That’s where we catch them.” In one case, a father had gone out, inadvertently leaving his mobile phone at home; as a result, the missile aimed at his flat killed his daughters, aged 3 to 6, while he himself was spared. The officer recalls listening in on the phone as one of the daughters burned alive and her mother called for help. An interviewee says the ability to hear everything happening inside people's homes made him "feel like God".

Several interviewees say the mass killing of civilians was not only accepted but viewed as a duty, reflecting the widespread belief in Israel that there were "no innocents in Gaza" in the aftermath of the October 7 attacks. Retaliation is said to have been uppermost in the Israeli intelligence services' minds: "We said we need to erase Gaza … they deserve it." Another interviewee says that killing Palestinians and carrying out the mission "felt good"; although psychological support was available, no one in his unit needed it. One likens it to a video game, while another speaks of doing a remote airstrike, then going for lunch, or going out with friends. The interviewees present themselves as liberals, not racists: "No one in my unit hated Arabs", one asserts.

A member of an elite unit says that at times, completing missions could be "insanely fun". He recalls a visit to Poland and says: "I still see those Nazis as evil, but what does that mean I am?" He says he now understands how a man can destroy an entire building, with all the people inside it, and then carry on as normal and "go home to his degree in clinical psychology". Asked whether he had participated in a genocide, he answers "yes" without hesitation, adding: "We intended to kill those children." Interspersed with this are images of people in Tel Aviv observing a minute of silence on Holocaust Remembrance Day and a retrospective at the Tel Aviv Cinematheque honouring Claude Lanzmann.

A "Bibi Department" within military intelligence is said to use methods such as blackmail to thwart efforts by Palestinians or Israelis to pass information to international investigators in The Hague.

At various points during the film, archive footage is shown. This includes an Israeli-made film from the 1970s celebrating the installation of Gaza's telephone infrastructure by Israel, with a Hebrew voiceover explaining how useful the system would be for surveillance in the years to come, as well as historical footage of the founding of Tel Aviv and images of the last standing building of the earlier Palestinian villages Tel Aviv engulfed, many of whose inhabitants were displaced to Gaza.

There is more that would be too risky to speak about, Abraham is told. Late in the film, a television clip shows a younger Netanyahu promoting his book Terrorism: How the West Can Win and defining terrorism as politically motivated violence against innocents. A short sequence from Gaza shows a Palestinian father looking for his children, calling into a destroyed building, and children's legs protruding from beneath a concrete slab.

More like nuanced bear

A quiet, but no less scathing, indictment of how land is robbed of its true purpose and the balance of nature is thrown completely off balance all so a few tourists can snap some photos and civilization at large can continue to prioritize convenience over intentional st…

The irony will be when this doc only attracts even more eco-tourism to Churchill, Manitoba.

wiki_plot.text: The film takes place in Churchill, Manitoba and Arviat, Nunavut, a small Inuit community located about 150 miles/200km north of Churchill. It documents the migration of polar bears as they move through the town, which is populated by tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters. An Inuit narrator, Mike Tunalaaq Gibbons, recounts how Inuit relate to polar bears, their cultural significance and how sedentary life and climate change are creating challenges for bears and humans alike.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in a diner, where a young man named Bear Bailey (Michael Johnston) is practicing with a waitress over how to confess his feelings to his childhood friend and longtime crush, Nikki Freeman (Inde Navarette). While the waitress thinks it’s sweet, Bear’s best friend Ian (Cooper Tomlinson) thinks it’s corny. Bear just wants some alone time with Nikki, but they are all going to trivia night later with Ian and their other friend Sarah (Megan Lawless).

When Bear goes home, he finds his cat Sandy dead, as she had accidentally gotten into his oxycodone. Bear puts her body in a garbage bag and then cries in his room.

Bear later talks to Nikki on the phone, as she tells him that she is planning to put in her two weeks notice at their job. He overhears her saying she dropped a crystal necklace down a sewer drain. Bear goes to a shop to buy her a replacement necklace, but then sees something called a “One Wish Willow”, which he also purchases.

Bear joins Nikki, Ian, and Sarah for trivia night. Afterwards, Bear drops Nikki off at home. He wants to confess his feelings to her but he is too awkward and he refers to her as “Freaky Nikki”, a nickname she despises. When she asks Bear if he likes her, he just denies it. After Nikki goes back inside, Bear takes out the One Wish Willow and wishes for Nikki to love him more than anyone in the world. Nikki suddenly reappears and offers to go home with Bear, saying she feels bad because her dad is dying of cancer.. When they get home, Nikki asks Bear to sleep with her. They start kissing until she suddenly pulls back in terror, claiming that there is something behind Bear.

In the morning, Bear finds that Nikki made a memorial for Sandy by taking her body out of the trash and putting it on the kitchen floor, which just disturbs Bear. Nikki thinks she took something that has been making her act weird.

Eventually, Bear and Nikki start dating, which confuses Ian and Sarah for how sudden it feels. While the two are out at dinner, Bear gets a call from Ian. He tells Bear that he’s done some digging and learned that Nikki’s dad is completely healthy, and Nikki doesn’t even have a good relationship with him. Furthermore, Ian says that Sarah told him that she and Nikki talked about Bear and she just saw him as a “little brother”. When Bear goes to ask Nikki the truth about her dad, she starts to yell and throw a tantrum in the middle of the restaurant until Bear calms her down. They later go back to his place to have sex, while Nikki doesn’t seem to be in control of herself.

At night, Nikki stands in the corner creepily, watching Bear sleep. When he tries to leave the bed, she screams at him to stay with her.

The next day, Bear is getting ready to leave for work but sees that Nikki has duct-taped the whole front door. She gives him a lunch box to bring to work, then stands by the door just smiling and peeing herself. At work, Bear is talking to Sarah before taking a bite of the sandwich and finding a note from Nikki that says “How’s the verdict: cat?” Bear lifts the bread and sees Sandy’s paw, causing him to vomit.

In his car, Bear calls the number for the One Wish Willow and speaks to a representative that tells him the wish cannot be altered or undone and only ends when the person who made the wish dies. The rep then puts “the real Nikki” on the phone, and she just just screaming. When he returns home, he finds Nikki standing in the same place she was before, covered in urine, vomit, and feces.

Ian expresses concern for Bear and invites him to a party. Bear tries to go without Nikki, but she protests enough that he brings her along, to Ian’s chagrin. The party plays a game of Drunk Jenga, which takes a turn when Nikki goes up and recites an incestuous monologue of “Hansel and Gretel” that makes everyone uncomfortable. When Bear goes up, his block reads “kiss the person to your left”, which happens to be Sarah. Nikki pulls Sarah out of the way and sits in her place so Bear has no choice but to kiss her. The real Nikki seems to snap out momentarily and begins stabbing herself in the face with a broken beer bottle. Bear goes to the hospital to try to get Nikki help, but he is denied for some reason.

Bear brings Nikki home and gets a text from Sarah to meet her. As Bear is leaving, the real Nikki speaks and begs Bear to kill her while “she” (“Freaky Nikki”) is asleep. Bear simply asks what’s so bad about being with him.

Bear goes to meet Sarah in her car. She tells him that Ian and Nikki were hooking up on and off again for several years, and Ian thinks that Nikki is dating Bear to get back at him. It is also implied that Sarah likes Bear, but before either of them can act on their feelings, Nikki comes charging toward the car. She smashes the window and then repeatedly slams Sarah’s face onto a brick until she’s dead and her face is gone. A terrified Bear helps Nikki move Sarah’s body

Bear goes back to the antique shop to get another One Wish Willow to try and undo the wish, but he is unable to break the willow in half like the first time since he already used his wish. He goes to Ian’s home to try and get him to make the wish for Bear to have never made the wish, but Ian sarcastically wishes for a billion dollars, and money instantly starts raining from the ceiling.

Bear goes back to the house to find that Nikki propped up Sarah’s corpse in the living room. He wants to get Nikki to reverse the wish by giving her a willow, but she plans to shoot him and herself. Ian comes in out of nowhere, leading to Nikki shooting him in the head. Bear locks himself in the bathroom and decides it’s time to end it. He almost shoots himself in the head but instead overdoses on the same oxycodone that killed Sandy.

When Bear exits the bathroom, Nikki has already broken the willow so that Bear can be in love with her. They share a final kiss until Bear collapses. Nikki holds him in her arms and almost shoots herself in the head until the wish wears off. Nikki snaps back to normal and begins screaming hysterically at all the dead bodies around her.

wiki_plot.text:
Baron "Bear" Bailey harbors romantic feelings for his friend Nikki Freeman, who works with him at a music store alongside their friends Ian and Sarah. He returns home one night to find his cat, Sandy, dead after consuming oxycodone. Bear visits a crystal shop to buy Nikki a replacement crystal necklace, but instead buys her a One Wish Willow, a novelty toy that grants one wish when broken. That night, when Nikki asks him if he likes her, he is unable to admit his feelings. Frustrated, Bear breaks the One Wish Willow and wishes that Nikki loved him more than anyone in the world. She immediately reappears and asks to stay with him, saying her estranged father is dying of cancer. In bed, Nikki kisses Bear but briefly screams and pulls back.

The next morning, Nikki creates a memorial with Sandy's remains, and explains her erratic behavior was the result of MDMA. After confessing their mutual feelings, the two begin happily dating. Ian calls Bear and says that Nikki had told Sarah that she saw Bear as her "little brother" shortly before they began dating, and that she lied about her father's cancer. When Bear questions Nikki, she reacts with defensiveness and anger. That night, Bear awakens to Nikki watching him sleep, and she cries hysterically, accusing him of not loving her.

The next day, Bear discovers that Nikki has duct taped the front door shut and that the sandwich she prepared him contains Sandy's remains. When Bear calls One Wish Willow's customer service hoping to alter his wish, he is told that the wish cannot be modified and that the wish will only end when he dies. The representative then puts a screaming Nikki on the line, and Bear hangs up in a panic. He returns home to see that Nikki has stood in place all day, waiting for him, and is covered in bodily fluids.

Nikki insists on accompanying Bear to a party at Ian's house, against Ian's wishes. During a Jenga drinking game, Nikki recites a violent and incestuous version of "Hansel and Gretel" she has written. Bear draws a block, which dares him to kiss the person to his left, Sarah. Nikki moves Sarah and kisses him instead, but then suddenly stabs herself with a broken bottle. Bear drives Nikki to the hospital but brings her home after she refuses treatment.

That night, Sarah texts Bear to meet at the park. As he attempts to leave, the real Nikki speaks, saying her obsessive personality is asleep and begs him to kill her. He refuses, offended that she would rather die than be with him. At the park, Sarah tells Bear that Ian and Nikki had been casually hooking up for two years and expresses concern that Nikki is using him for revenge against Ian. After Sarah hints that she is attracted to Bear, Nikki smashes through the car window and repeatedly slams Sarah's head into a brick, killing her. After they move the body, Nikki instructs Bear to go home while she disposes of it.

Bear buys the two remaining One Wish Willows from the shop to reverse his wish, but is unable to break one. He explains everything to Ian and begs him to undo the wish. Ian sarcastically wishes for a billion dollars instead, causing cash to rain from the ceiling. Bear returns home with the last One Wish Willow to have Nikki reverse his wish and discovers Sarah's mutilated corpse. Nikki, dressed like Sarah, threatens Bear and herself at gunpoint. Ian arrives and Nikki shoots him dead. Bear locks himself in the bathroom and prepares to shoot himself but is unable to go through with it and instead consumes the remaining oxycodone. He changes his mind and tries to induce vomiting just as Nikki breaks the last One Wish Willow. Under her wish's influence, Bear exits the bathroom and kisses Nikki before overdosing and dying. Heartbroken, Nikki prepares to shoot herself, but Bear's death causes the real Nikki to regain control. Horrified by the carnage surrounding her, she wails hysterically.
