spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in the kingdom of Ithaca, where a bard (Travis Scott) is reciting a song of the legendary warrior Odysseus (Matt Damon). Somewhere on the shores of Ithaca, the soldier Sinon (Elliot Page) is seen outside the Trojan Horse. Two Trojan soldiers fire arrows at Sinon, pinning him to the horse. With his dying breaths, Sinon says that it was a gift for Athena.

Odysseus’s home is now overrun by suitors, looking to wed his wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway), who refuses to hear the song. Among them are Antinous (Robert Pattinson) and Polybus (Corey Hawkins), the former who claims he would have fought in the war under Odysseus, though it is revealed he weaseled his way out of fighting so Sinon would take his place instead. Odysseus and Penelope’s son Telemachus (Tom Holland) has never known his father since Odysseus left when Telemachus was still a baby.

Telemachus spars with Mentor (Ryan Hurst), his guide, before speaking to the partially blind swineherd Eumaeus (John Leguizamo). He recounts to Telemachus how he was there with Odysseus when he chose his hunting dog, Argos. To this day, the old dog loyally waits for his master to return home.

Telemachus then goes to speak to his mother. Penelope only considers remarrying because Odysseus granted her his blessing to do so before he went off to battle. While they both knew that going off to fight for King Agamemnon (Benny Safdie) was a dangerous task, Odysseus feared Agamemnon would come for Telemachus, as the king had sacrificed his own daughter to the gods for favorable winds. Penelope also tries to get Telemachus to string a bow and make it hum the way his father did, as Odysseus was a skilled archer.

In the dining hall, Telemachus confronts Polybus for being cruel to Argos, who is now old and frail. Polybus attacks Telemachus until Penelope intervenes and orders him not to hurt her son. Telemachus confides to a handmaiden, Eurycleia (Kate Fuglei), that he is setting out to the seas in the hopes of finding Odysseus himself. Mentor later joins Telemachus with a small crew of men on a boat.

Odysseus is currently on the island of Ogygia, haunted by visions of the goddess Athena (Zendaya) speaking to him and urging him to remember his past. His only company is the nymph Calypso (Charlize Theron), who keeps his memories blocked by feeding him the Lotus Flower. He cannot remember his family or what happened to his crew.

Odysseus’s memories begin after the Sack of Troy, with Odysseus and his men getting ready to return home after ten years on a path separate from Agamemnon and his brother Menelaus (Jon Bernthal). After raiding a village for food and water, the men carry on with their voyage and end up on another island. Odysseus leads his men into a cave, which turns out to be home to the cyclops Polyphemus (Bill Irwin), son of Poseidon. Polyphemus traps the men inside the cave after using a large stone to seal himself and his flock of sheep inside. The men try to stay out of the cyclops’s sight, but Polyphemus grabs and devours two soldiers.

The men wait until the morning to rush their way out of the cave. Polyphemus eats a few more men while Odysseus and the rest remain inside. They wait until the cyclops goes back to sleep, and Odysseus blinds his eye with a fire-tipped spear. Polyphemus roars in agony and briefly speaks in whispers. He opens the cave once more, allowing the men to escape, but Odysseus fires an arrow at Polyphemus, leading the cyclops to chase the men back toward the water, where he kills a few more before the rest are able to flee. Odysseus is chided by his men, especially Eurylochus (Himseh Patel), for his actions, as this now means Poseidon will not make the voyage any easier on them.

Telemachus arrives in Sparta to meet with Menelaus and his wife, Helen of Troy (Lupita Nyong’o), the “face that launched a thousand ships”, now slightly disfigured after the war. Menelaus invites Telemachus and Mentor to sit at his table. He recounts to Telemachus his time being inside the Trojan Horse with Odysseus and the other Ithacan soldiers, and how Sinon was left behind as a diversion to pretend to be a deserter. After the horse was brought into the city, Odysseus led the soldiers to slaughter the Trojans and opening the gates to let the entire army enter and lay siege to the entire place. However, Menelaus has no current knowledge of Odysseus’s whereabouts to provide Telemachus.

Odysseus continues his memories to Calypso by mentioning how they encountered a rough storm before coming upon the island of Laestrygonians, giant brutish warriors. A child Laestrygonian taunts the men when they request food, and he shrieks to alert the other giants. The Laestrygonians pummel and bash many of the men, chasing the rest back out into the sea.

After landing on another island, Aeaea, Odysseus splits off from the rest of the men, while Eurylochus leads the others in finding food, as they are starting to question Odysseus’s leadership. Eurylochus and the others encounter Circe (Samantha Morton), who feeds them but reveals herself to be a witch that transforms the men into pigs. Odysseus realizes something is up since there are other animals on the island, many wild cats, but none try to attack. He shoots an arrow at what he believes to be a deer, but after being killed, it turns back into a man.

Odysseus runs to Circe’s home, not knowing who she really is, but he is able to avoid falling for her tricks. When confronted with the revelation that she turned his men into pigs, Circe rants to Odysseus about her feelings on men before saying that she can turn them back to normal. She tells him the only way for him to find out how to get home is to enter Hades. Circe turns the men back to normal, and they gather whatever provisions they can (except the meat that Circe gave them).

The men carry on and arrive past the great river. They offer their sacrifice and are met by the spirits of the dead, including Sinon, who realizes he was betrayed and left to die. Sinon also informs Odysseus that Antinous is plotting against him, and how he weaseled his way out of joining the war. Agamemnon also speaks to Odysseus, who warns him against returning home, since he arrived home to a celebration, but his wife Clytemnestra (also Lupita Nyong’o) murdered him in vengeance for sacrificing their daughter. Odysseus is then met by Tiresias (James Remar), who tells him that the gods have willed it that only he will survive the rest of the journey. The dead soldiers then chase Odysseus and his men out of Hades.

Back in Ithaca, Antinous tries to make a case for himself to win Penelope’s hand in marriage. After she won’t say where Telemachus is, Antinous finds out from Melantho (Mia Goth), Penelope’s traitorous servant, about where Telemachus is heading. He conspires with other suitors to catch Telemachus and his crew to prevent their return to Ithaca. Eumaeus overhears the scheming as well. Meanwhile, Telemachus, who has been practicing archery with Menelaus, believes it is his time to take over the throne of Ithaca.

Odysseus continues to remember his past. The crew first had to cross through the land of the sirens, with Odysseus ordering his men to tie him to the mast so that he does not do anything after hearing the siren song. At least one crew member jumps ship, while Odysseus is left screaming in pain. They then come upon the whirlpool of the creature Charybdis. Odysseus leads the men away from the whirlpool, but this leads them into the path of the monster Scylla, who devours some more of the crew. Eurylochus and the remaining men lose further loyalty to Odysseus for this decision, which he argues was the safer pick.

The men come upon the isle of Thrinacia. Odysseus tells the men not to hunt the cattle of the god Helios, as Tiresias told him the men would perish from doing so. They go against his orders out of hunger, and ultimately die during an unforgiving storm, in which only Odysseus survives. This is what led him to being found by Calypso.

Calypso reveals to Odysseus that she has kept him with her for seven years under the influence of the Lotus Flower. She admits that she had fallen in love with him and could not bring himself to restore his memories, until now. Calypso returns to Odysseus a token that Penelope left him with before the war so that he could remember her. He then boards a makeshift raft and sails into the sea.

Odysseus washes up on the shores of Ithaca with help from Athena. He poses as a beggar and finds Eumaeus after he was attacked by a group of conspirators, led by goatherd/Melantho’s brother Melanthius (Logan Marshall-Green). After Eumaeus tells him where Telemachus is going to be, Odysseus reaches his son’s group at the temples, where the conspirators are waiting to ambush him. Mentor is killed, but Odysseus slaughters the conspirators and saves Telemachus, though he does not reveal his identity and addresses himself as Sinon. When they return to the palace, Odysseus sees Argos, who wags his tail one last time upon seeing his master again before he dies. This causes Telemachus to realize who his father really is, but Odysseus continues to keep up the charade.

Odysseus is brought to the dining hall with the other suitors. Antinous and Polybus treat him cruelly until Penelope steps in and orders them to stop. After the suitors have been cleared out of the room, Odysseus speaks to Penelope but continues to hide his identity. He expresses his regrets for the entire Trojan War, and all the bloodshed that occurred. A flashback shows him decapitating the statue of Athena, which is presented as though he did it to the goddess herself, and explains why he keeps seeing her. Antinous attempts to kill Telemachus but misses his chance.

Penelope has the suitors gathered by dawn for a challenge that will decide who she will marry. She orders them to string a bow and fire an arrow between several positioned axes. Predictably, none of the men are able to carry out the task, until Odysseus volunteers to go. Penelope knows it’s him once he succeeds and makes the bow hum, and then he fires the arrow as intended. Once the suitors realize who they are dealing with, Odysseus begins to battle the suitors, beginning by firing an arrow at Polybus’s neck.

Penelope and the others stay hidden, but she keeps Melantho out for her deception. Melanthis breaks into the armory and drops weapons down for the suitors to fight Odysseus with, while Antinous can only hide and bark orders. Telemachus fights Melanthius and eventually manages to slit his throat. Odysseus takes several hits but still kills most of the suitors, and others have begun to surrender and kneel to him. Once Antinous is the last one left, Odysseus corners the bastard and returns to him Sinon’s token before impaling him through the stomach.

In the aftermath, Odysseus tells Penelope that he only came to see Ithaca one last time, but he must travel west to honor his fallen men. Penelope joins him on his voyage while Telemachus takes over the throne. Penelope promises to Odysseus that their civilization will rise again someday.

The last we see is a final flashback of Odysseus in the middle of the war, looking up as the Trojan Horse goes up in flames.

wiki_plot.text:
For twenty years, Odysseus, the king of Ithaca, did not return from the Trojan War. Several suitors, including nobleman Antinous, aggressively court Odysseus's wife Penelope to claim the throne from Odysseus and Penelope's son Telemachus. Only Penelope, Telemachus, and Odysseus' half-blind servant Eumaeus still believe Odysseus will return. Penelope tells Telemachus she fears attacks by murderous "Sea Peoples" who violate Zeus's law, the custom of respect between guests and hosts. Telemachus travels with Odysseus's friend Mentor to Menelaus, the king of Sparta, to learn where his father is. Antinous learns of this and conspires to kill Telemachus when he returns and plunder Ithaca. Menelaus and his wife, Helen, tell Telemachus about the war but remain uncertain about Odysseus's fate.

Meanwhile, the goddess Athena appears to Odysseus on the island of Ogygia, where the nymph Calypso is infatuated with Odysseus. Athena commands Odysseus to return home; Calypso dislikes this, but encourages Odysseus to remember his past. Years ago, the Greek army, led by Menelaus' brother Agamemnon, conquered Troy using Odysseus' stratagem, the Trojan Horse, by hiding the Greeks inside, with the soldier Sinon sacrificed as a decoy. While Menelaus and Agamemnon returned home, Odysseus and his crew, including second-in-command Eurylochus, searched an island for supplies. However, the Cyclops Polyphemus traps them in a cave and devours several soldiers. They blind Polyphemus and escape, but hear him cry out to his father, the sea god Poseidon. As a result, the crew faces harsh sea conditions. They land on Telepylus, where Laestrygonians (man-eating giants) kill most of them and sink two of their three ships. The survivors rebel, leaving Odysseus with their ship as they seek refuge on Aeaea with the witch Circe, who turns them into pigs. After Odysseus persuades her to change his men back, Circe advises that to reach Ithaca, Odysseus must cross the river Oceanus into Hades.

There, Odysseus meets his fallen soldiers, including Sinon's shade, who reproaches him for deceiving him, and reveals that Antinous manipulated him into taking his place in the Greek army. Next, Agamemnon's shade reveals that his wife Clytemnestra murdered him upon his return as revenge for sacrificing their daughter Iphigenia to Artemis for fair seas. Finally, Odysseus speaks with the shade of the prophet Tiresias, who predicts that, by divine will, only Odysseus will return home. Chased from the underworld by Odysseus' fallen army, Odysseus follows Tiresias' guidance to survive encounters with the Sirens and sea monsters Charybdis and Scylla. On Thrinacia, Odysseus warns his men not to kill the cattle of Apollo, as Tiresias foretold Odysseus' men would die if they did, but the starving men disobey. Zeus sends a storm that sinks their ship, killing all but Odysseus. He washes ashore unconscious on Ogygia, where Calypso's lotus flowers render him amnesic. 

After seven years, Odysseus regains his memories, builds a raft, and surrenders his fate to the storm. He washes ashore in Ithaca, where he disguises himself as "Sinon". Eumaeus tells him that the suitors sent bandits to assassinate Telemachus and Mentor. The bandits kill Mentor, but Odysseus rescues Telemachus and kills the bandits. Odysseus's elderly dog Argos dies after recognizing Odysseus, and Telemachus deduces Odysseus's identity. During a feast, Odysseus confronts Antinous about betraying Sinon. Antinous thrashes Odysseus before Telemachus intervenes. 

After the meal, Odysseus, still disguised, confesses to Penelope his guilt for violating Zeus's law during the sacking of Troy, desecrating the statue of Athena after killing her priestess (whose form Athena assumed in visions), and initiating the Late Bronze Age collapse. He reveals that the "sea people" were the Greeks themselves, and begs Penelope's forgiveness. Penelope announces she is ready to remarry and tells the suitors to return at dawn.

Penelope declares she will marry whoever can string Odysseus' bow and shoot an arrow through a row of axe heads, as Odysseus did before leaving for the Trojan War. All the suitors fail, but Odysseus succeeds, thereby revealing his identity. The hall erupts in battle. Telemachus helps Odysseus kill many of the most challenging suitors, including Antinous. After the remaining suitors surrender, Odysseus cedes his throne to Telemachus and leaves with Penelope to seek peace in exile. Sailing west to honor Odysseus' fallen soldiers, the couple expect civilization to be renewed and muse that time will forget Odysseus' mistakes.

Smart, smiley, and bursting with undimmed enthusiasm despite such difficult cir…

Following Isra’a from childhood to adulthood, the film traces her family’s journey from Syria to Germany and back with remarkable intimacy and honesty. Rather than focusing on the destruction of her world, co-directors Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes capt…

wiki_plot.text: One in a Million follows Israa, a 11-year-old girl from Aleppo at the start of the documentary, and her family over the following ten years of her life. The film begins with the flight of the family from Syria via Turkey and the Balkan route to Germany. It shows their experience of war, displacement and the personal development of the protagonist and her family. It ends with Israa's journey to destroyed Aleppo after the end of the Syrian civil war.

spoiler_text.text:
Harry (John Turturro) is an aging career pickpocket in a New York where hardly anyone carries cash anymore. The phones and cheap watches he steals barely pay. He lives in a Bronx walk-up with his wife, Rosie (Karina Arroyave), who is catatonic: she can see and hear but cannot move or speak. Harry devotes his life to her. He carries her up flights of stairs because the elevator never works, dances for her to a 1970s disco song, and steals to pay for her care. He sells what he steals through his old friend Ben (Steve Buscemi), who runs a pawnshop.

One evening in a parking lot, Harry spots Dylan (Will Price), a cocky young man with a restored vintage muscle car. First, Harry picks Dylan’s pocket and lifts his wallet. While he’s close, he also quietly wedges a penny into the car door so it won’t lock. Later, while Dylan is inside a bar with his friends, Harry comes back, opens the car, and takes a gym bag. Inside are cash, a gun, and a strange drive that looks like a cross between a credit card and a USB stick, and Harry also comes away with an expensive watch. He gets rid of the gun. Neither he nor Ben knows what the drive is, so Harry sells it, along with some phones, to Frank (Kelvin Han Yee), a fence who runs a Chinese herb shop in Chinatown.

The drive is a crypto wallet holding a fortune, and Dylan is the heir to a powerful New York crime family. The card also has a built-in tracker that sends out its location whenever it is plugged into a computer. When Ben plugs it into his old computer to figure out what it is, the signal leads Dylan straight to Ben’s pawnshop. Dylan ransacks the shop and beats Ben until Ben gives up Harry’s address. When Harry gets home, Dylan is there threatening Rosie. He gives Harry six hours to bring the device back, making it clear that returning it will spare Rosie, but not Harry.

Frank refuses to help. With no other options, Harry calls Detective Allan Warren (Giancarlo Esposito), a police detective nearing retirement whom Harry has known for years, from a pay phone. Allan quietly shows him a Brooklyn address connected to Frank: an electronics store run by Frank’s grandson, Ernie, which ships stolen phones and gadgets overseas to mainland China. Frank has already passed the drive along to Ernie, so Harry heads to Brooklyn. Instead of asking for it, he falls back on his old trade: he creates a distraction in the shop and, while everyone’s attention is elsewhere, lifts the drive back. By the end of the day, he has it in hand.
Along the way, Harry’s day turns into a kind of farewell. On the subway, he catches a young pickpocket in the act and, instead of scolding him, teaches him some tricks of the trade, along with advice that working alone doesn’t have to mean being lonely. He also has a strained visit with his estranged daughter, Kelly (Tatiana Maslany). As he crosses the city, he thinks back on his regrets, the New York of his younger days, and his memories with Rosie.

Harry returns the drive to Dylan at his Bronx apartment, as promised. What Dylan doesn’t know is that Harry, Ben and Eve have pulled off one last job. Eve made a copy of the crypto wallet earlier, and Harry had already lifted Dylan’s smartwatch and left it for her. She used the watch to get past the wallet’s security and drained just under $1 million, so the drive Dylan gets back is empty.

Ben and Eve carry Rosie out to their car and drive her away to safety. After a brief scuffle, Harry gets into a car with Moira, Dylan’s grandmother and the family’s true boss. They drive over the bridge toward the harbor, and the two old pros reminisce about the past.

Some of the stolen money is left for Harry’s daughter, Kelly, in an unmarked envelope.

The final shot shows Harry looking across the water at the Manhattan skyline, seemingly at peace. The film doesn’t show what happens to him, but it makes clear he doesn’t expect to survive.

wiki_plot.text:
Harry Lehman is an aging pickpocket who lives in The Bronx, New York City, with his wife Rosie who is catatonic and unable to speak. Harry does not own a cell phone and is not good with modern technology.

One evening, Harry pickpockets a young man, Dylan, and breaks into his vintage car. He steals a duffel bag from the car, but after finding a gun inside, dumps the bag in a trash can. When Dylan tries to pay for drinks at a bar later on, he discovers he has been robbed. He identifies Harry from surveillance cameras.

The next day, Harry visits his friend Ben, who owns a pawn shop, and is the fence for his stolen goods. Harry shows him a variety of cell phones, Dylan's watch, and Dylan's USB crypto wallet. Neither of them know what the USB device is. Ben plugs the device into an old computer but is unable to open it. He recommends that Harry visit Frank, a fence in Chinatown who is more familiar with electronics.

Harry goes to Frank's Chinese herb shop in Chinatown. Frank buys the device from Harry, along with some smartphones. On his way back home, Harry passes Ben's pawn shop which has been broken into. Unbeknownst to Harry, the device had a tracker on it, and Dylan had ransacked Ben's shop to find the device. An apologetic Ben tells Harry that he had to give up Harry's home address.

Harry returns home to find Dylan threatening Rosie. Dylan reveals that he is the heir of a criminal "family", and Harry is irrevocably condemned to death for crossing him. However, Dylan gives Harry six hours to bring the device back to him in exchange for Rosie's life. Harry goes back to Frank's store but Frank refuses to help him. Out of options, he uses a payphone to contact his friend Allan, a police detective. Allan discreetly shows him an address in Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn which is affiliated with Frank. In Brooklyn, Harry visits an electronics store run by Frank's grandson. He refuses to help Harry and turns him away, but Harry returns and steals the device back by causing a disturbance outside the store.

Harry calls his home using a stranger's cell phone to inform Dylan that he has the device. Dylan still says that he will have to "pay" for his crime. Fearing that he may be dead soon, Harry visits his estranged daughter in Forest Hills, Queens. On his way home, he stops at Ben's store.

Harry returns home, with Ben and Ben's granddaughter, Eve, and returns the crypto wallet back to Dylan. Ben and Eve help Rosie downstairs and take her with them.

A car takes Harry away towards Staten Island, and Dylan's grandmother, the matriarch of the crime organization, reminisces with Harry about the old days. In flashbacks, it is revealed that Eve was able to clone the crypto wallet, and Harry had stolen Dylan's smartwatch, leaving it for Ben and Eve to find. She uses the smartwatch to verify the wallet's two-factor authentication and steals Dylan's cryptocurrency, worth just under $1,000,000, before they leave the United States via the Canadian border to escape retribution from the mob. Some of the money is left for Harry's daughter in an unmarked envelope.

The film ends with Harry staring across the harbor at Manhattan, the World Trade Center in the background, ready for his impending death.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1986, Irwin Pearl, an engineer raising a family in Queens, is approached by his brother Gary, a former NYPD officer, with a business proposition. Both face financial difficulties; Irwin's family is on a tight budget and aspires to send their two teenage sons to Ivy League universities, while Gary is in the middle of an expensive divorce. Since leaving the force, Gary has parlayed his law enforcement experience and wide-ranging political connections into a security and consulting business. He proposes to partner his relationships with Irwin's engineering expertise to consult for Russian immigrant businesses at the docks who are struggling to comply with environmental regulations.

Irwin and Gary have an initially productive meeting with a prospective client. Irwin decides to visit the premises again at night, bringing his sons along to show them his work. He stumbles upon preparations for illegal dumping, and the Russians steal his car and threaten him and his sons. Gary arranges for him and Irwin to meet with Simeon Bogoyavich, a Russian mafia boss who owns the business at the docks and expresses concern that Irwin will contact the police about what he saw. Bogoyavich wants access to Gary's political network and says he will leave Irwin alone if Gary agrees to work for him; Gary, who unlike many of his NYPD colleagues never took bribes, insists that Bogoyavich instead accept a payoff to settle the matter.

Days later, Bogoyavich's men break into Irwin's family's home in the middle of the night, rearranging the furniture and leaving behind photos of the family sleeping. Gary visits the men the next day and beats them up as retribution. Irwin's wife Hester is diagnosed with glioblastoma and given a prognosis of six months to a year to live. Feeling that Irwin and Gary are unable to handle the situation, she reports the matter to the FBI, news which makes its way back to Bogoyavich.

Bogoyavich demands that Gary figure out who contacted the FBI. Realizing that it was either Irwin or Hester, he lies and tells Bogoyavich it was a false report. Bogoyavich tells him that he never saw Irwin as a real threat, and threatened him only to pressure Gary to work for him. With Gary still defiant, Bogoyavich sends his men to kill him. After giving Scott his birthday present and the keys of his car, Gary lures them to a field of tall grass, killing two of Bogoyavich's men before he is shot and killed himself. Meanwhile, Hester prepares to leave for the hospital, aided by her mother, and kisses her sons goodbye as they sleep. In the morning, Irwin expresses his love for his sons to them and reflects.

wiki_plot.text:
The automaker firm SP Heavy Industries, which runs a plant where respected welder Choi Ho-seok works, announces massive layoffs. The metalworkers' union rejects the cuts and barricades themselves on the factory roofs; the strike is broken when police commandos execute a brutal helicopter raid on the roofs, leading to the deaths of several of Ho-seok's friends. In the aftermath, Ho-seok and his fellow survivors are fired, and begin bitterly referring to themselves as "the dead" and to those who kept their jobs as "the living". 

Two years later, Ho-seok reluctantly attends a funeral for another of his co-workers who died by suicide. Ho-seok's wife, Ahn Mi-ok, a mask factory worker, and ten-year-old son Cheol also attend, alongside ambitious documentarian Lee Ye-ji and her wealthy husband Sang-woo. When Mi-ok confronts Ho-seok over his drinking, he notices Ye-ji training a camera on their argument. Infuriated by her intrusion, Ho-seok shouts at her. Embarrassed, Mi-ok steps outside and accidentally drops her loose wedding ring; Sang-woo helps her recover it. Observing the tensions between the couple, Ye-ji decides to make Ho-seok and Mi-ok the primary subjects of her next documentary.

Ye-ji meets Mi-ok at an upscale café, hoping to entice Ho-seok to agree to the film. During their conversation, Mi-ok shares a childhood memory of playing with a hose at her mother's manual car wash job to catch a glimpse of a rainbow, only for her mother to angrily snatch the hose away out of fear Mi-ok would end up in such a lowly position. Seeing the power of the story, Ye-ji asks Mi-ok to retell the story on camera. Seeking to overcome Ho-seok's reluctance, Ye-ji invites him, Mi-ok and Cheol for a weekend getaway at Sang-woo’s lavish estate on the west coast of Korea, where they are treated luxuriously.

Ho-seok finally agrees to sit for an interview, but demands that Mi-ok leave the room. On camera, he suffers a panic attack as he vents his bottled-up rage at his former coworkers, who had left him to be badly beaten after he tried to save them. He angrily denounces the slogans his union chanted, including "solidarity, struggle, and workers' rights", as "all bullshit". As the interview continues, Mi-ok and Sang-woo walk along the beach and partake in flirtatious conversation. Meanwhile, Cheol wanders into the groundskeeper's shed and watches the four adults through the house's closed-circuit television cameras, observing in silence. Cheol befriends the groundskeeper and Mi-ok later witnesses the two hosing down a bush. One night at dinner, Mi-ok and Ye-ji both share memories from their youth of staring at the full moon in the night's sky.

Mi-ok's trust in Ye-ji fades after she surreptitiously follows Ho-seok out of the house into the forest to find him screaming and writhing on the ground, only to turn around and discover Ye-ji had followed her with a camera. Mi-ok and Sang-woo's flirtations culminate with the two skinny-dipping on the beach, though she ultimately rejects his repeated advances. The two return to the estate to find Ye-ji conducting another emotionally charged interview with Ho-seok, at which point Mi-ok demands that filming cease and tells her husband that their family must leave.

As they drive home, news breaks that SP Heavy Industries has been acquired by an American private equity firm, limiting Ho-seok's hopes of ever regaining his job. When Mi-ok and Ho-seok arrive at their house, Mi-ok discovers that Ye-ji has texted her asking if they safely arrived home. She considers replying with a picture of the full moon in the sky but ultimately leaves it unsent.

spoiler_text.text:
American Rick Power (Paul Rudd) lives in Ireland with his Irish wife Rachel (Marcella Plunkett) and their teenage daughter Aja (Beth Fallon). When he was younger he used to be in a band that had some success in the late 80s in a band called Octagon, but now he makes a living as the lead singer for a wedding band. As the film starts, he and his band – which includes his best friend Sandy (Peter McDonald) and band leader Binzer (Rory Keenan) are playing at a small wedding, which Rick imagines as being a massive stadium. He takes a break from the set list to play one of his old original songs, but the crowd doesn’t know it and becomes bored. Binzer tells him that they aren’t there to be rock stars.

Their next wedding gig is at a very fancy castle for an upscale wedding. The groom is American and the bride is Irish, and the wedding has been receiving a lot of local attention because one of the groom’s best friends is former boy band superstar Danny Wilson (Nick Jonas), who hasn’t found strong success as a solo artist despite some of his former bandmates doing so. During the band’s performance, the groom asks Rick if Danny can come up on stage and sing a song with him. Rick is hesitant, but the band insists that the bride and groom make the calls, so Danny joins the band onstage and performs “I Wish” by Stevie Wonder. Danny brings Rick in to duet with him and the two have a great performance that the crowd loves. Rick, who initially thought Danny was nothing special, is impressed by him.

After the set, Rick steps out back to smoke a joint and runs into Danny. Danny asks if he can have some, and the two smoke and get to chatting. Danny asks Rick why he stopped playing with his band – Rick explains he still writes but while touring in Ireland he met Rachel and then they started a family. He took a year off and when he returned to his label he was dropped. The two keeping smoking and drinking, and Danny brings Rick into a music production space. Danny plays Rick some samples of the new solo album he’s working on – Rick likes it, but offers Danny some ideas for melody and note changes that Danny really enjoys. Danny is having a hard time launching his solo album and has lots of different directions he wants to go. Rick picks up a guitar and plays Danny some of a song he wrote called “How to Write a Song Without You”, that ends with the line “every song I ever wrote in my life is about you”. As the evening ends, Rick encourages Danny to play the music he wants to play, and Danny tells Rick he is too good for a wedding band and gives him his manager’s card to look him up if he’s in LA. On the way out of the venue, an assistant brings Rick a parting gift from Danny: one of his very expensive guitars.

Danny and Rick’s performance from the wedding goes a little viral. Danny returns to Los Angeles to the mansion he lives in with his girlfriend Marcia (Havana Rose Liu). He plays her some of his new tracks, which she feels are fine. He meets with his manager Mac (Jack Reynor), who has listened to Danny’s new tracks. He likes them but doesn’t think any are strong enough to be a hit single. He tells Danny that he needs to introduce the world to a new Danny, and tells him the internet is joking that he’s a wedding singer. Back in Ireland, Rick plays one of his newest songs for Aja called “Satellite”, about a woman who is lonely and adrift. Aja tells him it feels old – women aren’t lonely anymore. In Los Angeles, Danny sits at his piano and begins playing “How to Write a Song Without You”, which Marcia overhears and begins listening to. She asks who the song is about – when he says it’s about her, she is deeply touched and says it’s the most romantic thing she’s ever heard. She tells him he needs to record it.

Six months later, Rick is at a shopping mall when the music in the background starts to feel familiar to him. He realizes that it is “How to Write a Song Without You”, and rushes home excited to tell his family that he wrote a hit song. They wonder if they’re going to be rich because of it, but Rick doesn’t know. He asks if they remember him playing the song for them, but they don’t – they explain he plays so many samples and demos that it’s hard to remember that specific one. Similarly, his band do not remember the song or him playing it for them. No one seems like they particularly believe Rick, who insists he wrote the songs but can’t find any recordings or demos in his many many music files on his computer. Rick attempts to call Mac with the number from the card Danny gave him, but is unable to get anyone to take him seriously. His daughter urges him to seek legal counsel – he meets with attorneys who tell him without any demos or evidence of the song existing he doesn’t have any recourse.

On the set of the “How to Write a Song Without You” music video shoot, Mac tells Danny about the messages he’s gotten from Rick and asks Danny if there’s any truth to the idea that Rick wrote the song. Danny says he remembers jamming after with Rick, but that he was so high and drunk he doesn’t remember that and says there’s no truth to the idea. Mac then calls Rick and tells him that he asked Danny personally and he denied it – he then threatens Rick that if he continues down this path he will bury him in lawsuits. Meanwhile, “How to Write a Song Without You” goes all the way to number one and Danny’s career skyrockets – he and Marcia break up. Rick becomes angrier and more depressed as more people around him in Ireland make fun of him for claiming to have written the song.

At another wedding gig, one of the brides asks the band to play “How to Write a Song Without You”. Rick bluntly refuses, and Binzer again tells him the client decides and demands they play it. Rick gets into a physical brawl with Binzer, who fires him from the band. Sandy quits in solidarity with Rick. Later, Rick is driving with Rachel and Aja in the car when “How to Write a Song Without You” comes on the radio. Aja likes the song and wants to listen, but Rick angrily changes the station on the dash and in doing so loses control of the car, which careens off the road and flips over. Everyone is injured but okay, and when they get home Rachel tells Rick he needs to leave. She says with him being fired she doesn’t know how they’re going to pay their bills, and tells him to stop dreaming. Rick angrily says he’s tired of living with two women who don’t believe him and storms out, packing a bag and going to stay at Sandy’s. On the way there, he sees a street musician playing “Falling Slowly’, and is angry when two teens steal the tips out of his guitar case. Sandy relays that Aja texted him with a message for Rick – she believes him. Rick resolves to go to Los Angeles and solve this once and for all, and Sandy goes with him.

Danny has thought about the Rick situation, and goes to Mac to suggest that maybe they should just pay Rick. Mac explains that Danny told him to kill the situation and so he did – he explains it would be a really bad look if the story went public. Rick and Sandy go to Danny’s concert at the LA Forum, and afterwards attempt to get into the backstage area – Sandy fakes a phone call to Rick pretending to be Danny, but the security doesn’t buy it. Just as they give up, they run into the bride and groom from the wedding, who offer to give them a ride to the after party at Danny’s house. At the party, Rick and Sandy split up. A beautiful woman hits on Sandy but he is more drawn to one of Danny’s beautiful guitars, which he starts playing. Rick follows Danny and two women up to his balcony where they get in the hot tub. Rick reveals himself and Danny asks the women to leave so they can talk. Rick climbs into the hot tub fully clothed and tells Danny that having a credit on the song would’ve changed his entire life forever, and demands Danny admit he wrote the song. Danny seems to give, and Rick insists he knew he wasn’t crazy and wants to know why he’s done this. Danny attempts to leave and in trying to stop him Rick accidentally pushes him over the balcony. Mac begins coming upstairs and Rick jumps over the balcony as well.

Both bloody and disheveled Danny and Mac continue to fight on the street. Rick tells Danny that he knows he could never have written the song, and that they both know it. Danny wants to know why, and Rick explains that the song was never a love song – he wrote it about his daughter after she was born. That he was so scared about giving up the band for his family but he stayed and it’s the best thing he’s ever done, and that’s where the song comes from. Rick tells Danny how disappointed he was, how he liked Danny and thought Danny seemed real. Danny tells Rick he doesn’t know how much pressure he is under, and he wanted so badly to create something real. Security arrives and Rick and Sandy flee, and Rick tells Sandy he got what he needed. Back in Dublin, Rick returns home where Rachel asks him if he got Danny to admit it. Rick is surprised that Rachel believes he wrote the song – she tells hims he does, and that they got robbed, and sometimes that’s what happens. They reconcile, and Rick goes back to Binzer to ask for his job back. The band brings him back, and at their next performance, “How to Write a Song Without You” is requested. Rick tells the crowd it’s not about what the song is about, but it’s about who’s listening.

Aja looks at old photos on her dad’s computer, and finds a video from one of her youngest birthdays. In the background, Rick is playing the piano… and Aja hears that it is a few lines from “How to Write a Song Without You”. She is thrilled, and excitedly runs to tell her mom. Some time later, Rick again walks by the street musician, and this time leaves a massive wad of bills inside his guitar case – it seems like he got the royalties from the song. Rick’s original music begins playing, the song is about Dublin to LA, indicating that he’s returned to making his own original music.

wiki_plot.text:
Rick Power is the American lead singer in a Dublin-based wedding band, The Bride and Groove, who has given up his dreams of musical stardom after marrying his Irish girlfriend, Rachel, and having a daughter, Aja, with her. While performing at a castle wedding, the band meets Danny Wilson, a former boy band member who is struggling to find success as a solo artist. After joining the band onstage, Danny later spends the evening with Rick, during which they drink, smoke marijuana, and share music. Rick performs an original song he wrote, "How to Write a Song (Without You)".

After returning to Los Angeles, Danny struggles to find material for his solo album, and his producer, Mac, criticizes his songs as generic. Trying to find inspiration, Danny plays Rick's song which his girlfriend, Marcia, overhears and encourages him to record and release. Six months later, the song becomes a major hit and revives Danny's career. After hearing it while shopping, Rick attempts to convince others that he wrote the song, but is unable to prove it. Danny's record label dismisses Rick's claims and threatens legal action if he continues contacting them.

When a bride requests the song at a wedding, Rick refuses to perform it and is fired from the band after attacking the drummer. After crashing his van with Rachel and Aja both inside, Rachel kicks him out of the house. Desperate to receive credit, Rick convinces his bandmate, Sandy, to come with him to Los Angeles. The two attend Danny's concert at the L.A. Forum and sneak into the afterparty at his home. Rick confronts Danny and demands recognition for writing the song, but Danny refuses. Rick reveals that the song is not a love song, but a song written for Aja about fatherhood. Rick and Sandy are then kicked out of the party.

Returning to Ireland, Rick accepts that he is unlikely to receive credit and reconciles with his family and rejoins The Bride and Groove. Later, Rick and Danny each perform the song separately, Rick at a wedding, and Danny at Madison Square Garden. While looking through old photographs and videos on Rick's computer, Aja discovers a home video from when she was two years old that shows Rick singing the song to her, providing proof that he wrote the song. Several months later, Rick donates a large amount of money to a busker, showing that he was finally compensated for his work.

spoiler_text.text:
Los Angeles, California, 2006 – Chris Hansen (Robert Pattinson) is rehearsing in front of a mirror before getting ready for a sting operation for his program, “To Catch A Predator”. He joins his producer Andie Bender (Merritt Wever) and the rest of the crew while decoy actor Del Harvey (Phoebe Bridgers) meets their target, a divorced father (Tony Revolori). Del poses as a 13-year-old and leaves the man alone before Hansen comes out and reveals that the man is being exposed for his pedophilia. The man breaks down in tears as the crew comes out. Hansen lets the man walk out the door before police swarm and arrest him.

Elsewhere in California, Dan Plum (Skyler Gisondo) is a struggling actor. After a failed audition, he studies Billy Bob Thornton’s interview on “Inside The Actors Studio” to get an idea on how to improve his skills.

“To Catch A Predator” has successfully exposed sex offenders and pedophiles, with at least one fan (Creed Bratton) expressing to Hansen that he wishes those people would die, but Hansen thinks his shows does worse for those men. While working on the show, Hansen often obsesses with getting the perfect shot or take, often frustrating the crew (especially Andie) with his perfectionism. They also work with an anti-pedophile vigilante group, Perverted-Justice, led by Xavier Von Erck (Matthew Maher), who poses as teens to lure the predators out.

Hansen and Andie meet with Jeff Zucker (playing himself), who isn’t a fan of “Predator” but decides to move the show to a primetime spot at NBC to compete with ABC’s “Lost”. Hansen is excited and goes home to tell his wife Mary (Anna Faris) and their sons Connor and Chase (Franco and Luca Brocato).

Dan is flown out to work on the show as a new decoy actor. He shows up late for their shoot, while Del refuses to go out for the decoy because she discovered that their merchandise website has crude products. Dan arrives and gets set up by Andie to pose as a teenage boy. The predator (Jonathan Lipnicki) arrives at the house and exposes himself to Dan before putting whipped cream on his genitals. Dan is freaked out before Hansen emerges. Hansen later joins Dan for a drink to tell him that his work is like being a superhero. Dan later starts to get used to the job as they film more stings and catch more creeps.

Hansen goes to a hotel to meet with a woman named Krysten (Caroline Hebert), with whom he is having an affair. He wants to break things off with her, which makes Krysten cry. Hansen tries to comfort her, and she starts sucking his thumb. Someone in the corner starts taking pictures of them.

A reporter from the National Enquirer calls Hansen, informing him he’s got pictures of Hansen with Krysten. He asks for comments from Hansen, or else he threatens to expose him to his family. Hansen refuses to give him anything.

The crew starts to work with the Rockwall County Police Department, and their Chief Cortland Gunn (Bokeem Woodbine). During another taping of “To Catch A Predator”, Dan plays a decoy to a man who says he is a rabbi. When Hansen steps out to confront him, the man doesn’t listen to him as quickly as the other predators usually do, and he even appears to intimidate Hansen by making it seem like he’s in the wrong for exposing him.

Andie is called by a woman named Patty Patterson (Jessica Hecht), who works with John Quiñones for the show “What Would You Do?”, which is partially inspired by “Predator’s” success. Patty wants to poach Andie for a position on the show, though Andie does not immediately give her a response.

Dan talks to a friend, Troy (Eric Rahill), who saw an ad for his appearance on “Predator”. While Troy expresses pride because Dan is his friend, he says the clip is too short to give his career any kind of boost. Dan makes a defensive comment to Troy before hanging up and going to find Hansen. When Dan expresses his concerns over his job, Hansen tells Dan about his time in India while covering a story on child disappearances, which is where he got a bracelet that he wears the whole time. During his investigation, he recalls hearing about a figure in the area who was supposedly responsible for the missing kids, and he is represented as a horrific masked figure. Hansen likens what the show does as “cleansing the world of an ancient evil”.

While on another sting, Andie finds out that hackers spread info to the other predators that the house they are using is working with police. The car that arrives at the house ends up driving away after they realize something is up. Another car pulls up, but Hansen appears to shut down after being compromised. Dan steps in as the predator, a man with cerebral palsy, comes to the house. Dan talks to him the way Hansen talks to others before he gets arrested.

Andie briefly considers joining “What Would You Do?” because of Hansen’s increasingly erratic behavior. However, she ultimately calls Patty to tell her she will not be joining them.

Xavier brings up how he was talking to someone in a chatroom who slipped up and said they were going to a wake in Denton, Texas. The only wake happening was for a high profile senator. After getting the predator’s number, it gets traced back to Bill Conradt (Alex Winter), a district attorney that Gunn personally knows. The crew gets Dan to call Conradt, and Gunn recognizes his voice on the other end, which enrages him.

Hansen gets a call from Mary, who says she was contacted by the National Enquirer about the photos. Although Hansen tries to explain himself, Mary hangs up on him.

Despite waiting for the predators to come to them, Hansen goes ahead with leading a sting straight to Conradt’s house. Dan keeps Conradt on the phone, singing a song from “Rent” to him. Hansen sees Conradt from his window as police move in on him. As the light shines on Conradt’s face, he takes out a gun and shoots himself in the head. The crew is shocked, especially Dan. Andie tries to salvage the episode by talking to police. Dan is mortified by the ordeal and leaves the area without a word. Hansen stands tearfully outside Conradt’s house, repeating his catchphrases to himself, while the masked figure from India appears to lurk in the bushes.

One year later, Dan is living somewhere else. A neighbor brings him his mail after a mix-up. Dan opens it to find that he has finally received his card to join the Screen Actors Guild.

wiki_plot.text:
In 2006, journalist Chris Hansen hosts To Catch a Predator, a Dateline NBC series in which he conducts sting operations with the anti-pedophilia vigilante group Perverted-Justice. They lure would-be child predators, expecting to engage in sex with minors, played by decoy actors of legal age, to houses where Hansen and his camera crew confront them before they are arrested. To Catch a Predator is a ratings success, and NBC's head Jeff Zucker, despite not liking the show, places it in the primetime slot to compete with ABC's hit show Lost.

Dan Plum, an aspiring actor seeking credits for membership in the Screen Actors Guild (SAG), is cast as one of To Catch a Predator's decoys. Although he is initially disturbed by the shooting process, he acclimates and comes to admire Hansen. Hansen breaks off an extramarital affair with a younger woman at a restaurant, unaware he is being photographed. A National Enquirer reporter begins calling Hansen for comment on an upcoming story about the affair.

Disturbed by the threat of his affair going public and under pressure to maintain the show's ratings, Hansen becomes consumed in making To Catch a Predator a commercial success. An ABC executive attempts to poach Hansen's producer Andie Bender for What Would You Do?, a reality television series inspired by To Catch a Predator. Andie declines, but reconsiders as Hansen's behavior grows increasingly erratic. Dan confides to Hansen his worries that To Catch a Predator will not advance his career. Hansen tells Dan that their work is "cleansing the world of an ancient evil" and recounts his time in Pandalam, India investigating the mysterious disappearance of children where he was told of this "ancient evil" retreating into a cave after the villagers resorted to killing one another out of desperation.

After receiving a letter from a fan in Murphy, Texas, Perverted-Justice founder Xavier Von Erck begins searching for pedophiles in the area. He finds a prospective predator who covers their tracks diligently and, upon discovering they are attending a wake for a Texas state senator in Denton, excitedly surmises that they may be a government official. Under pressure from NBC to improve ratings and eager to catch a high-profile "whale", Hansen cancels an upcoming shoot in New Jersey over Andie's objections and takes the To Catch a Predator team to Texas.

The "whale" is reluctant to meet in person, but gives their phone number, exposing their identity as Bill Conradt, an assistant district attorney for Rockwall County. Andie, reinvigorated, tells ABC she will not join What Would You Do?. Forgoing the usual protocol, Hansen decides to confront Conradt at his house, which heavily armed police officers surround. Hansen receives a call from his wife, who tells him the National Enquirer called her for comment about his affair.

As Hansen and the police prepare to move in, Conradt glares through a window at Hansen, who sees Conradt as the manifestation of the "ancient evil" from his trip to India, before Conradt shoots himself. Andie is disappointed they could not interview Conradt but plans to interview the police officers to salvage the episode. Hansen cries while repeating the chat logs before uttering his catchphrase "What would have happened if I wasn't here?" as he sees the "ancient evil" escape back into the woods. A shaken Dan walks away from the scene; a year later, living in Mesa, Arizona, he receives his SAG membership card in the mail.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens on a spacecraft. A man named Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) wakes up from a coma. He struggles to get himself on his feet again and has no memory of how he got there. The only other two crew members onboard, Captain Yao Li-Jae (Ken Leung) and engineer Olesya Ilyukhina (Milana Vayntrub) are both dead. He looks out his window and sees he is somewhere up in space, in a star system far from Earth. Grace estimates it will take him roughly thirteen years to return home.

Some of Grace’s memories slowly come back. He was a middle school teacher, explaining to his students that there is an infrared line going from the sun to Venus, called the “Petrova Line”, and how the Astrophage emitted by the Line is dimming the sun and will slowly cool the planet to dangerous levels. He assures his students that the best minds in the world are working to resolve the issue.

A government agent named Eva Stratt (Sandra Huller) visits Grace over his work on the Petrova Line. Knowing that there is a credible threat to the Earth’s sun, she brings Grace in to do some research with some samples of Astrophage gathered. After a few failures, Grace learns that the Astrophage is a cell. It dies after some exposure but Grace deduces it’s made entirely of water. Further research shows that the Astrophage comes from Venus via the planet’s carbon dioxide and taking energy from the sun.

Grace reports to Stratt for Astrophage replication since it is considered a viable fuel source. She brings him before a council of other scientists as she explains to him that she is bringing him onboard “Project Hail Mary”. The issue is that other stars are being affected by Astrophage, except for one: Tau Ceti. The mission is to go there on a one-way trip and find a way to handle the Astrophage that is affecting the stars, on what is essentially a suicide mission.

Back in the present, Grace eulogizes Yao and Ilyukhina before ejecting their bodies into space. After an issue with the ship’s controls, Grace approaches Tau Ceti and sees the Petrova Line as close as he can. He then sees a gigantic alien spacecraft before him. The spacecraft sends a container toward Grace’s ship, which he catches and brings onboard after determining it is not dangerous. Inside is a model made by the ship’s inhabitant depicting a sort of map of the star system, indicating its origin is from 40 Eridani.

The spacecraft produces a tunnel made of an element known as xenonite, allowing Grace to cross over in his suit. He meets a rock-like alien that mimics his movements and also made a small figure based off Grace (raising his hand in triumph catching the previous container). Grace names the alien “Rocky” (voice of James Ortiz) and creates a voice modulator to translate Rocky’s speech to English for them to communicate since Rocky’s species sees via echolocation. Grace learns that Rocky was part of a crew of 23 Eridians and is also the sole survivor. They make a pact to save the stars together.

A flashback shows Stratt introducing Grace to Yao, Ilyukhina, and lead scientist Dr. Martin DuBois (Malachi Kirby) prior to the mission, as well as their backups. They are all aware of the fate that awaits them but tell Grace they have methods of death they can choose from. They witness the power of the 1099 spin drives powered by the Astrophage on the Hail Mary ship by showing how it melts a ton of metal. Grace tells Yao that he doesn’t think he has the “bravery genes” that they do, but Yao says one just needs to find someone to be brave for.

Present – Grace brings Rocky onto his ship as he walks around in a small type of spacesuit to adjust to Grace’s atmosphere. Grace documents his time with Rocky as his new “roommate”. They work together to collect a sample of Astrophage to figure out why it’s not affecting Tau Ceti. Grace also shows Rocky aspects of Earth culture, though he starts to open up and admits that he didn’t have anybody back on Earth, while Rocky had a mate back on his planet. Another flashback shows how lonely he felt on Earth among the crew, who all had partners of their own. After a talk with Stratt, she goes up to sing “Sign of the Times” for karaoke to the crew, to their astonishment.

Grace and Rocky make it close enough to Tau Ceti’s surface that Grace finds himself in the Petrova Line. They approach the planet Tau Ceti-e, which they rename “Adrian” (to keep the “Rocky” theme going). Grace recovers a sample of the organism that eats Astrophage, which is a bacteria that he calls “Taumoeba” produced by the life that exists on Adrian. When Grace tells Rocky that he is not getting home, Rocky offers to give him the Astrophage he needs to help him get home, even if it means Rocky will get home much slower than anticipated. This makes Grace emotional, and he introduces Rocky to a hug.

Flashback – Grace and Stratt are admiring the ship for the mission, until an explosion breaks out as a result of mishandling the Astrophage. DuBois and the backups are killed. Stratt wants Grace to go in place of the dead scientists, but Grace doubts that he is capable of pulling it off. She gives him time to think it over.

Present – Grace and Rocky move above Adrian’s atmosphere to get a sample of the Taumoeba, but a fuel leak breaks out and causes damage to the Hail Mary. While trying to get a handle on the situation, Grace gets knocked out after slamming against the controls. Rocky gets out of his spacesuit to protect Grace, though it causes him severe damage.

Grace wakes up and finds Rocky injured. He gets him somewhere to regulate his temperature so he can recover. During this time, Grace works to breed the Taumoeba to use against the Astrophage. Rocky wakes up, and he and Grace celebrate their discoveries. Eventually, the time comes for the two to part ways, though it is clear that neither wants to go. They acknowledge their friendship and head home.

One last flashback shows Grace coming to Stratt with his decision, which is to not join the mission despite understanding how high the stakes are. With no choice left, Stratt has Grace drugged and put on the ship, which explains why he had no memory of being on the Hail Mary.

En route back to Earth, the Taumoeba starts to eat through the xenonite containers and is eating the Astrophage on the Hail Mary. Grace manages to get his situation under control, but he realizes that the Taumoeba will eat through Rocky’s ship since it is entirely made of xenonite, and if that doesn’t kill him, extreme radiation exposure will. Knowing he only has enough fuel for one option (go home or save Rocky), Grace decides to rescue his friend. He sends probes filled with Taumoeba back to Earth and goes to reunite with Rocky.

The probes successfully land on Earth, and Stratt is seen reviewing Grace’s logs. He and Rocky made it back to Erid, where the Eridians have built a bio-dome for Grace to live in and work as a teacher to the children of that area. Rocky tells Grace that their scientists have made it possible for Grace to return home, but he decides to think it over.

wiki_plot.text:
In the near future, middle school teacher and former molecular biologist Dr. Ryland Grace wakes from an induced coma aboard the interstellar spacecraft Hail Mary, suffering from amnesia. He learns that he is the sole survivor of a three-person crew travelling to the Tau Ceti system, 11.9 light-years from Earth.

In flashbacks, Grace recalls that scientists discovered a "Petrova line" of infrared light between the Sun and Venus. A dark substance in the line, dubbed "astrophage", was proliferating on the Sun, dimming it at a rate that would cause catastrophic global cooling within thirty years. Eva Stratt, head of the Petrova Taskforce, recruited Grace because of his expertise in speculative astrobiology. Grace discovered that astrophage samples consisted of unicellular organisms capable of absorbing electromagnetic radiation from the Sun and expelling it for propulsion.

Grace joined Stratt's Project Hail Mary, an international "long-shot" mission to send a crewed spacecraft to Tau Ceti, using astrophage as fuel. Tau Ceti was the only nearby star not occluded by astrophage. The mission was a suicide mission, as the spacecraft could carry only enough fuel for a one-way journey; any findings would have to be returned by space probes.

In the present, Grace encounters an alien spacecraft that docks with the Hail Mary. Made from a solid form of xenon, which Grace calls "xenonite", it carries a rock-like, five-legged alien from Erid, a planet in the 40 Eridani A system. Grace names the alien "Rocky", deduces that Eridians perceive their surroundings through echolocation, and develops a machine translation system to interpret Rocky's musical language. Rocky is a mechanical engineer, and the sole survivor of the Eridians' mission to save their own star from astrophage. Rocky and Grace agree to collaborate, and soon become close friends. As neither can survive the other's atmosphere, Rocky and Grace construct pressurized xenonite chambers inside the Hail Mary for Rocky to work in. 

Grace and Rocky investigate the Petrova line around Tau Ceti e, which Grace names "Adrian" after the name he gave to Rocky's Eridian mate. They discover a microbial biosphere in the line; Rocky theorises that other organisms further down in Adrian's atmosphere keep the astrophage population in check. After learning that Grace cannot return home, Rocky offers to share some of his astrophage fuel with the Hail Mary. Grace then remembers that an astrophage explosion killed the original crew's science officers, and that Stratt recruited him when no replacements could be trained in time.

During a risky maneuver to collect the astrophage's predator, a fuel leak causes the Hail Mary to spin uncontrollably, knocking Grace unconscious. Rocky enters Grace's atmosphere to save him, but is badly injured. While Rocky recovers, Grace studies the captured predator, names it "taumoeba" and selectively breeds it to survive in the nitrogen-rich atmosphere of Venus. After Rocky recovers, the pair celebrate their success. Grace then remembers that he initially refused to join the mission, but Stratt had him drugged and put aboard the ship, believing he was the only person capable of completing it.

Grace and Rocky part ways to return home. Soon afterwards, Grace discovers that the taumoeba has escaped its xenonite breeding tanks and begun consuming the Hail Mary's astrophage fuel. Although he contains the outbreak, he realises that Rocky's xenonite ship cannot contain the organism and will eventually lose all its fuel, stranding Rocky and dooming Erid. Grace chooses to sacrifice his remaining fuel to rescue Rocky and the Eridians, sending his video logs and taumoeba samples to Earth by probe.

Stratt and her team receive the probes, and use the taumoeba to cure the Sun's astrophage infection. On Erid, Grace lives in an Earth-like biodome built for him by the Eridians. Rocky tells him that Eridian scientists can prepare the Hail Mary for a return voyage to Earth. Grace considers this before beginning another day teaching science to enthusiastic Eridian children.

wiki_plot.text:
At the end of the Thirty Years' War, a former soldier arrives in a remote Protestant village and lays claim to a neglected estate as its long-missing heir. Unbeknownst to the villagers, the soldier is in fact Rose, a woman who has been posing as a man for years and has assumed the identity of a fellow soldier killed during the war. 

Rose works tirelessly to rebuild the farm and gradually earns the respect of the community. Her reputation grows when she shoots dead a bear, saving the life of a villager in the process. Desiring to expand, Rose offers to purchase a patch of land by a stream from a prominent local farmer. The farmer, unwilling to sell, grants her access to the land on the condition that she marries his eldest daughter, Suzanna, to which Rose agrees. Rose's unwillingness to consummate the marriage upsets both Suzanna and her father. She later resorts to using a makeshift strap-on dildo without Suzanna's knowledge, and is surprised when Suzanna announces her pregnancy.

While the birth of a child appears to secure the family's future, an accident occurs one summer when Rose is badly stung while beekeeping, leaving her bed-bound for an extended period. When checking her body for injuries, Suzanna and a maid discover that Rose is a woman. Rose reveals the truth of her life to Suzanna, who, out of genuine care for Rose and unwilling to give up her own newfound freedom, elects to maintain the appearance of a marriage. The maid on the other hand informs the villagers, leading to a confrontation at Rose's farmhouse. The two women are forced to flee with the child but are quickly apprehended.

A bailiff is dispatched to the village to conduct an investigation, during which Rose defends her desire for freedom to no avail. Suzanna is ultimately sentenced to death by drowning for fraud and adultery. Rose is sentenced to death by beheading, though her execution is postponed until she could give birth following her rape by four men. During the reprieve, Rose decides to write down her own life story.
