spoiler_text.text:
The film opens with Peter Parker (Tom Holland) writing a letter to MJ (Zendaya), hoping that he may one day give it to her and explain what happened between them. After having Dr. Strange cast a spell to make everyone forget about his existence, Peter has become Spider-Man full time, taking on villains like Mac Gargan/Scorpion (Michael Mando), Tombstone (Marvin “Krondon” Jones III), Boomerang, Tarantula, and The Hand, and working alongside Detective Jean DeWolff (Liza Colon-Zayas). Over the next four years, he watches MJ and Ned (Jacob Batalon) from afar as they go to MIT together.

Spider-Man chases after a runaway tank in Manhattan. Also pursuing the tank is Frank Castle/The Punisher (Jon Bernthal). Spidey knocks Frank out of his vehicle and stops him from following. The tank makes its way towards the Department of Damage Control. Spidey is unable to stop it from crashing through the building. When he opens the tank, he is surprised to find an old woman in there. Someone controlling her telepathically mind jumps from her body to a guard’s body, and Spidey notices. He chases the Mind Jumper to the rooftop, but he is too late, as the Telepath makes a guard direct an escort team to take Scorpion to Bellevue instead of The Raft. Before the Telepath escapes, they let Spider-Man know there is a bomb in the tank, which he is too late to stop from detonating, but the building is evacuated before it goes off.

DeWolff informs Spidey that Scorpion was let out from Bellevue. In order to get a lead on the mysterious villain behind this, Peter pays a visit to a Russian bathhouse, where he meets Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh). She makes him get in by taking off his suit (but not the mask). Yelena says that Damage Control has been attacked four times lately, and someone is looking for something called “V-Max”.

Spider-Man visits the DODC, where he meets the head of the place, Bill Metzger (Tramell Tillman). He discovers that The Hand’s ninjas are working for them. Metzger doesn’t know who is behind the attacks or what “V-Max” is, but Spidey knows that whatever they want is hidden behind a giant vault in the building.

Peter is at a shop, talking to DeWolff on the phone over what he’s learned, but he sees Ned and follows him to his and MJ’s apartment, where they are hosting a party. Peter sees Ned’s wall of Spider-Man theories, including his belief that Spidey is either Flash Thompson or their old teacher Roger Harrington. He has also developed a “Spidey Tracker” app to keep tabs on where the Wall Crawler may be. Peter sees MJ and gives her flowers that he meant to bring to Aunt May’s (Marisa Tomei) grave. He leaves when he sees MJ kiss another guy, and he swings home sadly. When Peter gets home, he experiences something painful before passing out.

Peter wakes up in a web cocoon outside the apartment. He discovers that he now has organic webbing, and that his web cartridges don’t work. He uses his A.I. assistant, E.V. (Naomi Watts), to determine that he is going through changes in his body and DNA, as his arachnid genes are developing and causing him sensory overload.

Once Spidey gets the hang of things (sort of), he goes after Scorpion, who is attacking the DODC downtown. Spider-Man fights him but is losing until he lets the arachnid genes take over. He grabs Scorpion and thrashes him around, but he slams the villain onto a cop car and severely injures the officer inside. After ripping off Scorpion’s tail, Spidey sees he was controlled by the Telepath Peter is horrified at what he did.

Peter goes to a college campus to find Dr. Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo), who is teaching a physics class, but all his students only want to ask Avengers-related questions. When the students leave, Peter approaches Bruce since he now wears an inhibitor on his wrist to stop him from becoming Hulk. Peter asks for advice on creating an inhibitor, as well as a universal one that affects everyone. Peter goes home to work on one for himself, and then another for the Telepath.

The Telepath finds Peter and taunts him by saying they are going after MJ. Spider-Man swings through the city, tracking everyone who appears to be mind-jumped, and based on his scans, he finds that the Telepath has a range limit of about 33 feet. When they control a helicopter pilot, Spidey webs the chopper up to stop them from getting anyone else.

Spidey goes to MJ’s apartment and convinces her that she needs to go with him. They stop on a rooftop, where it seems as though MJ might remember who Spider-Man really is. She takes off his mask and kisses him, and it seems as though her memories come back…until it turns out to be the Telepath playing a cruel trick on him. The Telepath makes MJ walk off the building. Spidey catches her, but she falls unconscious. Peter surrenders when the Telepath approaches him as another man, but he catches a glimpse of the Telepath in a car, who turns out to be a teenage girl (Sadie Sink).

Spider-Man brings MJ to Frank’s hideout, which is laced with booby traps that Spidey has to protect MJ from. After some bickering, Frank agrees to let MJ stay there for a while. Spidey scans the Telepath’s face and finds that much of the information on her has been scrubbed, but he did get a name: JEAN. ELAINE. GREY. After MJ suggests a way for Spidey to use his inhibitor properly (it overheated the first time), he works on the one he plans to use on Jean. He and Frank also have an argument because Spidey doesn’t think Frank ever had anyone to care about, seemingly unaware of Frank’s own tragic past and what happened with his family.

Spider-Man heads to the DODC when Jean attacks the place again. MJ convinces Frank to go help him. Metzger gathers his people in a safe room when something starts trying to smash into the vault. Spidey arrives and finds that Jean is controlling Bruce after removing his inhibitor, and he is back to his Hulk form (or at least, his Professor Hulk form). Frank arrives to shoot at Hulk, but they manage to get Jean out of his head. However, Bruce says that something in him broke, and he turns into an even more gigantic Hulk (Savage Hulk). Spidey does his best to stop Hulk from causing too much damage, even stopping a ton of debris from hitting the ground below. Hulk manages to snap out of it when Spidey reminds him they are friends, and he is incapacitated. Unfortunately, Jean manages to get in Frank’s head and uses his explosives to blow up the vault. Spidey gets in there before Jean can kill Metzger and uses the inhibitor to get her out of Frank’s head. Metzger shoots Jean with a tranquilizer dart. Before losing consciousness, Jean simply mutters “Sara…”

Bruce is taken to a hospital, while Metzger thanks Spidey for saving them, and Damage Control takes Jean into custody. When Spidey mentions Sara, Metzger says that Jean entered his mind and saw a memory of a coworker named Sara who died recently.

Spidey swings back to Frank’s hideout, only to discover that MJ found his letter. This forces him to admit who he is and the past that they had together. Peter tells MJ he loves her, but she says she does not feel the same because she has absolutely no memories of them together. Peter is heartbroken but understands. He takes MJ home, and she lets him go “meet” Ned, who is excited to meet his hero. While talking, MJ mentions that she had no memory of being possessed by Jean when she kissed Peter, which makes Peter realize Metzger was lying about Jean entering his mind and seeing a memory. Spider-Man contacts Yelena again, who finds that a lot of info on Jean was scrubbed by Damage Control, but she tells Peter that Sara was Jean’s sister. Spidey realizes Jean is in danger.

As Jean is being held at the DODC, a flashback shows her with Sara (Olivia Booth-Ford). They were abandoned by their mother after their mutant powers developed, but Sara showed Jean how to mind jump between people. Jean watched as a team of Damage Control agents led by Metzger showed up to arrest Sara. When Jean tried to save her, Sara stopped her from doing so.

Metzger has Jean strapped to a chair and begins to activate a device to see how far Jean’s range can go. In the room, Jean discovers that “V-Max” is really something Sara saw in the room from the ventilation system. Jean realizes Sara is dead from the experiments, and she removes her inhibitor, allowing her powers to expand as she sends a psionic wave across the city that leaves almost all of New York frozen, including MJ and Ned. Frank is just outside the range, and he plans to use a sniper rifle to take Jean out. Spidey arrives at DODC and is confronted by The Hand’s ninjas, all controlled by Jean. They overpower him until he takes off his inhibitor and accepts his enhanced genes, declaring to Jean that he can be both Peter Parker AND Spider-Man. Spidey defeats The Hand and some Damage Control guards in a spectacular fashion before breaking into Jean’s room.

Jean has shards of glass aimed at Metzger, while Frank sets up his sniper position. Peter allows Jean to enter his mind so that she sees a memory of May talking to Peter. Jean then sits in his place so that it seems like May is talking to her and assuring her that she is not alone. Peter then talks to Jean, and she understands that he has lost someone like she did. Jean lets go of her anger, but Frank fires his shot. Peter moves Jean out of the way and takes the shot himself. Jean uses her powers to keep him alive while Frank heads over and rushes him to the hospital. All of New York waits anxiously to learn if their hero is okay.

Peter wakes up with Frank by his side. He is remorseful for getting Peter hurt, but he admits that the two of them are friends. Frank lets Peter slip out while he puts on Spidey’s mask and gloves to stand out the window and address the crowd of fans. Peter is touched by the love everyone has for Spider-Man. In MJ’s apartment, she is still wearing the Black Dahlia necklace that Peter gave her a long time ago, and she starts to smile.

Jean takes a bus out of the city. Peter talks to DeWolff, who says that Metzger is missing but the police are investigating Damage Control. She also expresses happiness that Spidey is not so alone anymore but also encourages him to rest. Peter then sees Ned and approaches him. He does their secret handshake, and it seems as though Ned’s memories of Peter are starting to come back.

After the credits, we see Ned’s Spidey Tracker app losing a signal of Spider-Man on Earth. It then moves to the far reaches of outer space, where the signal picks back up. The final text promises “Spider-Man will return”.

wiki_plot.text:
After Dr. Stephen Strange's magic spell makes the world forget that Peter Parker exists, he chooses to protect his girlfriend Michelle "MJ" Jones-Watson and best friend Ned Leeds by not reintroducing himself to them. Over the next four years, Parker anonymously protects New York City as its celebrated hero Spider-Man. He defeats major criminals, including Mac Gargan and the Hand ninjas, earning the trust of police detective Jean DeWolff. Parker regularly visits his aunt May's grave.

Parker stops Frank Castle from causing collateral damage in pursuit of an armored personnel carrier that crashes into a Department of Damage Control (DODC) prison. The driver is possessed by a telepath who body hops from person to person to help Gargan escape, but is unable to enter Parker's mind. Yelena Belova informs Parker that multiple DODC facilities have been attacked by someone searching for "V-Max". DODC director Bill Metzger, now using the Hand for security, denies any knowledge of "V-Max" to Parker.

Ned and MJ move back to New York after graduating from MIT. Parker encounters them and sees MJ kiss her new boyfriend. Returning home in distress, he wakes up the next day with heightened senses and spinnerets in his wrists. When the telepath attacks another DODC facility with a possessed Gargan, Parker loses control of his new abilities and brutally beats Gargan, inadvertently injuring a police officer. After DeWolff tells him to regain control, Parker learns from Bruce Banner, who has an inhibitor device that uses siRNA to suppress his super-powered alter ego, the Hulk, and builds his own inhibitor. While he tests it, the telepath finds his apartment and learns about MJ from an unsent reintroduction letter he wrote to her. Parker races to get MJ to safety, but the telepath possesses and almost kills her. He rescues MJ and identifies the telepath as teenager Jean Grey.

Parker takes MJ to Castle's hideout for protection, where she helps complete his inhibitor and a universal inhibitor. Jean attacks the DODC's headquarters with a possessed Banner, whose inhibitor is removed, causing him to become the Hulk. While Parker fights the Hulk, Jean possesses Castle to open a vault hiding DODC agents. Parker calms the Hulk, then blocks Jean's powers with the universal inhibitor while Metzger tranquilizes her. Jean mentions "Sara" before losing consciousness; Metzger claims he remembers thinking of a colleague by that name while possessed by Jean. Parker returns to MJ, who has found the letter. He apologizes for not telling her and declares his love, but MJ does not remember him nor reciprocate his feelings. Despite this, she invites him to her and Ned's apartment, where a masked Parker bonds with them both. After MJ describes not remembering anything while possessed, Parker realizes Metzger lied. Parker contacts Yelena, who learns from redacted DODC files that Sara is Jean's sister, another telepath kidnapped by the DODC.

Metzger experiments on Jean at a DODC facility on Roosevelt Island that Parker infiltrates. Jean deduces that "V-Max" is the weathered label on the air vent in her cell, the last thing Sara saw—and mentally communicated to Jean—before she died. Enraged, Jean creates a psionic field that extends beyond the facility, freezing everyone within it except for Parker, including MJ and Ned. Jean rebuffs Parker's apologies and attacks him using the Hand. He removes his inhibitor and embraces his new abilities, defeating the Hand and stopping Jean from killing Metzger. Parker lets her enter his mind, where she experiences a memory of May saying she loves him for who he is. Parker and Jean reconcile over their respective losses. Parker senses Castle shooting at Jean from a distance and shields her, sustaining a critical injury. Jean drops the psionic field.

Parker wakes up in a hospital with a remorseful Castle, who says Jean remotely kept him alive with her powers. Jean leaves the city, Metzger disappears, and the DODC comes under investigation. At May's grave, Parker vows to stop trying to do everything alone, later agreeing to let DeWolff handle a robbery while he recovers. Seeing Ned again, Parker reintroduces himself with their old handshake.
wiki_plot.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day

wiki_plot.text: When Alzheimer's disease begins to strip away Midge's vibrant personality, her daughter Sarah, a headstrong young woman, is forced to return to her oddball family in the conservative small town she recently fled in order to care for her. She quickly realizes she must accept the cruel and warped reality of the disease — and the imperfect beauty of her family — in order to become the daughter they need.

wiki_plot.text:
Camp Miasma is a long-running slasher franchise that originated in 1983. Its recurring villain is "Little Death", the ghost of a child who in life transformed from a boy to a girl at weekly intervals. After being drowned by hateful campers, Little Death periodically rises from the lake that borders Camp Miasma and uses a spear to slaughter everyone they find. Though the series' earlier installments were successful, a spate of low-quality, unprofitable sequels has left it in limbo.

Queer filmmaker Kris Williams is hired to direct a reboot of Camp Miasma. Though she knows she has been selected to make the franchise's transphobic premise more palatable to a modern audience, Kris feels genuine attachment to the series, owing to her childhood experiences watching it. She is particularly interested in casting Billy Presley, an actress who abruptly retired after playing a camp counselor in the original film. She travels to the Pacific Northwest to meet with Billy, who, she discovers, lives on the abandoned campgrounds used to film the series. Billy is warm, perceptive, and obsessed with Little Death. Kris quickly opens up to her, discussing her dissatisfaction in her polyamorous relationship. Billy dismisses Kris' overly academic interpretation of the series, but expresses interest in acting again. To her agent's chagrin, Kris becomes convinced that the reboot should star Billy in her original role.

Kris and Billy watch the original Camp Miasma together. Kris knows the film by heart and points out lines and filming techniques while watching—one of these techniques being a split diopter shot—although Billy appears uncomfortable during the screening. Kris is especially fond of an image in a sex scene featuring a close-up of Billy's eye with Little Death reflected in it, but the campgrounds' power goes out just as the shot appears on screen. Kris and Billy return to Billy's house, where Kris initiates sex with Billy before abruptly stopping and lamenting that sex has always been difficult for her to enjoy, and that in order to enjoy it she has to imagine herself as the final girl in a slasher movie. Billy explains that she was sexually assaulted during the filming of the Camp Miasma sex scene, during which she learned to orgasm and enjoy sex by imagining that she is simultaneously herself, and Little Death watching her have sex and stabbing her. Kris admits that she can only enjoy sex if she fantasizes herself as a sexualized final girl. Billy encourages her to explore her fantasies and offers to "make a movie" with Kris.

The next morning, Kris has a pitch meeting with the studio executives. Instead of pitching a film, she explains that Little Death actually resides under the lake and imagines the world through the Camp Miasma films, and everyone, including Kris, are characters in one of their films. She then returns to the camp, where it is suddenly summer and Little Death has begun another killing spree. Billy encourages Kris to assume the role of the final girl. She is chased by Little Death and watches him kill her partner, agent, and the studio executives. Finally, Kris is chased to a cabin where Billy awaits. As the two have sex, Little Death approaches them; Kris initially pleads for her life before accepting her fate, appearing to have an orgasm as Little Death spears her and Billy simultaneously. In Little Death's lair under the lake, a VHS copy of a new film called Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma appears.

The following morning, Kris and Billy revive. Still covered in blood, they leave the campgrounds, travel past the carnage left by Little Death, and return to the gas station where the original Camp Miasma began. After buying snacks, Kris repeats the lines spoken by a final girl in an earlier Camp Miasma film, claiming that she can still feel Little Death's presence at the bottom of the lake, where they are waiting to come for them once more. She and Billy smile at one another, before Kris is centered in a split diopter shot with Billy behind her. The two then walk away hand in hand.

spoiler_text.text:
Vassar College, 1975 – A young Anthony Bourdain (Dominic Sessa) is pitching his idea for a novel as he is applying for a fellowship, describing his book as “a conversation between Jack Kerouac and George Orwell”. He also goes by “Tony” and comes off very cocky.

Tony later goes to a bar with a friend and sees his high school crush, Nancy Putkoski (Emilia Jones). He goes to talk to her, though she does not appear impressed with his arrogance. She mentions she is going to spend the summer in Provincetown, Massachussetts.

Tony has dinner with his parents and brother, telling them that he secured the fellowship and that he will be traveling to New York City. He then gets a phone call from the school to inform him that they have picked another student. Frustrated, Tony swipes some cash from his parents and takes a trip to Provincetown.

Upon arriving, Tony goes to a pizza place where he sees Nancy working, but then sees her kissing one of the employees there. Tony goes to a bar/restaurant, The Flagship, and gets drunk. He tries to hit on the bartender Mary (Monica Raymund) before the owner, Chef Jose Vatel (Antonio Banderas), orders Tony to leave for his behavior. Tony gets aggressive and gets thrown out, robbed, and knocked out by one of the cooks, Sal (Leo Woodall).

Tony prepares to head home but discovers he is broke. After Nancy sees him, Tony lies to her about why he is there and says he got the fellowship, so he is there to do some research. He goes back to The Flagship and apologizes to Chef, asking him to crash on his hammock until he’s made enough money to leave.

Chef makes Tony work in the kitchen washing dishes. He works alongside Sal, plus other kitchen workers like Stavros (Stavros Halkias) and Tyrone (Michael Jibrin). They haze him a bit, and Chef usually wakes Tony up by throwing water on him. Tony mentions that he can cook and that his dad is one of the best chefs in Jersey.

Tony and Sal crash a party where Nancy is at. Sal hooks up with one of the girls while Tony continues to talk to Nancy and keep up his lie. He tries to show her how to shuck an oyster and ends up making a mess. When Tony and Sal see Nancy and her boyfriend at a bar later during the week, Sal pushes Tony into the guy and then starts to beat on the guy for no reason, which only drives Nancy away from Tony. Tony bonds more with the kitchen crew and eventually contacts his family to let him know he’s okay.

Sal comes in one morning hungover and presumably coked out. He shows Chef attitude and shoves Tony when he tries to intervene. Chef steps in and Sal punches him, then dares him to strike back, but he doesn’t. Sal just leaves, knowing he’s done.

Tony goes to the pizzeria to apologize to Nancy for what happened, as well as to ask her to take his pictures for his book, because he likes the way she looks at him. Nancy eventually agrees.

Tony starts bonding with Chef, who refers to him as “Flaco”. He makes Tony join him at church and shows him some of his culinary skills. Chef later brings Tony to his house for a drink, and then they hop on a boat to shoot fish and join other fishermen around a bonfire, which is witnessed by Nancy and her friends. When she finds Tony in the kitchen of The Flagship, he lies some more and says that he is doing research for his book. He invites her to have dinner with her friends there on Friday night.

The crew starts serving lobster thermidor. Nancy and her friends show up, and Tony sees that she appears to enjoy his dish. However, a fire breaks out on the stove, and Chef’s fire extinguisher is all out. Tony makes it worse by throwing water on it, and the restaurant is evacuated before it burns down.

A guilty Tony goes home with Nancy. They make out and prepare to have sex, but he comes clean to her about how he was working in the kitchen, that he never got the fellowship, and that he’s only there for her. Nancy kicks him out.

Tony later joins Chef on the beach. He tells Tony he was going to give him a full-time job, but Tony responds poorly about the prospect, leading Chef to telling him he is nothing.

Tony finds Sal and convinces him to steal from Chef’s house while he is away so that he can return to New York. Tony then gets another idea to host a clam bake on the beach. They get donations by saying it’s to repair The Flagship, but Tony decides it should actually be for that. He reconciles with Nancy and Chef at the event, while he and Sal exchange a glance that makes it clear they are done when Sal sees Tony put the donation money away. Nancy also gives Tony the pictures she took of him.

Tony returns to New York and to his family. Nancy returns to college and appears to be missing Tony. The Flagship reopens, and the crew gets back to work. Tony goes for an interview at the Culinary Institute of America, where Chef had graduated from. He gives Tony a recommendation letter for the interview, where Tony addresses himself as Anthony Bourdain.

The final text states that Bourdain worked in kitchens from 1975 to 2002, retiring as Executive Chef of Brasserie Les Halles in New York. He would go on to write “Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly”, a best-selling book. The last we see is a photo of a young Bourdain with two of his coworkers.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1975, a 19-year-old Anthony "Tony" Bourdain is a student at Vassar College. He falsely tells his family and high school love interest Nancy Putkoski that he has received a writing fellowship that would send him to New York City to pursue a career as a writer. When he learns his application was rejected, he impulsively travels to Provincetown, Massachusetts, where Nancy said she was spending the summer. When he discovers Nancy is dating her coworker from a pizza restaurant, he goes to The Flagship, a local seafood restaurant, to drink. While inebriated, he is rude to Mary, the waitress and bartender, and is kicked out and robbed by Sal, one of the restaurant's cooks. While trying to get a ferry ride home, Tony encounters Nancy and falsely tells her he came to Provincetown for research for his fellowship. He accepts her invitation to a party, then returns to The Flagship and appeals to the head chef, who avoids divulging his real name and is referred to only as Chef, for a place to stay. He lies about having restaurant experience and is hired as a dishwasher. 

As months pass, Tony is drawn into the raucous, drug-fueled lifestyle and camaraderie among the Flagship cooks, especially the brash but volatile Sal. He begins to experiment with hard drugs, including cocaine, and Sal revives an old heroin habit. After a violent confrontation with Chef upon arriving late for work, Sal quits. Tony is promoted to replace Sal, under Chef's mentorship. Tony also grows closer to Nancy, but continues to lie about the fellowship even after she discovers that he works in a kitchen.

To impress Nancy, Tony invites her to The Flagship, and convinces Chef to offer lobster thermidor as a special. A grease fire starts, made worse when Tony tries to douse it with water, and consumes The Flagship's interior. That night, when Nancy makes sexual overtures to Tony, he is unable to reciprocate and admits he lied about the fellowship and followed her to Provincetown.

On the beach, Chef tells Tony he was planning to give him a full-time job, then tells the remorseless Tony he won't amount to anything. Tony convinces Sal to steal from Chef's house for money to return to New York, then decides to host a clam bake on the beach. Tony falsely solicits donations for repairs to The Flagship to fund the event, but guiltily donates the proceeds to The Flagship after seeing Nancy, the other cooks, and Chef in attendance. He reconciles with them and agrees to part ways with Sal. 

Tony returns to his family in New York while Nancy returns to college and The Flagship reopens with its original staff. Tony interviews at the Culinary Institute of America, for which Chef, an alumnus, has given Tony a recommendation letter. Following an earlier suggestion by Chef, who had mused that Tony is a childish nickname, Tony introduces himself as Anthony Bourdain.
wiki_plot.title: Tony (2026 film)

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens on an island, where a whole pack of high-tech Buzz Lightyear action figures (all voiced by Tim Allen) have been washed up. One of them wakes up and activates the others. Per their Buzz programming, they believe they are actual space rangers. They see a star in the sky and make it their mission to reach what they believe is Star Command.

A flashback shows Jessie (Joan Cusack) when she was still owned by Emily, her first child. In the present day, Jessie continues to lead Bonnie’s (Scarlett Spears) toys – Buzz, Rex (Wallace Shawn), Hamm (John Ratzenberger), Slinky (Blake Clark) Mr. and Mrs. Potato Head (Jeff Bergman and Anna Vocino), Bullseye, Dolly (Bonnie Hunt), Trixie (Kristen Schaal), Mr. Pricklepants (John Hopkins), Forky (Tony Hale), and Karen Beverly (Melissa Villaseñor). Bonnie acts out a scenario where Forky and Karen Beverly are getting married, and that Rex, the maid of honor, has been poisoned. Bonnie also tries to befriend her twin neighbors, but she is too shy.

Jessie and Bullseye see that the twins are using tablets. She discovers from other discarded toys in the neighborhood that every kid in town has moved on to electronics, while Bonnie is still playing with toys and having a hard time making new friends. Bonnie’s parents (Lori Alan and Jay Hernandez) purchase her a LilyPad (Greta Lee), which poses a threat to the toys.

After Bonnie leaves the room, Jessie tries to interrogate Lily. The toys are impressed with how advanced she is, though she has a smug and snobby attitude. Lily quickly uses her programming to reach out to a group of girls in Bonnie’s dance class, setting up a playdate for the weekend in a matter of seconds.

At night, Jessie feels worried that Lily’s arrival will lead to another Emily scenario where she is given away or put back into storage. Using her walkie-talkie, Jessie is able to contact Woody (Tom Hanks), who is still with Bo (Annie Potts), Duke Caboom (Keanu Reeves), Giggle, Ducky and Bunny in aiding lost toys. Woody rescues a tiny toy named Dr. Nutcase (Matty Matheson), who thinks he’s a goner since tech has taken over. Jessie expresses her fears to Woody, but she hides the walkie from Buzz. Woody mistakenly overhears Jessie and thinks she is asking for his help, so he heads back to Bonnie’s house.

Bonnie gets ready for her sleepover. Jessie and Bullseye sneak into her bag, even though Lily tells them that it would be a bad look for Bonnie to show up with toys. When Bonnie shows up to meet the girls – Chelsea, Kara, and Heidi – they are all playing with their tablets and laugh upon seeing Bonnie with Jessie and Bullseye. She quickly ditches the toys in the car and brings out Lily.

Jessie and Bullseye hop out of Bonnie’s dad’s car and end up on the streets. They are found by an elderly couple, who see that Jessie has Emily’s old home address written on her. They are dropped in the mailbox, but Jessie gets them out. They find a horse named Daffodil and attempt to ride him back into the city, but the horse ends up taking Jessie and Bullseye towards the house’s barn. Bullseye is found by Blaze (Mykal-Michelle Harris), the girl who lives there, while Jessie is left behind.

Woody returns and reunites with his friends after Bo and Duke drop him off. He and Buzz have a minor gripe over who is Jessie’s assigned deputy.

Jessie encounters Blaze’s pet pig, Jimmy Dean, and tries to get him to take her into the house. He does, but rather, to a plastic doll house with Blaze’s old toys. Jessie accidentally wakes up Smarty Pants (Conan O’Brien), a potty-training electronic and the first device that Blaze got, which causes the other toys to resent him. Smarty convinces Jessie to let him tag along as she tries to go into the house to rescue Bullseye.

The army of Buzzes make their way across the land. They find a crane that points them toward the North Star, which they think is Star Command. They end up in the woods, where one Buzz is left behind and taken by two brothers on a camping trip with their parents.

Once inside Blaze’s house, Smarty gets Jessie to replace his batteries (he seems “drunk” on low battery) and then does the same for two of Smarty’s friends, also devices – Atlas (Craig Robinson), a GPS hippo device, and Snappy (Shelby Rabara), a talking camera. Each of them have been around for brief phases in Blaze’s life before being put away. Jessie reluctantly lets them tag along as they make it to Blaze’s room, which Jessie recognizes as previously belonging to Emily. They find Bullseye, who has befriended Blaze’s horse toy collection. Jessie is ready to leave with Bullseye until Blaze comes back to her room. They watch as she reads a message from a classmate who bailed on hanging out with her, leaving Blaze disappointed. After seeing how she is sweet, funny, and imaginative, Jessie decides that Blaze would be a perfect friend for Bonnie.

Bonnie returns to her house in a sour mood. Lily informs the other toys that the other girls were playing Hide and Seek, and they “forgot” to look for Bonnie. Woody and Buzz try to confront Lily, but she sends a text to Bonnie’s dad to place the other toys in the garage. The cowboy and spaceman manage to avoid getting boxed too. They hide and wait for Bonnie to go to sleep so that they can unplug Lily’s charger and leave her with low battery in the morning.

Jessie convinces Blaze’s devices to help arrange a meeting. Snappy takes a picture of her and Bullseye, then uses Smarty to send a message to Bonnie about coming to pick the toys up, with Atlas providing directions. Meanwhile, Lily wakes up groggy on low battery. Woody and Buzz try to get her to say what happened with Jessie and Bullseye, discovering that “Hey Lily” programs her to do whatever they command. They see the message from Blaze’s devices, but in the ensuing scuffle, the message goes out to all of Bonnie’s contacts. Her mom sees the message, which makes Bonnie realize Jessie and Bullseye are missing.

At the camp site, the Buzz army goes to retrieve their comrade. However, they see that he is happy in the care of the brothers, so they leave him alone. They see the nearby laptop with the message from Smarty, and the location star on the map leads them to think this is where Star Command is located, and that Jessie is the leader.

Blaze finds Jessie and acts out a playtime scenario with them, even getting Bullseye to talk (voiced by Alan Cumming). Blaze sees the devices and includes them in a spy movie scenario, leading Smarty, Atlas, and Snappy to feel delighted at being played with for the first time.

Bonnie’s mom drives her to Blaze’s house to pick up the toys, while Woody and Buzz hitch a ride on the car to join them. Unfortunately for Bonnie, the message was also seen by Chelsea, Kara, and Heidi, who all make fun of her in the group chat. This leaves Bonnie humiliated enough that she refuses to pick up Jessie and Bullseye when they get to Blaze’s house. This is seen by Woody and Buzz, who are in disbelief. Jessie is taken back to Blaze’s room, where she snaps at the devices before leaving the room by riding on Daffodil. Bullseye chases after her.

Bonnie’s mom finds out what is troubling her daughter, and they stop for ice cream. Feeling that she has failed Bonnie, Lily puts herself in a donation box, which is taken by a truck.

The Buzzes reach Blaze’s house and capture Woody, thinking he is an enemy until Main Buzz convinces them that Woody is an ally. They use Blaze’s horse toy collection to go after Jessie.

Jessie goes by the old tree where Emily used to swing with her. Bullseye catches up to her, but Jessie still feels like a failure for not being able to help Bonnie. Moments later, she looks around the tree and sees a carving that says “Jessie was here”. Underneath is a lunch box acting as a time capsule full of things that came from after Jessie’s time with Emily. She then sees a picture of an adult Emily with her daughter…who happens to be named JESSIE. Realizing she still held a special place in Emily’s life, Jessie feels better.

Woody, Buzz, and the other Buzzes catch up to Jessie, along with the devices. After Jessie apologizes to them, they get in touch with Lily, who is remorseful over not listening to Jessie and screwing things up for Bonnie. Jessie proposes a solution to make things right by getting Bonnie and Blaze to become friends. Jessie leads the toys to track Lily down, with help from the other devices. After they reunite, they send Blaze a message as Bonnie so that she can return Jessie and Bullseye. Lily connects to the Buzzes electronically, upgrading them so they can produce propellers to make them fly and carry the toys and devices home. Before making their returns, Buzz proposes to Jessie, and they finally kiss.

Blaze and her mom arrive at Bonnie’s house. Although Bonnie briefly declines Jessie and Bullseye again, Blaze tells her how she had fun playing with them. Bonnie changes her mind and quickly strikes up a friendship with Blaze over their shared imagination and silliness.

Bonnie and Blaze set up a “wedding” for Buzz and Jessie, while also creating a dramatic scenario where Buzz was having an affair with Trixie. Woody parts with his friends once more, until the next adventure. Bonnie and Blaze even get the neighbor twins to join in on their fun.

The credits show Bonnie and Blaze’s growing friendship. Later, the high-tech Buzz figures all make their way to a playground to be played with by other kids (and one of their teachers). They are then stunned to see their old nemesis/dad, an action figure of Emperor Zurg.

wiki_plot.text:
An ocean container filled with a unit of hi-tech edition Buzz Lightyear toys shipwrecks on a deserted island. Stuck in demo mode, the shipwrecked Buzzes escape the island and follow the North Star to return to "Star Command".

Eight-year-old Bonnie receives a frog-themed tablet named Lilypad ("Lily") from her parents in hopes of helping her socialize with children her own age. Bonnie soon becomes addicted to Lily and begins to neglect her toys. Jessie, as Bonnie's favorite and the new leader of her toys, explains to Lily about Bonnie's need for a real friend, which Lily attempts to solve by sending a friend request to Chelsea, one of Bonnie's classmates, on social media.

Fearful of losing Bonnie's affection, Jessie contacts Woody via a walkie-talkie for advice. Woody, who has left to help Bo Peep find homes for abandoned toys, decides to return to Bonnie, believing that Jessie needs help. When Chelsea invites Bonnie over for a sleepover, Jessie and Bullseye stow away in her suitcase while Bonnie takes Lily with her. Though she is initially happy to have them, Bonnie has her father take Jessie and Bullseye home after Chelsea, alongside her friends Heidi and Kara, question Bonnie for still playing with toys. Jessie and Bullseye escape but are found by an elderly couple. Seeing an old address written under Jessie's chaps, the couple takes the two back to the farmhouse of her original owner, Emily.

There, Jessie ends up in a Wendy house of forgotten toys, including a potty-training device toy named Smarty Pants. As they enter the house searching for Bullseye, Jessie meets GPS receiver Atlas and camera Snappy. They inform her that a new family, the Manoukians—consisting of a young girl named Blaze and her parents—now inhabit the farmhouse. After experiencing a joyful playtime with an imaginative Blaze, Jessie decides to have her meet Bonnie and help them become friends. 

Woody reunites with Bonnie's toys, and they confront Lily about Jessie's whereabouts. Believing the toys are hindering Bonnie's social life, Lily tricks Bonnie's father into putting them in storage while Woody and Buzz escape. At the farmhouse, Jessie works with the device toys to send a picture of herself to Bonnie in Blaze's name. Seeing this on social media, the Buzz units believe Jessie is the leader of Star Command due to her sheriff badge. Woody and Buzz hitch a ride with Bonnie and her mother as they go to the Manoukians' house. On the way, Bonnie reads a group chat in which Chelsea, Heidi, and Kara ridicule her over the picture. As a result, Bonnie rejects Blaze's offer to return Jessie and Bullseye, disassociating herself from the toys.

The Buzz units capture Woody, suspecting he means Jessie harm, but Buzz clarifies matters. Jessie sulks by a tree where Emily used to play with her. She discovers a buried time capsule filled with late-20th-century objects alongside photos of an adult Emily and her daughter, who is named after Jessie. Realizing that she still had an impact on Emily's life over the years, Jessie regains her faith in Bonnie. With the Buzz units' help, along with the device toys, Jessie tracks down Lily, who boarded a donation truck out of guilt for hurting Bonnie. Jessie and the others catch up with the truck and convince Lily to help Bonnie befriend Blaze. Buzz professes his love for Jessie and they kiss.

The toys and devices arrange a new meeting between Bonnie and Blaze. After some hesitation, they bond over their love of toys. They play together with all of Bonnie's toys and pretend to marry Jessie and Buzz, with Woody happily watching before he departs with Bo. Each of the Buzz units are later taken in by various children at a school playground.

spoiler_text.text:
Niki White (Leo Woodall) works as an assistant piano tuner for Harry Horowitz (Dustin Hoffman) who has his own small piano tuning business. Harry and his wife Marla (Tovah Feldshuh) are like surrogate parents to Niki, since they were friends with his father before he died. Niki suffers from a condition called hyperacusis, where he has an extreme sensitivity to sound, always wearing protective devices in his ears to keep most of the sound out, and even wearing large headphones over those when he’s in louder spaces. Harry is jovial but ailing; he is having difficulty hearing and occasionally some dementia, forgetting things, and Niki helps him however he can. They spend their days traveling to homes of very wealthy people to tune up their expensive pianos.

Niki has dinner with Harry and Marla, where Marla admonishes him for not wearing his very expensive hearing aids, reminding him they will have to pay out of pocket for a new set if he loses them. He explains that he accidentally switched two items – he put his hearing aids in the safe and his watch in the bathroom. On top of that, he changed the safe combination and can’t remember it. Niki offers to take the safe home to try to open it – he uses his extremely sensitive hearing and after taking his time is able to listen closely and crack open the safe, retrieving Harry’s hearing aids.

With Harry’s health declining, Niki begins going to tune pianos on his own to pick up some of the slack. He goes to a prestigious music conservatory, where he meets Ruthie (Havana Rose Liu), a piano student working on her final composition. She is wary of him at first, but is very impressed by the fact that Niki has perfect pitch and can even name exactly what notes she is playing on the piano as she tests him. He explains that he used to play but with his condition doesn’t play anymore.

His next tuning job is at an extremely large mansion, where he is unable to properly tune the piano due to the noise of construction. He returns in the evening to finish tuning, only to hear loud noises upstairs. He goes to see what is making the noise, and discovers Uri (Lior Raz) and his two associates, Yoni and Uri’s nephew Benny, attempting to drill into the safe. He assumes they are robbing it, but Uri explains that he runs home security and this is part of his job. Knowing that they won’t stop making noise until the safe is open and wanting to finish his job and go home, Niki opens it for them, impressing Uri, who gives him a large stack of money and his phone number.

Harry and Niki are having lunch at a diner when they run into Ruthie, and Harry demands that Niki walk her to class, which he does, a little awkwardly. When he returns to the diner, he sees Harry being loaded into an ambulance. He meets Marla at the hospital, where Marla reveals that she has discovered Harry had stopped paying his insurance premiums without telling her, and they now will owe more money than they can afford to the hospital. The first thing she decides to do is sell the business’s van – and Niki insists he will buy it. Marla doesn’t think he can afford it, but Niki is determined to figure it out. When Uri calls him for help with a job, Niki says yes knowing he needs the money.

Niki goes to Uri’s headquarters, a warehouse that they use as a club space on the weekends. Uri explains that though he does run a security company, his clients are so wealthy that they don’t notice if a small amount goes missing from the top, so they steals a few valuable items per client. Uri asks Niki to prove himself again on one of his own safes; Niki demands extreme quiet and is able to open the safe. He agrees to start working on jobs for Uri, provided Uri gives him a large cash advance – which he does. Niki takes the cash and uses it to buy the van from Marla, who is surprised he was able to get the money.

The next day he gets a call from Ruthie, who is upset because a pipe burst and got water all over her piano which belonged to her grandmother. Niki comes over and begins fixing the piano – Ruthie is deeply upset because her grandmother only gave her two things – an expensive watch that she lost on the train, and the piano. Niki refuses to accept any payment, so Ruthie makes them pasta for dinner. Ruthie opens up about how she is very nervous about her composition because she hopes to be selected by prestigious composer Marius Maissner (Jean Reno) as his next apprentice. Niki tells Ruthie how he used to play piano until his illness make it too painful for him to continue.

Uri continues to call on Niki, and he joins Uri’s crew as they break into their wealthy clients’ homes where Uri has Niki unlock the safes. Niki is hesitant, but Uri insists these wealthy people make their money in unscrupulous ways. Niki is able to use his next large payout to pay off a huge portion of Harry’s hospital bill. He returns to Ruthie’s apartment to check on her piano, and the two almost share a kiss when Niki smells something burning. As Ruthie realizes she’s left food in the oven, the smoke alarm goes off, and the extreme volume causes Niki deep deep pain. Ruthie apologizes, very upset, and the two finally kiss. Over the next few weeks, Niki and Ruthie continue dating and he fixes pianos by day and cracks safes for Uri by night. He is able to pay off the full balance on Harry’s medical bill.

One of the safes Uri has him open contains a beautiful pearl watch that reminds Niki of the one that belonged to Ruthie’s grandmother, and the next time he sees her, he gives it to her as a gift. She is initially taken aback because it’s such an extravagant gift and they’ve only been dating a month, but Niki asks her to be his girlfriend officially and she accepts. Niki brings Ruthie with him on a visit to Harry in the hospital, where Harry, confused, says Niki’s deceased father was just there visiting him and bragging about what an incredible piano player Niki is. Niki brings in a piano so Ruthie can play for Harry, and meanwhile Marla tells Niki she’s found out he’s paid off the hospital bill. She is worried about him, and says that he should not do anything that could harm him and that she and Harry will be fine.

Uri calls Niki to another job which is way farther out, and Niki is confused when he arrives at what is clearly not a rich person’s home. He enters to find Uri’s crew there with some Korean gangsters, and Uri orders Niki to crack the safe. Niki is deeply uncomfortable and has a hard time due to the house being near the airport (planes constantly flying overhead creating noise) but does what Uri asks, cracking the safe that the gang members retrieve a small notebook from. Just then, the homeowner comes in holding them all at gunpoint, demanding they hand over the notebook – which contains codes to enter a cryptocurrency wallet. Holding a gun at Niki’s back, he orders him to tear up the codes and eat them, which Niki does. Suddenly, a gun goes off – Benny, who was outside on guard, has shot the homeowner. The loudness of the gunshot causes Niki to stumble out of the house in pain and he vomits on the street, declaring himself done with the robberies. Later at home, Niki logs into the crypto wallet – he had actually memorized the code words, and discovers access to 18 million dollars in drug money.

Niki begins ignoring Uri’s calls, and then Niki gets a call from Marla – Harry has passed away. At the shiva, Niki is upset to find Uri at the buffet, following him. Uri demands that Niki answer him when he calls, and implies that he might be willing to hurt Ruthie (who is there playing piano) if he refuses. Angry and depressed, Niki keeps ignoring the calls. Later, when Ruthie plays her composition on the piano for Niki in preparation for her show, Niki is barely listening. Ruthie gets upset that he can’t be supportive, and explains to Niki that she’s trying to go somewhere and build a career for herself, unlike Niki. Niki snaps back at her that he wanted to be doing what she does until he had to go to therapy for years to deal with his condition, and that he doesn’t know what he’s supposed to do since he can’t play anymore – and then he says he’s a better piano player than Ruthie will ever be.

He leaves Ruthie’s apartment, angry with himself, when Uri and his guys pull up. Uri screams at Niki that he will answer when he calls, then uses an air horn which causes Niki to crumble to the ground in pain and then pass out. When he awakens, he sees that Uri and the Korean mobsters have found another set of codes for the crypto they need Niki to break into a safe and get. The air horn blast has left Niki’s ears ringing and he can’t hear the safe, and demands to be let go because he’s going to miss Ruthie’s concert. Uri tells him he won’t go anywhere until the safe is open. Niki manages to get the safe open – Uri and his crew celebrate the access codes, which show 17 million in the crypto account. Niki races to the performance but it too late – he misses Ruthie’s composition, which she plays while wearing the watch Niki gave her. She is watched intently by Maissner in the audience.

Maissner asks to meet with Ruthie, who is honored, and he asks her to be his new assistant on his next work. Ruthie is thrilled and accepts, but Maissner says he has to take care of some business first. He asks about her watch, which it turns out was stolen from his safe a few weeks ago. He explains that his father had two watches that survived the Holocaust in Nazi Germany, and that both went missing. Ruthie is stunned and shocked and explains that her boyfriend gave them to her, just as Niki arrives. She confronts him, asking if he knew it was stolen. He can’t give her a straight answer, and she leaves, horrified. Niki sits down with Maissner, who seems put off from hiring Ruthie and is going to call the police, until Niki says he can get the other watch back and that Ruthie had nothing to do with the theft. Maissner agrees to hold off on calling the police.

Niki returns to Uri’s headquarters during one of their rave parties and sneaks into the back and breaks into the safe where the watch is supposed to be only to discover it isn’t there. He is then apprehended by Yoni who brings him outside where Uri, who is wearing the watch, begins beating Niki with a baseball bat and demands Benny retrieve the air horn. Niki tells Uri he just wants to get the watch back, that it survived the Holocaust, and that he will never contact Uri again. Yoni and Benny are disturbed, since they and Uri also had family survive the holocaust, and plead with Uri to stop. Uri refuses, brutally taking the air horn and putting it right up to Niki’s ear and blasting it over and over as Niki screams. He then grabs a knife and begins cutting Niki’s ear as he passes out.

Niki awakes in the hospital, bruised beaten and with the bottom of his ear cut off. Due to the air horn, he is now almost entirely deaf. When he retrieves his belongings while leaving the hospital, he finds that second watch among his things. Marla arrives at the hospital to see Niki, and later Niki gives her some of the money that he took off the top of the crypto wallet. Now without ear devices since he can barely hear at all anymore, Niki brings the watch to Maissner to return it. Maissner declares his debt with Niki settled, and leaves as Ruthie, who has gotten the job working for him, enters and is surprised to see Niki, especially so beaten and bruised. Uncomfortable, she starts to leave, and Niki sits down at the piano. With his hearing gone, he is finally able to play again, and begins playing the piano beautifully. Ruthie stops to listen as is deeply moved by his performance. After he finishes, Niki notes with his perfect pitch that one of the keys is off.

wiki_plot.text:
Niki White is the apprentice of New York City piano tuner Harry Horowitz, a friend of his late father who teaches him that the tones are more of a feeling than a sound. Although a gifted musician, Niki has hyperacusis and can no longer play the piano, wearing ear protection at all times against loud noises. After Harry forgets the combination to his safe, Niki teaches himself to open it with his heightened hearing, discovering a talent for safe-cracking.

While tuning at a music conservatory, Niki meets Ruthie, a hyper-competitive student pianist and aspiring composer. Flirting, he impresses her with a display of astonishing auditory acuity and memory recall. Later, Niki is tuning at a wealthy client's home until construction noise becomes too loud. He interrupts a trio drilling into a safe, who claim they are installing a new safe, and asks when they will finish. The trio feel insulted and rudely say an indefinite amount of time until the old safe is opened. Niki breaks into the safe for them to save time, impressing them in the process, and receiving an offer of "real money" from their leader, Uri. The next day at a diner, Harry encourages Niki to walk Ruthie to class, but the interaction fizzles when he suggests her composition is derivative. However, they begin a romance after Niki repairs her treasured piano. Niki tells her that it took years of exposure therapy to manage his sensitivity to sound. When Harry is hospitalized after a heart attack, Niki accepts Uri's offer, in order to purchase the tuning business and to save Harry and his wife Marla from a ruinous medical debt. Uri's security company acts as a cover to rob their own clients but is in the need of a safecracker on their team to make even more money. Uri invites Niki to prove his abilities--by opening Uri's own safe--which he does, and thus joins Uri, Uri's nephew Benny, and accomplice Yoni, to rob wealthy homes.

Uri's explanation as to why he was never caught is the law of diminishing marginal productivity: the more people have, the less likely they will notice if something small goes missing. Uri tells Niki, "You can't steal something obvious, like a painting or signature art piece that's on display. But clients generally don't notice if one of several valuable watches goes missing from a cache in the safe. And if they do notice it's missing, they blame someone else and recover from the insurance company." Niki and the crew commit several successful robberies. During one of them, Niki finds a pearl watch that resembles one Ruthie lost, an heirloom from her grandmother, and he gives it to her. He introduces her to Marla and the bedridden Harry, while secretly paying the hospital bills.

Suddenly one night, Uri changes their established routine, requiring Niki to open a safe for a pair of Korean gangsters, retrieving the seed phrase to their own uncle's cryptocurrency wallet. To everyone's surprise, the uncle bursts in, holding everyone at gunpoint and forcing Niki to eat the only copy of the password. Before the uncle can exact his revenge, Benny shoots the uncle dead, allowing Niki and Uri's gang to escape. It turns out that Niki was able to memorize the seed phrase and secretly discovers that the wallet holds more than $18 million. 

Sadly, Harry dies, and at his shiva Niki speaks with Herbie Hancock (as himself) telling that Harry's moniker was "tuner fish" (the film's running gag). Uri gatecrashes the event (meanwhile denigrating the meal prepared for the Shiva) and demands that Niki help steal the digital spare key to the Korean uncle's money.

A grieving Niki decides not to join the robbery, but Ruthie's anxiety about her upcoming performance causes her to pick a fight over his divided attentions. Ruthie complains that Niki has never had to work to achieve anything--he's just a piano tuner--while she is working to achieve something truly important and difficult. Niki lashes out--explaining just how hard it was to overcome his disability, and cruelly steps over the line by asserting that before his condition became severe, that he was a better piano player than [Ruthie] will ever be. Storming out of her apartment, Niki encounters Uri's crew. As Niki is disoriented by an air horn, the crew is able to take him in. On the day of Ruthie’s performance, Niki manages to open the safe and retrieve the spare key. It is revealed that the digital wallet now holds $1 million less than what had been shown, hinting that Niki had used the same law of diminishing marginal utility on Uri and his men. Once the ordeal is done, Niki runs across town--on foot--to the Music Academy.

Marius Maissner, a renowned composer who was impressed by Ruthie's performance, invites Ruthie to join a new project as his assistant but recognizes the watch she is wearing--the pearl watch that Niki gave her--as his own grandmother's heirloom, which survived the Holocaust alongside his grandfather's watch. Unfortunately, Maissner explains, the two watches were stolen from his home safe just a few weeks ago. Niki arrives and is confronted by Ruthie and admits the truth to Maissner. Assuring Maissner that Ruthie is blameless, Niki offers to recover his grandfather's watch in exchange for not involving the police.

Niki tries to retrieve the watch from Uri's safe, but is caught by Yoni. As it turns out, Uri is wearing the watch. Niki begs for the watch's return and reveals its history. He convinces Benny and Yoni--who are certain that keeping Holocaust jewelry is bad juju--but Uri viciously beats Niki for the betrayal, cutting off part of Niki's ears with a knife and deliberately cutting into Niki's eardrums. Waking up in a hospital, Niki discovers that doctors successfully repaired his earlobe but that he is now almost entirely deaf, to the extent that he no longer needs earplugs to tolerate noise since he can now barely hear. When a nurse hands over his things, he discovers that Uri has left him the watch. Niki delivers the watch to a grateful Maissner, and it is revealed that Maissner hired Ruthie as his assistant. When Niki and Ruthie have a moment alone together, Niki tells her he cannot hear her. Engrossed with the piano in the room, Niki begins to play. He gives a virtuoso performance--for the first time in years--playing an improved variation of Ruthie's original composition. Ending the performance, he points out that a key is flat and the piano needs tuning.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens with Mitt Gardiner (Josh Brolin) on a boat just a few miles from the shore with his friend Hewey (John Ortiz). Mitt, sick with cancer, ties weights to his body and jumps into the Pacific Ocean. Hewey can only sob quietly.

Mitt’s son Jay (Austin Abrams) rejoins his mother Zara (Elisabeth Shue) and older sisters Eva and Nan (Jane Levy and Emily Rudd) after being away for college. The ladies reminisce fondly of their father, but Jay has always had a strained relationship with Mitt because he was so hard on him while teaching him how to dive. The family is also sad that they are left without a body to bury.

Jay takes it upon himself to go diving and recover his father’s body. He stops at a store to get a tank and sees Hewey. They have a friendly chat but Jay doesn’t let him know what he’s doing.

Jay makes it to the water. He sneaks past police and puts on his gear, though he realizes he forgot to put on gloves. He dives in and ends up encountering a giant squid. It grabs Jay with its tentacle right as a massive sperm whale eats the squid. Jay unfortunately gets caught in the struggle and is pulled inside the whale’s mouth.

A brief flashback shows Mitt trying to teach Jay while out on the water. Mitt became too aggressive with showing him what to do and how he spoke to Jay, so Jay decided to go to school away from home to be far away from his dad.

Inside the whale, Jay wakes up to the squid trying to get one last swipe at him, even cutting Jay’s neck with its beak, but the whale’s stomach sucks it in and crushes it. Jay minds his depleting oxygen supply and tries to remember tips from his dad to help escape.

Jay tries to make his way into the next chamber of the whale’s stomach, thinking it might lead to an exit. However, the acid inside the stomach starts to burn his exposed hands. The squid’s beak also pierces his hand. Jay quickly makes his way back to the previous chamber and washes the acid off.

Jay uses certain items on his person to create a bandage and then a makeshift glove so he can grab a nearby jellyfish to light his way to the surface, as he remembers his dad’s advice on how “the ocean provides”. He climbs up the whale’s throat and is able to see outside its mouth. Jay tries to alert a nearby fishing boat, but the whale goes back underwater, and Jay sinks back into its stomach. The whale goes so far down that the pressure ruptures Jay’s ears and causes him to pass out again.

With oxygen running out fast, Jay starts to hear Mitt’s voice as though he is speaking to him as the whale. From outside, a pack of orcas begins attacking the sperm whale, severely injuring it before it calls out for help. Other sperm whales begin fighting the orcas off and help the injured whale move to safety.

Time and air is going quickly, and Jay starts to accept his fate. He thinks back to his mom and sister, and apologizes to his dad for not being as close as they could have been, as well as not reading one of the letters Mitt left his family. Mitt’s voice tells Jay that HE is what remains of Mitt. The whale uses the last of its energy to swim closer to the surface.

Jay then remembers a story the family brought up, which gives him an idea. As the whale dies from its injuries, Jay grabs some batteries he was carrying, along with some steel wool. Using the last of the oxygen in the tank, Jay uses the items to stuff inside the whale’s lower chamber and ignite the methane, creating an explosion that freed Jay. He swims until he is found by a nearby boat.

After recovering from his injuries, Jay goes on a boat with Zara, Eva, Nan, and Hewey. He finally reads his father’s letter and laughs to himself before deciding he is ready to go home.

wiki_plot.text:
Mitt Gardiner, a local dive-boat captain, is diagnosed with terminal mesothelioma. Before committing suicide by drowning at Central California's Monastery Beach, he leaves sealed farewell letters for his wife and three children in a cooler aboard his boat. He attaches diving weights to himself and jumps into the ocean. His body is never recovered, and his family holds a funeral with an empty casket.

One year later, Mitt's youngest child, Jay Gardiner, returns to California from university in Iowa. Struggling with his father's death, Jay reflects on their strained relationship and his refusal to speak with Mitt before his death or read the letter he left behind. Hoping to obtain his father's remains for burial and find closure, Jay undertakes an unauthorized solo scuba dive to search for the body, carrying a tank with approximately one hour of air. Near the edge of a submarine canyon, Jay encounters a giant squid fighting a sperm whale. As he attempts to reach the surface, the squid entangles his diving equipment and the whale finally swallows both Jay and the squid.

Jay regains consciousness inside one of the whale's four stomach chambers. He fights the squid, which is subsequently crushed by the stomach's muscular contractions. While searching for an escape route, Jay enters an adjacent chamber, where digestive fluids begin damaging his skin and equipment, and the partially digested squid's beak injures his hand. Jay returns to the first chamber, but his diminishing oxygen supply causes him to experience panic, delirium, and memories of his childhood.

Using the squid's beak and the faint illumination of a recently swallowed bioluminescent jellyfish, Jay attempts to climb through the whale's esophagus toward its mouth. When the whale surfaces to breathe, he tries to attract the attention of a nearby tour boat, which fails to notice him. The whale subsequently dives, and the rapid change in pressure causes Jay to suffer injuries and eventually lose consciousness. Upon regaining consciousness, Jay discovers that his oxygen supply is nearly depleted. Unable to find an exit, he attempts to force the whale to regurgitate him by stabbing its stomach wall with the squid's beak, but is unsuccessful. The whale is then attacked by a pod of orcas, before a nearby group of sperm whales intervenes and drives the orcas away. Jay's whale is mortally wounded and the injured animal begins ascending toward the surface.

As his condition deteriorates, Jay experiences hallucinations involving his father. He recalls a survival lesson Mitt taught him during childhood and concludes a means of escape. Using methane from the stomach chamber, oxygen from his remaining scuba supply, and steel wool and batteries carried as part of his diving equipment, Jay constructs an improvised explosive device. He uses the squid's beak to cut an opening in the stomach wall and positions the device inside it. The resulting explosion ruptures the whale's stomach and body, propelling Jay into the ocean. Jay reaches the surface as the whale's body sinks. A nearby tour boat rescues him and applies a tourniquet to his left arm. Later, Jay reunites with his family aboard Mitt's former boat. He finally reads the letter his father left for him and reacts emotionally, crying and laughing as he processes its contents.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in a village, where a lonely Fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) goes by the lake to gather fish for selling in the market. Everybody mocks and avoids her because of her smell. Meanwhile, people frequently visit The Basket Maker (Peter Dinklage), whose creations are often imbued with some type of magic. He gives a basket of wicker eggs to The Tailor’s Wife (Elizabeth Debicki) and her sister (Marli Siu), as the latter is set to marry The Bottlewasher (Gustav Lindh). The Basket Maker is also one of the few people who is genuinely kind to The Fisherwoman, who lives at home all alone.

The Tailor’s Wife’s Sister weds The Bottlewasher. After the ceremony, the maidens are given the wicker eggs for a tradition known as “The Maid’s Eggs”, which are supposed to be shaken and release a special colored smoke for whoever is set to marry next. All the ladies get yellow smoke from their eggs, but The Fisherwoman gets purple smoke, which visibly upsets the ladies. The Fisherwoman is mocked by The Baker’s Wife (Ella Bruccoleri) and The Innkeeper’s Wife (Emily Lloyd-Saini), which quietly gets to her.

The Fisherwoman travels to The Basket Maker’s home and gives him money for him to build her a husband. He agrees and tells her to be at the chapel in a month. Although he is surprised by such a request, The Basket Maker gathers his materials and creates a Wicker Husband (Alexander Skarsgard), who goes into town and shocks everyone with his appearance. The Tailor (Nabhaan Rizwan) gives him a suit in time for the wedding. The Fisherwoman arrives at the altar and marries the Wicker Husband. They go home and waste no time in having vigorous sex, causing their bed to break.

The Wicker Husband becomes the talk of the town. After The Butcher (Phil Daniels) takes a young bride, the villagers hold a ceremony and watch as The Fisherwoman and The Husband dance together. The women become enamored with the way he shows genuine affection toward The Fisherwoman and due to their loud and intense sex. The men are annoyed that their wives are now holding them to a higher standard. It also causes some women like The Tailor’s Wife to look at their own marriages, as The Tailor views her as the homemaker while he is the working one, so he denies her suggestion to help in the business. Her sister also finds herself sexually unsatisfied with The Bottlewasher.

The Husband later goes to the pub, where The Baker (Ben Ashenden) is drunk and demands that The Husband sleep with his wife to satisfy her since he thinks that’s what she wants. The Husband asks The Baker if he really loves his wife, and he breaks down in tears saying he does. Meanwhile, The Tailor’s Wife visits The Fisherwoman as she is picking berries to pry about her marriage, though The Fisherwoman implies that The Tailor’s Wife was responsible for the death of a boy from when they were younger, someone who “married” The Tailor’s Wife. When she implies to The Fisherwoman that her husband is sleeping around with other women, she whacks The Tailor’s Wife in the face with her basket, giving her a cut. When she returns home, The Fisherwoman begins to have her suspicions about The Husband.

The Bottlewasher falls through the roof of his house while trying to fix something in an attempt to follow The Wicker Husband’s lead and apply himself physically and get his wife aroused. He gets a nasty gash on his foot and is brought to The Doctor (Richard E. Grant), father to The Tailor’s Wife and her sister. Despite their efforts, The Bottlewasher dies from infection, leaving his wife widowed and grief-stricken. The Wicker Husband hugs her for comfort, something that rubs The Fisherwoman the wrong way. When she confronts him about it, The Husband assures her she has no reason to be envious.

The Tailor’s Wife’s Sister goes to The Basket Maker and asks him to make her a baby. When the child is brought to life, The Tailor’s Wife quickly suspects that The Wicker Husband is the father, though her sister denies it. The Tailor’s Wife herself is also exasperated by her life unraveling.

The sisters travel to The Fisherwoman’s home and present the baby to her, claiming it to be The Wicker Husband’s child. When The Tailor’s Wife threatens to burn the baby, The Fisherwoman instead grabs lantern and tosses it at The Husband in a blind jealous rage, setting him on fire. The Husband runs away into the woods, while The Fisherwoman cries with great regret.

The partially burnt Husband finds The Basket Maker, who is able to fix him up. They find The Fisherwoman, who has taken the Wicker Baby after The Tailor’s Wife’s Sister left him there. The Basket Maker explains that the rotted wood on The Husband means he will probably not last much longer. The Fisherwoman apologizes for what she did, promising to treat him as a person in his own right, and The Husband gladly takes her back.

The Basket Maker announces to the townsfolk that he is going to retire, but he will present one last creation, a Wicker Wife, to whomever gives him the best gift. After a week, all of the people give The Basket Maker items such as furniture, clothing, and baked goods. The Tailor’s Wife gives him a bag of coins so that she can give the Wicker Wife to her husband so that she and her sister can leave, and his new wife will take care of everything around the house. The Butcher, who just locked his bride in his cellar, gives The Basket Maker an even bigger bag of coins, granting him the Wicker Wife. As The Basket Maker leaves with everybody’s gifts, they realize too late that he made her from a different material from The Wicker Husband, a very prickly buckthorn. The Wicker Wife gives The Butcher a painful kiss, driving the thorns into his face while his escaped bride watches before she can take her revenge. The Tailor’s Wife also appears to be reconsidering her decision.

The film ends as The Basket Maker takes The Fisherwoman, The Wicker Husband, and The Wicker Baby away for them to start a new life together as a family.

wiki_plot.text:
A solitary Fisherwoman lives on the outskirts of a village and is often mocked and harassed for her spinster status. At the wedding of the Tailor's Wife's Sister to the inn's Bottlewasher, he struggles to fasten a ritual collar around her neck. After the wedding, unmarried women ritually shake small baskets containing eggs, which emit yellow smoke. The Fisherwoman's dropped basket shakes by itself and emits purple smoke, indicating that she will be the next to marry. The village women take this as a negative omen. 

The Fisherwoman visits the village Basket Weaver and commissions him to make her a husband. The Basket Weaver accepts and tells her to meet him at the chapel in one month. On the eve of the wedding, the Wicker Husband arrives in the village, asking for clothing, shoes and lodging to prepare for the ceremony. The Fisherwoman and the Wicker Husband wed, during which he declines to put a collar on her. While consummating their union, the bed collapses, and the Wicker Husband offers to repair it. He soon completes many tasks to improve the Fisherwoman's modest hut, such as gardening and repairing her roof.

Their marriage becomes the talk of the village. At the Butcher's wedding, their unique dancing becomes a spectacle, and the women are moved by the Wicker Husband's romantic overtures to his wife. The men of the village become leery of the Wicker Husband, whose kind demeanor contrasts their boorish behavior toward their own wives. At the inn, the men question his motive behind his domestic labour. He answers that his wife's happiness makes him happy. 

The men remain skeptical, though the Bottlewasher resolves to repair his own home's roof to please his wife, which goes awry when the roof collapses and he falls into the house. The town's Doctor attempts to heal the Bottlewasher, but his wounds become fatal. The Wicker Husband soothingly embraces the Bottlewasher's bereft wife after the funeral, stoking the Fisherwoman's suspicions, planted by the Tailor's Wife, that he has been unfaithful. He implores her to trust him.

The Bottlewasher's widow visits the Basket Weaver and asks him to make her a baby. Shortly after, the Tailor's Wife discovers the wicker child. She brings her sister to the Fisherwoman's hut, claiming the child is proof of the Wicker Husband's infidelity and threatening to burn it if the Fisherwoman and her husband do not claim the child. The Wicker Husband insists the child is not his, but seeks to protect it still. The Fisherwoman throws her lantern at the Wicker Husband, who runs burning into the woods. Wracked with guilt and grief, she becomes reclusive again.

In spring, the Fisherwoman discovers the wicker child in the woods and takes him into her care. Meanwhile, the Basket Weaver finds the charred but living Wicker Husband and brings him to his workshop to repair him. The Basket Weaver visits the Fisherwoman, explains his role in the child's creation, and helps reconcile the couple. At the village market, he announces his retirement, and one final creation - a Wicker Woman, to be given to whomever presents him the most generous retirement gift. The village greedily, excitedly dreams of the Wicker Woman's value. 

When the Basket Weaver returns with the veiled Wicker Woman, the villagers shower him with luxurious gifts. The Tailor's Wife arrives with a sack of coins, announcing she and her sister are departing the village, leaving the Wicker Woman to assume her domestic role in the Tailor's home. The lecherous Butcher, having trapped his wife in the cellar, arrives with a larger sum of money and wins the prize. The Basket Weaver departs with his gifts, explaining that the Wicker Woman is made of a different material than the Wicker Husband, who is made of supple willow. The Wicker Woman is revealed to be made of dangerous blackthorn; her kiss and touch stab the butcher, who is ignored by the surrounding villagers as he cries in pain. 

Her plan thwarted, the Tailor's Wife decides to stay, though the Tailor is furious with her. Meanwhile, the Basket Weaver drives his wagon, carrying the Fisherwoman, the Wicker Husband, and the wicker child to a new life abroad.
