spoiler_text.text:
Santiago, Chile, 1973 – Two CIA operatives – Chris Carlisle (John Malkovich) and Lee Chesterfield (Sam Rockwell) – are reporting to the bureau’s office under their chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Lee records Chris on a video camera discussing his feelings about the job. When MJ comes in to wish them a good trip, Chris responds profanely.

Chris and Lee are set to travel to the Easter Islands. At the airport, they meet two students, Monica (Mariana di Girolamo) and Alicia (Ailin Salas), who tell him the correct name is “Rapa Nui”. Chris responds obnoxiously and asks their opinion about current president Salvador Allende, before telling them their country is going to be “fucked”, and Lee has to get Chris to shut up. On the plane, Chris continues openly discussing previous jobs, including people they have killed, which only makes Lee more nervous. This is a result of Chris being sick with cancer and experiencing memory loss, as he is starting to say a lot of things he shouldn’t say.

The two arrive on the Easter Islands and are put in separate rooms. MJ contacts Lee about Chris’s behavior, as well as the subject of Chris planning to write his “memoirs”, even though Lee reminds Chris he can’t remember anything. MJ wants Chris dead over something in the memoirs. Lee and Chris later go to dinner and see Monica and Alicia again. While trying to get their attention, the guys end up arguing with a nearby couple over the proper name of the Easter Island heads.

Back in their rooms, Chris shoots up morphine. He brings up how Lee’s wife Marge (Parker Posey) has cheated on him repeatedly. After a drugged-up conversation, Lee leaves the room, and Chris finds two notes on his person that say “remember that you’re dying” and “don’t trust Lee”.

The next day, Lee bonds with Chris as he continues to say a bunch of nonsense before heading to see the Easter Island heads (“Moai”). Chris makes crude comments comparing one of the heads to a dwarf that he wants to have sex with. This is overheard by Monica and Alicia, who reprimand him for mocking something so sacred.

Later, Lee gets a call from Marge, who admits she slept with a lawyer. Lee is more annoyed than anything, but he also mentions to Marge that he doesn’t know if Chris remembers that he asked Lee to kill him.

At night, Chris drives out to the Moai to sit down alone. He is approached by a horse that he begins to pet. In the distance, a red car drives up, and the driver takes pictures of Chris. He sees the car and fires his gun, hitting the rear windshield twice before the driver gets away. Although Chris denies getting into anything eventful, Lee later finds out about the car shooting from MJ and tells him to make sure Chris hasn’t said anything in his memoirs about “Dallas”.

The guys later walk around the beach, where Chris spots Monica. Despite Lee wanting to keep him away from her, Chris approaches her and apologizes for his behavior, admitting that he is dying. Monica encourages him to be more honest with what little time he has left. When Lee finds Chris again, he brings up the subject of his request for Lee to kill him, but Chris suddenly tells Lee that he wanted to die in Venice, Italy instead of the Easter Islands.

Lee tries to arrange for the receptionist Rosa (Paola Giannini) to book them a flight to Venice, but MJ has decided to make his way to Chile to ensure Chris’s demise. As a result of Lee’s failure to follow through with orders, MJ has Marge kidnapped as she is calling Lee to tell him their house was burgled. Lee later discovers Rosa, who actually works for MJ, trying to open a briefcase belonging to Chris, but Lee forces her out of the room at gunpoint.

Chris goes to a night club to see a folk singer since Monica had mentioned him. She arrives with Alicia, and Lee joins Chris. The night quickly turns sour when Chris mentions in explicit detail of the impending coup d’etat in the country that will happen in September of that year, describing the horrific account of what will happen to anyone who stays there. Monica is disturbed by these comments and slaps Chris. On their drive back to their rooms, the guys pull over when Chris sees the horse that he met earlier is dead on the side of the road.

The two return to their rooms, where Rosa says she booked their flights. Over dinner, it’s revealed why the guys are in this mess to begin with: Chris is the one who assassinated JFK (despite his denials), and MJ fears he’s going to spill the beans in his memoirs. Chris discusses plans with Lee to kill MJ when he arrives in Chile after hearing about Marge. When Chris isn’t looking, Lee removes the bullets from his gun.

Before leaving the room, Chris contacts his reclusive brother Jim (Tom Waits) for the last time. Jim criticizes Chris for killing JFK, saying the country “went to shit” after it happened. Chris intercepts Monica before she can go to the airport and he makes her drive him towards the Moai.

MJ arrives in Chile and meets Alicia, who was working for him all along and was driving the car that Chris shot at. She tells MJ how Chris told Monica all about the coup. Before heading to eliminate him, Lee goes to the airport and takes MJ with him.

Monica brings Chris to the Moai, where he gives her one last speech about how certain people should be killed even at a young age if they appear like a threat. As she tries to drive away, Alicia and two gunmen block Monica’s car from driving away. The men try to take her away, but they are both shot dead by Chris from a distance. Monica gets back in her car and runs Alicia over, and it appears that Monica will remain on the island instead of returning home.

The whole thing was witnessed by Lee, while MJ is in the middle of a heroin-induced slump. He mutters that people liked Kennedy before Lee decides to shoot MJ in the head to keep him away from Chris. Lee walks over to find Chris sitting down. Chris gives Lee a Super 8 tape of him talking about the Kennedy assassination to help him get Marge back. After a final chat, Lee shoots Chris in the head. He then finds a note on Chris’s person, which simply states that he wishes he killed less people and hung out with more horses.

The last shot is Chris through Lee’s video camera, surrounded by horses on the island.

wiki_plot.text:
In 1973, CIA officers Chris Carlisle and Lee Chesterfield vacation to Easter Island from their station in Santiago, Chile. At the airport, they encounter Monica and Alicia, two young left-wing students. Chris jokes to them that they are CIA agents there to destabilize their government, which is quickly brushed aside by Lee.

During their trip, Chris's crude behavior and morphine addiction is of constant annoyance to Lee, though it is mostly tolerated. Chris is ageing and has begun recording a memoir on his voice recorder of his various involvements during his career (including the Guatemalan coup d'etat, the Bay of Pigs invasion, the assassination of Patrice Lumumba and the Kennedy assassination, among others). However, this is opposed by bureau chief MJ, who, it is later revealed, has instructed Lee to kill Chris lest he reveal confidential information.

The pair travel to various destinations on the island. It is revealed that Chris has dementia and terminal cancer with a week to live; he has asked Lee to kill him at the end of their trip, though he himself no longer remembers this fact. Chris believes that they are being followed and becomes increasingly paranoid and volatile. When Lee tries to confirm their plans with Chris, a confused Chris responds that he would rather visit Venice and insists that Lee books a new itinerary. A frustrated Lee relents.

Meanwhile, MJ pressures Lee, who is torn between his duty and his loyalty to Chris, to tie up loose ends. He needs Lee to locate a rifle which was used to assassinate Kennedy. Lee finds their hotel receptionist rummaging through Chris's belongings and discovers that she is acting on instructions from MJ. MJ coerces Lee by kidnapping his wife and children, and decides to travel to Easter Island himself.

Chris meets Monica again and apologizes for his earlier remarks. In the evening, while attending a Victor Jara concert, he informs her that Chilean president Salvador Allende will be overthrown and activists like her and Alicia will be persecuted. He warns her to flee and advises her to never stop fighting if she is being made to get into a car, but she angrily rebuffs him. Whilst leaving, Chris realizes that Monica's car had been the one following him.

MJ arrives on the island, and Lee goes alone to meet him. He pleads with MJ to spare Chris and let them go in peace to Venice. However, MJ refuses and insists Chris is to be killed on the island. MJ, Alicia (a CIA mole who was working for MJ all along), and Lee head to find Chris, who has forced Monica at gunpoint to drive him away from the hotel. After confirming that she is not a spy, he advises her on how to possibly prevent the upcoming Chilean regime, telling her to kill any person she sees in uniform, while acknowledging that even then there will be more people; the regime is inevitable. Still, this sparks a spirit of resistance in Monica. 

As Monica drives away, she is stopped by MJ. As his men drag Monica towards a car, she struggles to resist them with all her might until they are shot dead by Chris with the rifle used to kill Kennedy. She escapes after running over Alicia. MJ orders Lee to kill Chris, but Lee, disillusioned, shoots MJ instead. Lee and Chris share one final conversation, during which Chris gives Lee a film reel of the Kennedy assassination to be used as leverage to save Lee's family. Chris finally gives Lee the code word to kill him, which he does. In his final voice recording, Chris briefly reflects that he "could have killed a lot less people" and "should've hung out with a lot more horses"

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens in The Impassible Wilderness. A boy named Alexei walks out onto his balcony while his mother, the Dowager Governess Alexandra (Carey Mulligan), tries to stop him. Alexei pulls a large gear out of his body and jumps to his death. The people see that Alexei’s body is mechanical, and the new Governor Lars Svik (Marc Evan Jackson) orders for Alexandra to be arrested.

In Portland, teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) lives with her parents (Jake Johnson and Maya Erskine) and infant brother Mac (Arthur Knight). Mr. McKeel tells his kids fantasy stories about The Impassible Wilderness, but Prue feels she is too old for things like that. Her parents leave for the day and instruct Prue to not leave the house with Mac, but she decides to step out before they can come back.

Prue rides her bike around town with Mac in a wagon. They run into her friend and classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay). Prue sees Curtis as a dorky loser because he is still fixated on fantasy and nerdy things. When the kids go by the playground, a massive murder of crows swoops down and snatches Mac. Prue and Curtis pursue the crows and come before The Impassible Wilderness. Prue cuts her hand and touches the leaves, which, unbeknownst to her, is what opens up a path for her and Curtis to enter.

Prue and Curtis spot a group of coyote soldiers, led by Commandant Maksim (Tom Waits), who is berating a soldier named Dmitri (Charlie Day). After Dmitri talks back, Maksim attacks him but spots Prue and Curtis. The two run away but get split up. Prue ends up hitching a ride with The Postman (Len Cariou) while Curtis is taken by the coyotes.

Curtis wakes up to find Alexandra looking over him. She treats him as though he is Alexei and acts motherly toward him. When she leaves, Curtis is found by a talking mouse named Septima (Awkwafina), who sees Curtis as a friend after he lets her eat the stew that Alexandra gave him.

The Postman takes Prue towards the Avian Principality, where they are stopped by The General (Angela Bassett), a gigantic eagle leader. Knowing that Prue is an “outsider”, they redirect her to Lars’s mansion in the South Wood, where humans and anthropomorphic animals coexist. His major-domo Roger Swindon (Jemaine Clement) brings Prue to Lars’s office where she explains herself. Instead of helping her, they keep Prue up in a room. She makes her escape but is spotted by Rogers, Lars, and the other members of their banquet. They chase Prue throughout the mansion until she is able to outrun them and getting a ride on a cart.

Alexandra brings Curtis and her soldiers outside the forest, where a fierce battle has taken place and they see many fallen fighters. Alexandra orders Curtis to put one man out of his misery, but he is unable to do so, so she plunges her sword into him. The coyotes then capture the Bandits, led by their king Brendan (Mahershala Ali). Alexandra has dark plans for the forest and wants to control the Ivy of the wilderness.

Prue is dropped off at an address that she was given by Owl Rex (Richard E. Grant), Crown Prince of the Avian Principality. Rex tells Prue about Alexandra’s backstory. She was a beloved governess alongside her husband, and they both loved and adored Alexei. One day while riding horses, Alexei took a different path away from his parents and ended up on a mountain where his horse got spooked and threw him off, sending Alexei falling to his death. The Ivy absorbed Alexei’s body, so Alexandra was never able to bury her son. After her husband died, Alexandra turned to dark magic and used Alexei’s last baby tooth to put his soul into an animatronic body. When Alexei discovered his true nature, he chose to commit suicide. Alexandra was arrested and exiled with the coyotes, and now she is planning something evil to get her son back. Roger and a dog bodyguard arrive to get Prue, but Rex holds them off as he is arrested, and The General takes Prue with her.

Back in Alexandra’s lair, Curtis discovers Mac is being kept away in a room. She appears and admits she has plans to sacrifice the boy, and then has Curtis imprisoned with Brendan, plus other Bandits like Niamh (Amandla Stenberg) and Seamus (Olafur Darri Olafsson), as well as Dmitri. The Bandits assume Curtis is on Alexandra’s side until he says he is an outsider.

The General soars through the sky with Prue on her back, flying away from Alexandra’s crows and the coyotes. The General is taking Prue to see the Mystics in the North Wood, but one of the coyotes fatally shoots The General in the chest with an arrow, sending her plunging down. Prue is apprehended by the coyotes.

Prue is brought before Alexandra. She tries to make it look like Mac has been killed after she gives him his pajamas but Prue knows she is lying. Still, Alexandra makes her return home empty-handed.

Prue sadly rides her bike home and is forced to face her parents. After she tells them what happened, Mr. and Mrs. McKeel admit a big secret: they have always known about Alexandra because they made a deal with her. They were unable to conceive a child and came upon a Seer (Blythe Danner) who directed the couple to a bridge where they would ring a bell to meet Alexandra. Her deal was that she would grant the McKeels the ability to have a child, but the first child would be theirs to keep, and the second child they have would belong to Alexandra. Despite the risk, the McKeels went through with it and never planned to have a second child. This is why they told Prue not to take Mac outside, and it also explains why Prue has magic blood that grants her access to the woods. Feeling betrayed, Prue decides to return to The Impassible Wilderness on her own.

Septima sneaks past the guards and swipes their keys. Even though Curtis is bummed out, she encourages him to keep going, and Curtis helps Dmitri and the Bandits escape (after nearly falling to his death a few times). After seeing that Alexandra and the coyotes are gone, Curtis tells the Bandits that he found out Alexandra is planning to sacrifice Mac to control the Ivy, and she is headed to the Ancient’s Grove to do the deed.

Prue comes upon the Mystics and their leader, Iphigenia (Tantoo Cardinal). She guides Prue to the Great Tree that the Mystics communicate with. Iphigenia tells Prue that they have not heard anything, so Prue runs and touches the tree. She sees Alexandra and her soldiers marching towards the Ancient’s Grove to sacrifice Mac so she can control the Ivy and recover Alexei’s body and bring him back. The Mystics team up with the Bandits once they have made their way home, and they raise their own army to go against Alexandra.

Before reaching the Ancient’s Grove, the heroes prepare for battle against Alexandra’s forces. The Bandits charge first, while the coyotes fire their weapons. Archers on the heroes side fire arrows, but the coyotes deploy cannons and fireballs. Curtis, Niamh, Dmitri, and others sneak up on the coyotes to send them over the cliff to their deaths. In the battle, Septima is killed protecting Curtis, while Brendan is shot and briefly brought down. Prue goes after Alexandra, but Maksim tries to kill Prue himself. Curtis stabs Maksim with a sword and feels remorse for having to do so, but he tells Prue to save her brother.

Alexandra reaches the top of the Ancient’s Grove to perform the ritual. Iphigenia tries to talk some sense into her, but Alexandra is too far gone to listen to reason. After she spots Prue, she attempts to attack the girl before plunging her dagger into Mac, but Prue uses her blood to touch the Ivy and ask it to help her. The Ivy creates a vine tornado that keeps Mac away from Alexandra. When she tries to kill Prue, the girl uses the Ivy to impale Alexandra, and her body is absorbed by the Ivy. Prue calms the Ivy down to get Mac back, and she embraces her little brother.

The surviving heroes gather after running the coyotes out of their home. Prue apologizes to Curtis for how she treated him and hugs him. Before leaving, Prue and Curtis get help from the Bandits to stage a coup d’etat to remove Lars from his position and to free Owl Rex from prison so he can return home. They bid their new friends farewell and return home to Prue’s parents.

Although Prue brought Mac home, she still feels a sense of trauma and guilt over what happened with Alexandra. Mr. McKeel says it’s hard for some people to let go, but Prue says she is glad she didn’t let go of finding Mac. She then takes her little brother out on the town.

wiki_plot.text:
Portland adolescent Prue McKeel defies her parents' instructions and takes her baby brother Mac outside to play. While at a park with Prue's classmate Curtis Mehlberg, Mac is abducted by a murder of crows, which Prue and Curtis pursue into the Impassable Wilderness on the edge of town. Inside the forest, the two are pursued by uniformed anthropomorphic coyotes, led by Maksim. Curtis distracts them to allow Prue to escape. He is then brought before their leader, the dowager governess Alexandra, who explains that she is at war with bandits over control of the Impassable Wilderness—known to its inhabitants as "Wildwood"—and captures and imprisons some of them, including their leader Brendan, in the aftermath of a skirmish. A rat named Septima cautions Curtis not to trust Alexandra.

Prue is picked up by Wildwood's postmaster general, Richard, who takes her to the governor's mansion in South Wood. Along the way, they encounter the General, a colossal golden eagle. At the mansion, the governor, Lars, reveals that the woods are closed off to outsiders and imprisons Prue to hide her arrival. After receiving a message from Owl Rex, prince of the Avian Principality, Prue manages to escape and meet with him. Owl Rex relays Alexandra's tragic past: her beloved son, Alexei, had died during a horseback outing with his parents, but his body was never found, causing her husband, the former governor, to die of grief. Using black magic, Alexandra placed Alexei's soul into a new mechanical body, only for him to commit suicide upon discovering the truth behind his existence, leading to Alexandra's arrest for witchcraft and eventual exile.

Curtis finds Mac in the coyote warren, but is subsequently imprisoned with the bandits. Owl Rex is arrested by Lars' forces, but has the General fly Prue to the enigmatic mystic Iphigenia in North Wood. They are shot down en route by the coyotes, resulting in the General's death and Prue's capture. When Alexandra's attempts to divert Prue's suspicions fail, she convinces Prue that Mac has died. A devastated Prue returns home, where her parents reveal that, after struggling with infertility, they enlisted Alexandra to help them conceive their first child through magic. In exchange, they promised Alexandra their second-born child. They attempted to avoid this by only having one child, but failed when they unexpectedly had Mac. This magic granted Prue the ability to cross into Wildwood. Realizing that Mac is still alive, Prue sneaks back into the woods to find Iphigenia.

Alexandra prepares to march on the bandits' ancestral land, where she intends to sacrifice Mac on an altar in order to wake and take control of Wildwood's ivy to locate Alexei's body so she can revive him; however, the woods' inhabitants know she will lose control of its power, destroying their world. Septima frees Curtis, who helps Brendan and the other bandits escape with him. After meeting Prue, Iphigenia and the people of North Wood prepare for war. Knowing that they all share the mutual goal of stopping Alexandra, Prue negotiates an alliance between the two armies.

On the battlefield, Alexandra's army is pincered and crushed by the combined forces, though Brendan is wounded and Septima dies protecting Curtis. Maksim attacks Prue but is killed by Curtis, allowing Prue to reach the altar. Iphigenia and Prue attempt to reason with Alexandra, but she refuses to listen. Prue's hand is cut in the struggle. Absorbing her magic-infused blood, the ivy is made to obey her commands, causing a botanical tornado that saves Mac. Enraged, Alexandra attempts to sacrifice Prue instead. As Prue begs Alexandra to stop, the ivy fatally impales Alexandra and consumes her body, before Prue finally manages to take control and calm the ivy.

In the aftermath, Alexandra's coyotes abandon their uniforms and flee. Prue and the bandits stage a coup against Lars, taking control of South Wood and freeing Owl Rex. Prue, Curtis, and Mac return home, where Prue makes peace with her parents and, though haunted by the losses of her journey, begins to come to terms with the complexities of adulthood. Prue later plays with Mac, who is now allowed to go outside.

spoiler_text.text:
The film opens as a man is being hanged by the neck. The townschildren begin to laugh and point at his visible erection. The rest of the townsfolk start to display bizarre reactions, including a couple making out beneath the man’s corpse. Two children, Catherine Earnshaw (Charlotte Mellington) and her friend/paid servant, Nelly Dean (Vy Nguyen), are among the onlookers, and they also have strong reactions to the scene.

Cathy lives with her drunkard father, Mr. Earnshaw (Martin Clunes) in their dilapidated estate of Wuthering Heights in the Yorkshire Moors. Earnshaw is abusive toward Cathy but brings in a boy (Owen Cooper) off the streets, claiming his own father didn’t want him. Cathy names him “Heathcliff” in honor of her deceased brother. Though Heathcliff doesn’t speak at first, Cathy bonds with him and educates him, and they become devoted to one another.

One afternoon, Cathy and Heathcliff are stuck out on the streets in the rain. When they get home, Earnshaw is drunk and furious that they have come late for his birthday. He starts to blame Cathy, but Heathcliff takes the blame for it. Heathcliff gets Nelly to take Catherine out of the room while Earnshaw brutally beats Heathcliff, and Cathy can only hear in despair. Heathcliff is left with permanent scars on his back.

When they become adults, Cathy (now played by Margot Robbie) still bonds with Heathcliff (now played by Jacob Elordi). Wuthering Heights has fallen deeper into hard times due to Earnshaw’s excessive drinking and gambling habits. Cathy and Heathcliff go for a walk. She says she wants to court their new neighbor, Edgar Linton (Shazad Latif), so that their marriage may prove beneficial for both Cathy and Heathcliff. He is tired of hearing about Edgar and hoists Cathy up on a tree to shut her up. When he returns home, Heathcliff sits on a bunch of eggs that Cathy left in his bed as payback.

Cathy goes over to the Linton estate to spy on Edgar and his ward, an erratic young woman named Isabella (Alison Oliver). In the middle of Isabella’s chattering regarding “Romeo and Juliet”, she spots Cathy’s head peeking up and it frightens her, and causes Cathy to slip and injure herself. Edgar takes Cathy in to heal. He becomes smitten with her and eventually proposes marriage to her, which she accepts. Cathy returns home with a new dress, and Heathcliff is visibly jealous.

Cathy later spots two servants, Joseph and Zillah (Ewan Mitchell and Amy Morgan) engaging in an intense BDSM sexual encounter, while she watches from afar. Heathcliff shows up to cover Cathy’s mouth so she doesn’t make a sound, but she can still see and hear what is happening. Heathcliff later finds Cathy pleasuring herself in the barn. They go outside and nearly share a kiss, but Cathy doesn’t think their relationship would work.

Cathy talks to Nelly about how she feels some guilt in choosing Edgar over Heathcliff, but he walks by and overhears out of context the moment where she says that marrying him would degrade her status. Cathy catches Heathcliff trying to leave and tries to explain herself, but he is heartbroken and leaves on horseback.

A year passes. Cathy marries Edgar, and they are shown to have a passionless marriage at his estate of Thrushcross Grance, and they bring Nelly along as well. She spends time with Isabella, who helps her acquire fancy dresses and even makes a doll of Cathy with Cathy’s own hair, but Cathy continues to quietly yearn for Heathcliff.

After five years, Heathcliff returns, now having mysteriously acquired a fortune and looking well-groomed, clean-shaven, and sporting a gold tooth. Cathy is also now pregnant with Edgar’s child. Although Cathy is elated to see Heathcliff again, he remains resentful toward her over her marrying Edgar.

Heathcliff buys Wuthering Heights from Mr. Earnshaw, who eventually dies. Cathy and Heathcliff attend his funeral, though she holds no grief for her father. Despite their tumultuous reunion, Cathy and Heathcliff give in to their feelings for one another and begin a private sexual affair. Heathcliff even offers to kill Edgar for Cathy, which she briefly considers but ultimately chooses against. Isabella develops an obsession with Heathcliff as well and considers Cathy to not be good enough for him.

Nelly finds out about the affair. Cathy gets hostile and attempts to have Nelly fired and banished from Edgar’s estate. Nelly instead tells Edgar about the affair, and he attempts to sway Cathy from seeing Heathcliff.

Cathy tells Heathcliff about her pregnancy. Naturally, he reacts poorly. He goes to Isabella and proposes marriage to her, despite making it clear he is going to treat her badly, but she doesn’t care because the abuse arouses her. They enter a BDSM relationship, with Heathcliff treating Isabella like a dog and putting a leash on her so she can crawl on all fours. While she enjoys it, Nelly visits them and is mortified by the scene.

Cathy becomes depressed over losing Heathcliff again. She starves herself and eventually admits to Nelly that she lost the baby a long time ago. Heathcliff tries to send Cathy love letters through Isabella, but Nelly throws them all into the fireplace. Cathy starts to develop septicemia as a result of the miscarriage. She tells Nelly she forgives her for not clarifying her words to Heathcliff, but Edgar finds out about Cathy’s condition and fires Nelly for neglecting to tell him.

Nelly returns to Heathcliff and Isabella’s home. After telling Heathcliff about Cathy’s condition, Nelly takes Isabella away, and Heathcliff rides his horse to see Cathy. By the time he has arrived, Cathy has already bled out and died. Edgar tries to stop Heathcliff from seeing Cathy as she is now, but Heathcliff pushes through and tearfully holds Cathy’s body, professing his love and begging her to come back to him, before simply laying by her side.

The last scene is a flashback to young Cathy and Heathcliff. While it seems like Cathy is sleeping, Heathcliff whispers to her how he will always love her and remain close to her always. Cathy smiles.

wiki_plot.text:
In 19th-century England Mr.Earnshaw returns to his estate of Wuthering Heights on the Yorkshire Moors with a young boy he rescued off the streets, whom he introduces to his daughter, Cathy, and her companion, Nelly Dean. Cathy becomes protective of the boy and names him "Heathcliff". As time goes on, the pair become inseparable.

By the time Cathy and Heathcliff have reached adulthood, Wuthering Heights has fallen into disrepair due to Mr.Earnshaw's worsening alcoholism and gambling habits. Cathy plans to court her new neighbor, wealthy textile merchant Edgar Linton, to escape Wuthering Heights' bleak environment and help bring the lowly servant Heathcliff into high society, though Heathcliff is jealous and disapproves. The situation becomes more complicated when Cathy and Heathcliff begin to realise that they have fallen in love with each other, although Cathy initially shuns the idea of becoming romantically involved with Heathcliff and continues to pursue Edgar.

One day Cathy sprains her ankle while spying on Edgar and his ward, Isabella, and is taken in at their home for six weeks to heal. Edgar is smitten by Cathy and proposes marriage, which she accepts. While expressing to Nelly her guilt over choosing Edgar over Heathcliff, Cathy implies Nelly would not understand because she "never loved anyone" and no one loves her. Provoked, Nelly bitterly manipulates Cathy into saying that marrying Heathcliff would degrade her, so that it would be secretly overheard by him outside. Heathcliff leaves before he hears Cathy confess her love for him and her belief in their connection, wrongly believing that Cathy does not care for him, and then leaves Wuthering Heights, riding away secretly. By the next day, Cathy has changed her mind about marrying Edgar, but it is too late as Heathcliff has already left. Cathy is devastated by his departure and initially refuses to accept that he could have left her.

A year later Cathy has given up hope that Heathcliff will come back and decides to go through with the marriage to Edgar after all. After the wedding, she lives a lavish lifestyle with her husband at their home, Thrushcross Grange, but secretly longs to be reunited with Heathcliff again. In time, Cathy becomes pregnant with Edgar's child. Soon after Cathy learns of her pregnancy, Heathcliff finally returns, five years after his departure, and is now well-groomed and wealthy. Rather than being happy to see Cathy, he is bitter and angry over her decision to marry Edgar and considers marrying Isabella to make Cathy jealous. He purchases Wuthering Heights from Mr.Earnshaw, who dies soon after. Following this, Heathcliff consoles Cathy and they reconnect, beginning an intense romantic and sexual affair.

After Cathy realizes Nelly knew Heathcliff was listening when Cathy said marrying him would degrade her, she tries to banish Nelly from the Grange. Nelly then reveals the affair to Edgar, who forbids Cathy from seeing Heathcliff. Cathy later reveals her pregnancy to Heathcliff, who claims to not mind before having sex with her. He offers to kill Edgar, which Cathy rejects, and she dismisses him. Furious, Heathcliff enters into a loveless, BDSM relationship with Isabella, who understands Heathcliff's motivations and agrees to elope with him. Following the marriage, Heathcliff degrades Isabella and treats her like a dog, which Nelly witnesses when she visits them at Wuthering Heights.

Depressed over Heathcliff marrying Isabella, Cathy locks herself in her room and starves herself. Heathcliff tries to stay connected to Cathy by secretly sending her love letters while she is isolated and growing weaker, but Nelly intercepts them, letting Cathy think Heathcliff has abandoned her. Her pregnancy eventually results in a miscarriage which becomes septicemic. When Nelly realizes how serious Cathy's situation is, she returns to Wuthering Heights to rescue Isabella and to reveal to Heathcliff that Cathy is dying. Heathcliff frantically rides to the Grange on horseback, only to find when he arrives that Cathy has already died. Heathcliff then holds Cathy's dead body and begs her to drive him insane and not give him peace as long as he should live.

spoiler_text.text:
The film starts in 2023 as Billy Evans, partner to Elizabeth Holmes, expresses to the documentary crew how the two of them want to tell an “accurate” version of her story. The opening text explains that there are 34 days leading up to Elizabeth’s eleven-year sentence for defrauding investors with her company Theranos. A crew led by Nathan Fielder have been given the chance over other reporters and journalists because the couple trusts he will help tell the story Elizabeth wants.

Nathan does his research on Elizabeth’s history, from her start at Stanford, to her infamous rise and fall alongside her former president/lover Sunny Balwani. Elizabeth and Billy have also expressed negative feelings towards the Hulu miniseries “The Dropout”, where she is portrayed by Amanda Seyfried. They are also fixated on a quote in the New York Times regarding Amanda’s portrayal, as well as a scrapped film that would have starred Jennifer Lawrence: “They’re not playing me. They’re playing a character I created.” Elizabeth claims she never said SHE created the character.

Nathan joins Elizabeth and Billy at their beach house in San Diego, which they share with their kids. Elizabeth claims she is being as open and honest as possible, though Nathan has his doubts, especially since she’s claimed to have never lied a day in her life. Nathan asks Billy about how he met her, which was around the time she was found guilty of fraud. Billy insists that he loves her despite all that he heard about her.

Elizabeth’s parents Christian and Noel visit the house and meet Nathan. He speaks to Christian privately and learns that things started to go downhill for Elizabeth when she was raped as a student. Billy interrupts the meeting and seems to get defensive about Elizabeth’s parents not being with the family.

Nathan shows Elizabeth and Billy most of “The Dropout”. When it gets to scenes depicting Elizabeth and Sunny, she gets emotional and wants to stop watching. When she talks privately with Nathan, Elizabeth expresses sadness about her upcoming sentence and being separated from Billy and their kids.

Elizabeth shows Nathan a deconstructed version of her “scam device” that she claimed could run hundreds of tests at once with a single drop of blood. She insists that it works as she said it does, but somewhere along the development process, something went wrong. She and Billy are also in the process of trying to get “Theranos 2.0” going.

In the days leading up to her incarceration, Elizabeth gets 3D scans of her body done, though she is not comfortable at the thought of her image being used. She bids Nathan farewell before heading to prison in Bryan, Texas. Billy and the kids move closer to be near her.

Two years later, Nathan shows the footage up to that point to none other than Amanda Seyfried herself. She becomes stunned at what she has seen, especially Elizabeth’s reaction to her performance. For all the remaining scenes prior to filming or wherever the crew could not film, Amanda reprises her role as Elizabeth in re-enactments, while Billy is portrayed by Christopher Abbott. A “flashback” is shown when Elizabeth and Billy first met with Nathan, co-director Lance Oppenheim, and two executives from A24. After Elizabeth had left the room, Billy asked about possibly being paid for their part in the film, but Nathan and the others argue that it would be unethical since it would look biased on their part. Regardless, they negotiate a deal.

Nathan and Amanda review a clip where he spoke to Elizabeth about how she implicitly knew nothing about Billy making any money deals behind her back. Furthermore, Nathan and Amanda find out that Billy is using Elizabeth’s social media account and saying things that she would not say (mainly swearing and insulting people).

Billy meets with Nathan and Amanda in his house. He reveals he has power of attorney over Elizabeth, something that shocks the two. When Amanda accuses Billy of exploiting Elizabeth, he gets defensive and mentions her getting backlash for criticizing Charlie Kirk after his assassination, especially since Billy was a fan of his (make of that what you will). Amanda later tells Nathan that Billy is “batshit crazy” and that, despite her distrust of Elizabeth, she feels no woman should be with a guy like that. Billy also later shows Nathan that he has billboards with Elizabeth’s image in Times Square, with the famous image of her holding a blood sample that she dislikes, as well as AI videos of her.

Nathan has trouble contacting Elizabeth over the phone due to limited minutes. The one time Amanda gets to speak directly to Elizabeth, she is visibly unnerved. Eventually, they arrange for him to speak to her in prison before Billy and the kids arrive. With Amanda playing Elizabeth one last time, we see “Elizabeth” expressing her disapproval of Amanda’s portrayal in “The Dropout” because she thinks that’s the only image of herself that people will believe. On the subject of Billy making the money deal, she says that she would gain nothing anyway because she owes hundreds of millions in restitution, so all of it would be taken from her anyway. Elizabeth becomes emotional once again, proclaiming that her and Billy’s love for one another is real. Nathan leaves after Billy and the kids arrive.

Nathan and Amanda sit one last time to discuss Nathan’s final thoughts. Even though they know Elizabeth can hardly be trusted, Amanda believes Nathan grew to care for Elizabeth in some way.

The final shot is the real Elizabeth and Billy with their kids from outside the prison as they visit her.

The ending text states that Billy eventually dropped his deal to gain money from the film. Nathan eventually got in touch with the New York Times reporter, who, despite being unable to provide evidence, stands by her quote of Elizabeth saying that actresses portraying her are playing a character SHE created.

wiki_plot.text:
In April 2023, 34 days before Elizabeth Holmes begins her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors through her company Theranos, she and her partner Billy Evans invite filmmakers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim to document their lives at a rented beach house in Del Mar, California. Despite having extensive access to their personal lives, Fielder suspects them of withholding information. When Fielder questions Holmes about how she promoted Theranos's defective blood-testing device, she denies intentionally misleading anyone about its capabilities, claiming her words were semantically misinterpreted. Holmes and Evans call prospective investors about starting a new blood-testing company.

Fielder shows the couple the Abbott and Costello routine "Who's on First?" to demonstrate his frustrations in communicating with Holmes. Holmes says she finds it humorous, but admits to not understanding the joke when pressed by Fielder, which Evans claims exemplifies how she "thinks differently". Later, Fielder shows them The Dropout, a miniseries starring actress Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, but a distressed Holmes asks to stop watching. Shortly before her imprisonment, Holmes has her body 3D-scanned and expresses concern about her likeness being misused. Holmes reports to Federal Prison Camp, Bryan to begin her sentence. Evans and their two children subsequently relocate to Texas to be closer to her.

Filming resumes two years later, as Fielder follows Evans' development of his new company, Haemanthus. Evans exhibits behavior that concerns Fielder: he refuses to help Fielder speak with Holmes in prison, licenses Holmes's image for billboards and a deepfaked AI model, and abruptly ends Fielder's interview with a Haemanthus engineer who suggests Holmes lied about the Theranos device's capabilities.

Fielder meets with Seyfried and has her reprise her role as Holmes in dramatized reenactments of encounters during the making of the documentary which were not filmed. They reenact a meeting that occurred early in the project, in which Evans (portrayed by actor Christopher Abbott) requested a cut of the documentary's profit while Holmes was in another room. The filmmakers reluctantly negotiated a profit-sharing agreement with Evans, but Holmes later mentioned that she would receive no money from the documentary, raising suspicions regarding whether she knew of this deal.

Fielder and Seyfried find further examples of Evans controlling Holmes's public image, including impersonating her on X while saying things that Fielder and Seyfried believe she would never say. They confront Evans at his home, where Evans states that he holds power of attorney over Holmes, that most of his social media posts draw from emails she sends him from prison, and that she knows "some" details of his agreement with the filmmakers concerning the film's profits. He criticizes Seyfried for starring in The Dropout and for calling Charlie Kirk "hateful" following Kirk's assassination. He threatens to exact revenge on anyone who harmed Holmes, expresses concerns that he is being followed, and says that he always carries a gun.

Frustrated with Evans's interference, Fielder visits Holmes in prison and later reenacts the meeting with Seyfried. Fielder recounts that Holmes says she is being bullied in prison due to Seyfried's portrayal of her in The Dropout. Seyfried is taken aback by this, but she defends her portrayal and the dramatic license taken by the show. Holmes claims to approve of Evans's activities since her imprisonment, but remains vague about her knowledge of his financial decisions, which she admits she prefers to leave to his discretion because she owes hundreds of millions of dollars in restitution. Evans arrives with their children for their weekly visit, and he and Holmes tearfully embrace, which Fielder interprets as genuine affection. When Fielder starts to change the wording in his reenactment script, Seyfried suggests that Fielder has allowed his sympathy for Holmes to compromise his objectivity.

On-screen text reveals that Evans relinquished his profit-sharing agreement before the film's release. It also states that New York Times reporter Amy Chozick stands by (but does not provide evidence for) the remark she alleges Holmes made regarding The Dropout, which Holmes and Evans disputed: "They're not playing me. They're playing a character I created."

wiki_plot.text:
Latif, an ex-military hitman who works for security specialist Mike Mahmoudi, finishes a job in St. Louis before receiving a phone call from his daughter Fatiha telling him that Khadijah, his wife and her mother, died suddenly. Latif returns to his home in Houston for the funeral, reuniting with his family, including Fatiha, his son Qadir, and his infant daughter Aziza. A devout Muslim, Latif experiences a crisis of faith as he mourns his wife and struggles to care for his children.

Khadijah's supply of breast milk begins to run low, and Latif learns that Aziza cannot digest formula. He goes to the local mosque with his family to see if they can find a breast milk donation, where he runs into Mike and his nephew, Hatty, who runs a Muslim-themed porn studio. Mike tells Latif that a Charismatic Christian leader named Hwan Yoon plans to murder Hatty, believing that his porn studio is a front for human trafficking, and orders Latif to kill Hwan before that happens. Aziza is fed by Fugazi, a former employee of Hatty's who happens to be lactating.

Latif solicits his brother Talib, a physician assistant who disapproves of Latif's criminal lifestyle, for a prescription he can bring to the milk bank, but the bank is closed by the time he returns. Out of desperation, he drives to Hatty's mansion and asks him to bring him to Fugazi so she can feed Aziza again. Hatty initially refuses unless Latif kills Hwan, then threatens Latif's children; Latif overpowers him and handcuffs him in the backseat, where he guides him to the strip club where Fugazi works.

While Fugazi feeds Aziza, Hwan enters their private room, revealing that the strip club is now a church and that Fugazi became one of his followers after leaving Hatty. He thanks Latif, believing he brought Hatty for him to kill; Latif fights Hwan and his men, taking back Aziza from Fugazi and reuniting with an escaped Hatty. Latif, his children, and Hatty sit down at a restaurant to break the fast, but Hwan catches up to them and captures Hatty.

After being driven home by Latif's imam, Abdul Malik, Latif announces that they will go to Mexico. Learning that Mike and his men have come to their apartment complex, he has his children hide in the Mormon missionaries' apartment nearby as he returns to his apartment to grab more breast milk from the refrigerator. He is ambushed by Mike, who is furious that he let Hatty be captured; he kills Mike's henchmen, then Mike himself. Latif collects his children and drives to the mosque, where he finds that Abdul Malik was murdered by Hwan's men.

Latif leaves his children at Talib's house and says goodbye to them before driving to Hatty's mansion, which has since been taken over by Hwan. Hatty is bound to a chair, having been tortured in order to be "taught a lesson." Latif offers to help, but cuts Hatty free with his sword and engages in a fight with Hwan's men. Hwan shoots Latif several times with an assault rifle, apparently killing him. As he lies bleeding on the ground, he hears his daughter praying for him to return home, and miraculously returns to life. Awestruck, Hwan allows both Latif and Hatty to leave, and Latif reunites with his children.
